title: Four governance config fields promise risk-conditional HITL and have zero code consumers — wire them or delete them
description:
Declared in .context-index/governance/ and cited by ADR-0010, read by nothing:

- require_hitl_approval — verified 0 references under lib/
- approver_role — verified 0 references under lib/; described as "informational" everywhere it appears
- transitions: {} — empty, and validate Check 9 dispatches an LLM subagent per spec to evaluate it
- additional_gates: [] — empty

This is config that reads as a safety guarantee and delivers none. Either wire them (the research proposes generalizing reportHumanApprovalRequired + --require-human-final-pass into a policy-driven hitl consult, driven by risk-policies.yaml, which finally gives require_hitl_approval its consumer) or delete all four so the config stops implying a control that does not exist.

Context: the study counted 47 interactive human stop-points across the skills, of which exactly ONE is code-enforced (build --require-human-final-pass, opt-in, off by default). Everything else is prose an agent can talk itself past.

From .context-index/research/harness-simplification-study.md Part 3, "Current state of gating".

Source: 2026-08-14 research-vs-board audit. Claim re-verified against the codebase at that date, not taken from the research artifact alone.
close_reason: Merged into adev-plugin-8ekd.1 — 'Governance config ships empty and nothing populates or migrates it'. This issue covered four governance config fields (require_hitl_approval, approver_role, transitions, additional_gates), which is one view of that single root cause: adev's governance config ships empty, nothing populates it, and nothing migrates it. Scope preserved verbatim in the absorbing issue; no work dropped. Closing to reduce four overlapping issues to one.

title: Token Cost & Measurement
description:
Token cost of running the adev lifecycle, and the instrumentation needed to measure it.

Created 2026-08-17 after a token retro on session eef96958 found six issues about token cost with no common parent, scattered across gkfv, 882a and unparented ids. Six independent issues on one theme is the signature of a missing epic.

=== WHY THIS EPIC EXISTS ===

Measured on one real lifecycle (two amendments authored, two full-tier review rounds, plan, route, 10 implemented tasks, validate), main loop only:

  cache_read       335,935,349   98.1%
  cache_creation     5,353,678    1.6%
  output               959,542    0.3%
  input                  2,283    0.0%
  TOTAL            342,250,852

The stored module heuristic says cache reads are ~71% of session cost. This session measured 98.1%. The driver is not any single expensive action — it is turn count multiplied by context size. Mean cache_read per main-loop message grew 8.7x over the session (73,434 -> 641,098), so an identical tool call late in a session costs roughly 9x what it cost early. Cost is therefore superlinear in the number of round trips, which is why nothing looks expensive and the total is enormous anyway.

SCOPE CAVEAT that constrains every issue here: all 1,228 measured messages had isSidechain: false. Subagent contexts were NOT in the transcript, and the harness's reported subagent_tokens (~1.82M across 6 dispatches) does not state whether it includes cache reads. The implement subagent alone ran 124 tool calls over 106 minutes, so its true processed-token count is far above its reported figure. Consequence: the orchestrator loop is measured exactly, subagents are NOT, and no claim of the form "delegation is cheap" or "subagents dominate" is currently supported by evidence. Establishing subagent-side measurement is in scope for this epic.

=== SEQUENCING — this is the point of grouping them ===

adev-plugin-882a.1 MUST LAND FIRST. encodeCwd drops dot-directories, so adev's own token instrumentation is silently inert in every .claude/worktrees worktree — which is the workflow adev actively steers users toward. That is why the retro above had to be produced by hand-parsing the raw transcript instead of running `adev cost summary`, which correctly reported "no usage data yet".

Every other issue in this epic is an OPTIMIZATION HYPOTHESIS. None can be verified before or after a change while the meter is broken. Optimizing first means arguing from proxies, and the stored heuristic is explicit that byte-estimate proxies overstate savings by 2-2.5x.

There is precedent for a hypothesis inverting under measurement: adev-plugin-test-suite-per-behavior-granularity-usiy began as "adopt per-behavior test granularity" and measurement showed it would produce MORE suites than the 305 currently declared, because specs average 10.9 behaviors against 5.2 test-bearing tasks per plan. The original framing survives in that issue only as a footnote. Treat the remaining hypotheses here as provisional until measured the same way.

=== MEMBERS, in complexity order ===

  882a.1  encodeCwd dot-encoding                bug      trivial   PREREQUISITE, blocks the rest
  gyad    validate re-read caching              task     low-mod   one skill; watch the cross-subagent cache caveat
  ga1t    skill-description trigger collision    task     moderate  mechanical audit, judgment-heavy rule definition
  hl0m    evals depend on local session JSONL    bug      moderate  two problems in one: absolute path + ~31 never-CI-run tests
  gkfv.4  orchestrator loop norms                task     mod-high  cheap to write, no mechanism to enforce
  (new)   skill-load deduplication              task     high      split out of gkfv.4; likely needs harness support
  usiy    cut test suite 468 -> ~250            task     high      silent coverage loss is the undetectable failure mode
  xprl    implement TDD + 2-stage review cycle  task     highest   research spike into the most load-bearing skill

=== DEFINITION OF DONE FOR THE EPIC ===

Not "cost is lower" — that is unfalsifiable as stated. Rather:
1. adev can measure its own token cost, in a worktree, from its own instrumentation (882a.1, and subagent-side coverage per the caveat above).
2. Each remaining hypothesis has been measured and either implemented or explicitly withdrawn with its measurement recorded, as usiy's original framing was.
3. The measurement method is reproducible by someone other than the author on a clean checkout — which is what hl0m is about.

title: Skill-load deduplication: the same SKILL.md is loaded in full more than once per session
description:
Split out of adev-plugin-gkfv.4 on 2026-08-17 because its feasibility is unknown and it should not gate that issue cheap norms.

MEASURED, session eef96958, one lifecycle:
  specify       62KB  x3  = ~46,638 tok
  build         65KB  x1  = ~16,212 tok
  work          22KB  x2  = ~10,847 tok
  review-specs  37KB  x1  = ~9,161 tok
  TOTAL         7 loads    = ~82,859 tok

`specify` was loaded THREE times in one session — roughly 31K tokens of pure duplication. Two of those came via /adev:work routing into specify; the third was a direct invocation. `work` was loaded twice for the same reason.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF COST: a re-loaded SKILL.md does not just cost its own bytes once. It enters the context and is then re-read as part of the accumulated prefix on EVERY subsequent turn for the rest of the session. In a session where mean cache_read per message reached 641,098 tokens, ~31K of duplicated skill text is re-read hundreds of times. The duplication is multiplied by remaining turn count, not paid once.

WHY IT IS HARD, and why it is separated from the norms:
A skill cannot detect "my SKILL.md is already in this context" from inside itself. There is no introspection surface for what is already in the prompt. Plausible approaches, none obviously correct:
  1. Harness-level dedup — the Skill tool declines to re-inject a body already present this session. Cleanest, entirely outside adev repo control.
  2. Session-scoped marker — a skill records that it loaded, and a re-invocation reads a shorter "already loaded, here are the args" path. Requires every skill to carry a two-path structure and a place to record the marker; risks the second path silently diverging from the first, which is worse than the duplication.
  3. Composition instead of re-invocation — /adev:work hands off to a target skill WITHOUT a second full load of its own body, i.e. the router stops re-entering itself. Narrowest and most tractable: it addresses the `work` x2 case and possibly the specify x2-via-routing case, without needing to solve general dedup.
Approach 3 is worth scoping first; it is the only one fully inside this repo control and it covers most of the measured waste.

DO NOT confuse with adev-plugin-ga1t. That issue is about the ~100 tokens of always-loaded DESCRIPTION metadata per skill and trigger-phrase collisions among 31 descriptions. This issue is about the full SKILL.md BODY being injected more than once. Both are real, they compound, and they have different fixes.

CAVEAT before optimizing: measure first. Per the epic sequencing, adev-plugin-882a.1 must land so this can be verified rather than estimated — and the stored module heuristic warns byte-estimate proxies overstate savings by 2-2.5x. The token figures above come from real message.usage records, but any post-fix claim must be measured the same way.

title: Standalone Invocation
BeadsAdapter.createEpic delegates to the read-only FileAdapter, so epics can never exist on the beads backend
description: Found 2026-08-13 immediately after fixing issue-626 (the --db path bug) and retrying 'adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed' on this repo. SECOND, INDEPENDENT blocker -- structural, not a config or path problem. beads-adapter.mjs:241 has createEpic() delegate unconditionally to this._fileAdapter.createEpic(), and file-adapter.mjs:133-135 is 'async createEpic(_epicData) { throw deprecatedWrite(); }' -- an unconditional throw, because the file (markdown) backend is read-only by design. So epic creation on the beads backend is impossible by construction. The adapter's own header comment states the intent: 'Epic operations are delegated to a FileAdapter instance since beads_rust has no epic concept (hybrid approach per SA-5)' -- but the adapter chosen to hold them cannot be written to, so the hybrid has no writable home for epics. OBSERVED RESULT of the retry: all 308 issues migrated successfully and .beads-map.json holds 308 entries (verified directly: 'br --db .beads/beads.db list --json' returns 308), then the run aborted at index 308 -- the FIRST epic, epic-1 -- with 'The file (markdown) backend is read-only.' So 0 of 106 epics and 0 of 41 dependency edges migrated. Epic MEMBERSHIP does survive: 242 of the 308 map entries carry epicId metadata, consistent with backend-adapters.spec.md:49 which says epicId/planRef filters read from .beads-map.json because beads does not track them natively. What is missing is the epic ENTITIES (title, status, milestone) and every dependency edge. SECOND DEFECT observed in the same run: the migrate verb reported created:{issues:0,epics:0} even though 308 issues were demonstrably created -- the counter is not incremented before the abort, so a partially-successful run reports as a total no-op and understates what actually landed. That is dangerous on its own: a re-run looks safe when it is not. (It is in fact idempotent via .beads-map.json, but the report gives no way to know that.) NOTE ON API GENERATION: createEpic emits 'createEpic is deprecated; use create() instead. See task-management charter rev 3' under ADEV_DEPRECATION_WARN=1, so the migrate verb drives a deprecated path. Any fix should decide how epics are represented under beads at all -- most plausibly as tiered issues via the unified create() rather than as a separate entity class -- which is a design decision, not a patch. CURRENT STATE, nothing is live: manifest still reads tasks.backend: json, the json board remains authoritative and complete at 308 issues / 106 epics, and the populated .beads store plus .beads-map.json are present but unwired. Pre-migration snapshot committed at c3d4a875 on branch chore/board-migrate-to-beads.; Closed: ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN. Commit 9dc95701 identified the same root cause ("Epics were delegated to FileAdapter, which is read-only-deprecated, so createEpic threw BACKEND_READ_ONLY_DEPRECATED"), and dcb4f591 ("make beads the single source of truth — delete the sidecar") went further than this issue proposed: it removed .beads-map.json entirely, storing adev ids in br external_ref, metadata in br agent_context, and epics as br issues with issue_type: epic. That is the same charter-derived conclusion this issue reached (an epic is a root-level WorkItem, not a separate entity) but implemented without a second store that can disagree. A local fix was written independently (commit 34a5c685, 8 TDD tests) and is DISCARDED as redundant; reflog only. Verified fixed: migration against main creates 106 epic-* external_refs with 0 errors. Also note the created-counter misreporting flagged here is still live on main -- a run that demonstrably created 106 epics reported created:{epics:0}, skipped:106. Rolled into issue-628.

title: Provider install copies 358MB of the repo into the plugin cache — dominates suite wall-clock and ships .beads and .claude
description:
Found 2026-08-18 while chasing the two slowest test files in a per-test-file
coverage matrix. The slow tests were a symptom; this is the cause.

=== ROOT CAUSE ===

providers/claude-code/adapter.mjs:107

  cpSync(PLUGIN_ROOT, cacheDir, {
    recursive: true,
    filter: (src) => {
      const name = src.split('/').pop();
      return name !== '.git' && name !== 'node_modules' && name !== '.DS_Store';
    },
  });

A three-item DENYLIST. Everything else in the repo root is copied.

MEASURED, walking PLUGIN_ROOT with that exact filter:

  358.2 MB across 25,191 files

  142.2 MB  .claude/          local worktrees and session state
  105.5 MB  tests/            includes vendored eval projects
   84.4 MB  .beads/           the issue-tracker database
   16.4 MB  .context-index/   project context, sessions, lifecycle logs
    3.3 MB  viz/
    2.3 MB  lib/              <-- actual payload
    1.9 MB  providers/        <-- actual payload
    1.0 MB  skills/           <-- actual payload

The shipped plugin is roughly 5 MB. The copy is ~70x that.

=== BLAST RADIUS: dev/dogfood installs only ===

package.json declares a 'files' allowlist (cli, lib, providers, hooks, skills,
templates, extensions, .claude-plugin, .githooks), so the PUBLISHED npm package
does not contain .beads, .claude, tests or .context-index. Users installing via
npx are NOT affected.

PLUGIN_ROOT is resolved at runtime as join(__dirname, '../..'), so the 358 MB copy
happens whenever install() runs from a git checkout — local install, npm link,
--plugin-dir, and the test suite. Not a published-artifact data leak, but it does
copy a developer's local .claude and .beads into ~/.claude/plugins/cache/.

=== WHY IT SHOWS UP AS A TEST PROBLEM ===

Seven test files call a real install():
  tests/provider/claude-code-adapter.test.mjs      165s measured  (3 installs)
  tests/cli-install-scope.test.mjs                  60s measured
  tests/cli.test.mjs                              >200s — TIMED OUT
  tests/provider/cursor-adapter.test.mjs           >200s — TIMED OUT
  tests/provider/codex-adapter.test.mjs
  tests/copilot-adapter.test.mjs
  tests/copilot-adapter-uninstall-defense.test.mjs

Those four are the two slowest files in the suite AND the only two files a
coverage harvest could not measure at all (200s timeout). One installer
inefficiency explains all four.

=== PROPOSED FIX — NOT APPLIED, needs approval ===

Replace the denylist with an allowlist mirroring package.json 'files':

  const SHIP = new Set(['cli','lib','providers','hooks','skills','templates',
                        'extensions','.claude-plugin','.githooks']);

MEASURED with that filter: 1,497 ms, 542 files, 5.7 MB — versus 358 MB / 25,191
files. ~63x smaller per install.

CLAUDE.md lists 'Modifying the CLI installation path structure' under Requires
Human Approval, which is why this is filed rather than fixed.

=== DESIGN POINT WORTH SETTLING ===

The adapter's filter and package.json 'files' encode the same knowledge — what
ships — in two places that cannot disagree safely. They already do disagree: the
adapter copies dirs npm excludes. Adding a shipped directory to 'files' today
does not tell the adapter about it, and the failure is silent in both directions
(missing file at runtime, or 100 MB of junk copied). Deriving the adapter's
allowlist FROM package.json 'files' at runtime removes the divergence class
entirely and is probably the better fix than a second hardcoded list.

Check the other adapters too — codex, cursor, copilot, opencode — for the same
copy pattern before fixing only the Claude one.

=== DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY WEAKENING THE TESTS ===

claude-code-adapter.test.mjs asserts real install semantics: cache layout, skills
present, settings.enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces registration, user vs
project scope separation, and uninstall cleanup. It was initially flagged as
'zero unique coverage' by the coverage matrix, which was WRONG — the harvest
filtered coverage to lib|cli|hooks|scripts and excluded providers/ entirely, so
the adapter's own code was invisible. The test is not redundant. Mocking the
install to make it fast would delete the only end-to-end coverage of the install
path.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-18. Allowlist derived from package.json files via lib/provider/ship-filter.mjs.

Payload 358.2 MB / 25,191 files -> 5.7 MB / 547 files.
claude-code-adapter test 165.2s -> 2.8s | cli-install-scope 60.0s -> 0.8s |
cursor-adapter >200s timeout -> 6.9s | FULL SUITE ~360s -> 27s.
Tests 6,864 pass / 0 fail; 9 new tests on the filter.

Applied to claude-code, cursor and opencode. copilot already copied only
skills/ and hooks/; codex does not copy.

EXPOSED A SECOND BUG, now fixed here: package.json files omitted
.cursor-plugin/, so the published npm package never contained it and a cursor
install from npm could not have worked. The old permissive denylist hid it
because checkout installs copied the directory anyway. release-please already
bumps that manifest in lockstep, so the omission was an oversight. Added.

STILL OPEN, filed separately: providers/opencode/adapter.mjs shells out to
execSync(cp -r) with an interpolated path instead of cpSync.

title: Pre-flight scan: /adev:work Step 1 should read open PRs, remote branches, and other-owner in_progress issues
description:
Root cause established 2026-08-12 after two agents independently fixed the same p0 vulnerability an hour apart (PR #214 and duplicate PR #215, both for issue-582), and after a whole concurrent epic (epic-102, issues 568-581, PRs #210-#214) stayed invisible to a study pursuing the same goal. The issue board resolves storage via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs) and IS shared across worktrees. Execution state does NOT: lib/execution-state.mjs reads <projectRoot>/.context-index/.execution-state.json, which is worktree-local. Measured live: /adev:work Step 1 reported status "idle" in this worktree while four epic-102 issues were in_progress and five PRs were open. Second, behavioural half: the board DID carry the signal (issue-582 was already in_progress) and nothing re-reads an issue at the moment work begins, so stale local knowledge won over the shared record.

HIGHEST VALUE, LOWEST COST — needs no new data model. Step 1 currently scans four purely local signals (execution state, plan tasks, lifecycle states, recent sessions). Add: gh pr list (degrade silently when gh is absent or unauthenticated), git branch -r, and issues whose status is in_progress under a different owner. This alone would have surfaced epic-102 and PR #210 before any work started — which is where the real waste was. The duplicate PR cost an hour; the duplicated ANALYSIS cost far more.

RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (epic-107): Closed by 470aa3e0 — adev coordination scan + /adev:work Step 1 signal 5.

title: Retire the 83 prose-matching test files once tier-2 diagnostics replace them
description: The missing BACKFILL half of issue-557. 557 builds the replacement (tier-2 diagnostic producers for SKILL.md/spec/docs structure) and forbids string-matching prose as a future test deliverable — but it does not touch the existing corpus. Nothing on the board currently migrates or retires it, so without this issue adev would ship the new mechanism while keeping ~10k lines of the old pattern in the suite indefinitely. Found 2026-08-13 when the gap was queried directly; the orchestrator had previously and incorrectly assumed 557 covered remediation. Scale (2026-08-10 audit): ~27% of this repo's test CASES are change-detectors; 103 files import NO production code and only readFileSync a .md and call .includes(). tests/skills/ is ~87% this pattern and tests/docs/ is 100% — together 83 files / ~10k lines / 824 cases with essentially zero production coverage. 340 assertions use the near-tautological includes(x) || includes(y) form. Precedent for the split: epic-104 separates producer fixes (issue-585 spec templates, issue-586 review/validate writer) from the backfill of ~400 existing artifacts (issue-587). epic-108 had the producer half (557) and was missing this one. HARD DEPENDENCY on issue-557: do not delete a prose test until the tier-2 producer that covers its invariant actually ships, or coverage is silently lost rather than migrated. Per-file the decision is three-way, not a blanket delete: (a) invariant now covered by a tier-2 diagnostic -> delete the test; (b) invariant real but NOT expressible as a diagnostic -> rewrite as a behavioral test that imports production code; (c) assertion was tautological (the includes(x) || includes(y) family) -> delete outright, it never tested anything. Requires a per-file audit; the count of files deleted vs rewritten vs dropped should be reported, since 'deleted 83 files' and 'migrated 83 invariants' are very different outcomes. Interacts with issue-555 (its hygiene test-debt pass detects prose-assertion density, so it can measure progress here) and issue-615 (cross-layer duplicate coverage — some prose tests may be duplicates rather than needing migration at all). || SCOPE ESTIMATE CONTESTED 2026-08-13 — RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING. issue-555's shipped test-debt scanner (Audit Pass 23) dogfooded this repo and found PROSE_ASSERTION = 25 files, not the 83-103 this issue was filed with. The numbers measure different things and both are internally valid: 227 test files reference a .md path and 115 reference SKILL.md, but only 25 also clear the 0.5 containment-assertion ratio. The audit counted files that TOUCH markdown (specifically: import no production code and only readFileSync a .md and call .includes()); the scanner counts files whose ASSERTIONS are predominantly markdown containment. A file asserting via assert.match regex rather than .includes() lands in the audit's set but may miss the scanner's ratio. Neither is wrong; they answer different questions. Consequence for this issue: do NOT plan against either figure. Run 'adev test-debt scan' for the low-false-positive set (25), then separately enumerate the audit's criterion (no production import + markdown-only assertions) for the outer bound, and reconcile per-file — the three-way audit below is what actually decides each file, and it will resolve files the ratio heuristic misses. title: adev gate doctor verifies the raw gates.yaml, not the merged gate set its consumers execute
description:
**Reduced to remaining scope 2026-08-14.** The verb shipped. Verified against the original
acceptance criteria:

| Criterion | State |
|---|---|
| (a) discover test files, ask each runner what it collects, diff | **shipped** — emits `gate-doctor/runner-unknown` per gate when collection cannot be verified, rather than passing silently |
| (b) execute each declared gate and confirm it runs | **shipped** — `adev gate doctor --execute`, verified actually running `npm test` and `npm run test:evals` |
| (c) verify CI config exists and invokes the gates | **shipped** — `lib/gates/doctor.mjs:73-74` checks `.github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}` and `.gitlab-ci.yml` |
| (d) flag unsubstituted `{{ }}` placeholders | **shipped** — `lib/gates/doctor.mjs:294`, `:820` |
| (e) flag gate commands pointing at gitignored or nonexistent paths | **shipped** — binary resolution across PATH / `node_modules/.bin` / literal path |
| Wire into `/adev:validate` | **shipped** — `validate.check-14-gate-executability`, `kind: deterministic-check`, calls `adev gate doctor --json` |
| Wire into `/adev:hygiene` | **shipped** — Audit Pass 8 (Governance Policy Health), `skills/hygiene/SKILL.md:359` |

## What remains — the defect absorbed from issue-625

`lib/gates/doctor.mjs::loadGates` (line 1109) reads `.context-index/governance/gates.yaml` directly:
`readFileSync` → `parseYaml` → return `doc.gates`. **No domain merge.**

Every real consumer executes the *merged* gate set — `lib/domains/merge-gates.mjs` composes bundled,
domain-profile and project gates. The doctor therefore verifies a different gate set than the one
validate and implement actually run. A gate contributed by a domain profile or extension overlay is
invisible to the doctor: it can be unrunnable, point at a gitignored path, or carry an unsubstituted
placeholder, and the doctor will report the project clean.

This inverts the verb's own thesis. It exists because adev verified authorship but never execution;
in its current form it verifies execution of a gate set that is not the one executed.

## Fix

Route `loadGates` through `lib/domains/merge-gates.mjs` so the doctor inspects the same merged set
its consumers run. Note that `merge-gates.mjs:36` rejects string commands (`INVALID_GATE`), so the
merged view may legitimately contain fewer gates than the raw file — that divergence is itself worth
reporting rather than silently dropping, and it is the subject of `adev-plugin-ogjm`.

## Priority

Held at P0. The original P1→P0 repricing reasoned that the thesis reproduces inside adev — `npm test`
is green while `npm run test:evals` is red with 27 failures, so "tests pass" is tier-dependent here.
That reasoning survives: a doctor blind to merged gates is blind to exactly the tier where the
failures live.

## Blocks

`adev-plugin-8ekd.1` (governance config population) — pre-wiring an integration tier by default is
gated on being able to verify that declared gates actually run. Edge transferred from
`adev-plugin-n8ko` when that issue was merged.

title: Redact out-of-repo absolute paths in session summaries
description:
Session capture writes absolute paths from unrelated repositories into committed session summaries. This is the root cause of the 2026-08-13 client-name leak into the public repo: .context-index/sessions/2026-05-27-9038da0.md and 2026-08-10-12e3fdb.md each leaked a client name through a 'Files touched:' line listing paths from other checkouts and /private/tmp scratchpads.

Fix: extend REDACTION_PATTERNS / redactSecrets() in lib/session-summary.mjs (applied unconditionally by fromTranscript) to redact absolute paths outside the repository root, emitting repo-relative paths only.

Scale evidence: during the 2026-08-14 stash rescue, 211 of 509 recovered files contained /Users/<user>/Development/<repo> absolute paths and 22 contained /private/tmp scratchpad paths. See PR #261.
close_reason: Fixed in 9fde06af. Out-of-repo absolute paths are now redacted at BOTH write chokepoints, not just the one named in the issue: fromTranscript (session-summary.mjs:536) and writeSummary (:833). That second one is what actually closes the cited 2026-08-13 leak — the leaked "Files touched:" lines are built by .githooks/post-commit:150 and written via writeSummary at :156, a path that never calls fromTranscript, so fixing only the transcript pipeline would have hardened the framework while leaving the real vector open. Design: patterns run LAST (path-first would eat the token= anchor in /Users/x/proj/token=abc123 and leave the secret exposed); prefix-scoped deny-list so /usr/bin/node survives by construction; FAILS CLOSED — a project root that is or contains homedir() is rejected so nothing is exempt. In-repo paths preserved as useful signal. 36 redaction tests, 89/89 across session-summary. Already-committed leaked files deliberately untouched — rewriting public history is a separate decision.

baselined until this is repaired.

INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED 2026-08-14 (md5 + line counts, not taken from the research):

  brainstorm

    conservative  04e2fee99d5d6522d80c66fb6c3a620e   216
    summarized    9076b0682890ab3b90a45e80911972b6   298   <-- IDENTICAL to baseline
    aggressive    9a8ea18c1ab166ef2afc0bc28543c5d4   179

    baseline      dca561eb812c9c47613f1260d29d575a   682 lines
    conservative  b5860cbaaa4f4f93c072a7417cf7585b   564
    summarized    dca561eb812c9c47613f1260d29d575a   682   <-- IDENTICAL to baseline

    conservative  MISSING
    summarized    455812c9d20a6e31cf3cb7225e25555f  1002   <-- LARGER than baseline
    aggressive    MISSING

Of 12 matrix cells: 2 missing, 2 byte-identical to baseline, and the one genuine
"summarized" variant is BIGGER than the thing it summarises. The summarized arm
therefore has exactly zero valid cells.

Also: tests/evals/skill-compression/outputs/ does not exist. The runner globs
outputs/<variant>/<skill>/output.md and scores nothing.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN NO DATA. Capture outputs now and the summarized arm scores
identically to baseline — not because summarising preserved quality, but because
the files are the same bytes. That reads as evidence that compression is free, and
it is the baseline every skill-consolidation issue in epic-9zqjfj would be measured
against.

REPAIR ORDER:
  1. Author genuine conservative/plan.md and aggressive/plan.md.
  2. Re-author summarized/{brainstorm,specify}.md as actual summarisations.
  3. Explain or fix summarized/plan.md being larger than baseline.
  4. Add a matrix-integrity check (no two cells byte-identical; no cell missing;
     summarized < baseline by line count) so this cannot silently regress.
  5. Only then capture outputs/ and wire the deterministic layer into CI.

The harness-simplification-study flags this as unfiled work — its epic-108 /
issue-620 citations name IDs that were never allocated. This is that issue.

Method note worth keeping, from the study: that audit checked whether each harness
RAN. It did not check whether each harness's INPUTS were valid. That is a distinct
check, and it is where this defect hid.
close_reason: Fixed. All 12 matrix cells now exist, are byte-distinct, and satisfy the ordering; verified independently (0 duplicate md5s). ROOT CAUSE, which the issue did not have: commit 1166071a created summarized/{brainstorm,specify}.md as VERBATIM baseline copies — filler to make the directory look complete — and summarized/plan.md was legitimately larger because summarized was originally a DIFFERENT AXIS: output verbosity (artifact-to-disk), not prompt compression. It was baseline plus a 33-line output directive. Resolved by making the arm both — condensed body plus the artifact-to-disk directive, applied uniformly. That is also why the integrity check deliberately has no conservative-vs-summarized assertion: the two arms compress along different axes. Line counts: brainstorm 298/216/261/179, specify 682/564/262/107, plan 969/875/369/195. Beyond line counts, each rubric match_pattern set was run against every variant prompt to prove no load-bearing instruction was dropped — baked into the test as a rubric floor, because a variant missing an instruction would make the eval report an authoring bug as a quality cost of compression. Integrity check: 39/39, and re-verified it still bites (removing one cell drops it to 36/3). TWO CAVEATS RECORDED: conservative/plan.md is a weak treatment at -9.7% because plan baseline is dominated by tables and fenced blocks the conservative tier keeps by definition, so its likely parity with baseline must NOT be read as compression being free; and the summarized arm intensity varies across skills (-12.4/-61.6/-61.9%), so do not average across skills within an arm — the harness scores per-skill against per-skill rubrics, so within-skill comparison is unaffected. outputs/ deliberately not captured; baselining is the next step and is now safe to take.

title: adev issues claim rejects ids that br show resolves — Phase 1.6 ownership gate silently unenforceable for those issues
description:
Found 2026-08-18 while running /adev:debug on adev-plugin-hl0m.

SYMPTOM
  adev issues claim adev-plugin-hl0m --owner dpavancini/local --branch fix/token-epic-bugs
  -> 'No beads issue for id: adev-plugin-hl0m', exit 1

but 'br show adev-plugin-hl0m' resolves the issue fine, as does 'br show --json'.

MEASURED PATTERN (4 ids, all of which br show resolves):
  adev-plugin-hl0m     br:OK  claim:FAIL(1)
  adev-plugin-ga1t     br:OK  claim:FAIL(1)
  adev-plugin-gkfv.4   br:OK  claim:OK
  adev-plugin-04jr.1   br:OK  claim:OK
  adev-plugin-882a.1   br:OK  claim:OK

The two failures are bare 4-char suffixes; the three successes carry a dotted
child suffix. That correlation is suggestive, not confirmed — n=5, and no attempt
was made to isolate the lookup path in lib/issues/. Someone should confirm before
treating 'dotted vs bare' as the rule.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ERROR MESSAGE

The debug skill's Phase 1.6 ownership claim treats exit 1 as non-blocking:
'usage error, unknown issue, or CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED_BACKEND -> warn and continue'.
That is the correct policy for a backend that genuinely cannot check-and-set. But
here the backend CAN, and the id is real — so a claimable issue is reported as
unclaimable and the agent proceeds unclaimed.

Phase 1.6 exists because two agents once independently fixed the same p0 an hour
apart. For every id in the failing class, that gate is currently a no-op that
announces itself as a warning and is designed to be ignored. This happened in the
session that found it: hl0m was investigated and fixed with no claim held.

Exit 1 conflates 'unknown id' with 'backend cannot claim'. Those warrant different
handling — the first is a bug worth surfacing loudly, the second is expected.

REPRO
  adev issues claim adev-plugin-ga1t --owner probe --branch tmp; echo $?

CAUTION FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: a successful claim mutates board state. See
adev-plugin-idqa — release does not revert status, so probing leaves issues
stranded in in_progress. Probe on a scratch board, or restore with
'br update <id> --status open' afterward.

title: Heuristics learn only from first-run PASS and are consulted only at skill entry — close the loop
description:
The heuristics loop is broken at both ends, in a mutually reinforcing way: the system learns only
from successes, and consults what it learned only at skill entry. The result is a store that
records "this went fine" and is never queried at the moment it would matter.

## What already works

Retrieval widened to 8 skills — brainstorm, debug, implement, plan, prototype, review-specs,
specify, validate — covered by `tests/skills/heuristic-injection-widening.test.mjs`. The store,
schema (`.context-index/memory/heuristics/_format.md`), and `lib/heuristics.mjs` all landed.

## Defect 1 — capture fires only on first-run PASS

`adev heuristics extract` is validate Check 13, "first-run PASS heuristic capture".
`lib/cli/heuristics.mjs:129` hardcodes the title prefix `"First-run PASS: "`, and
`--check-first-run` SKIPs when a validate report already exists. Automatic capture therefore fires
only when a spec passes on its first attempt, and is structurally blind to failures.

This explains the measured inertness better than "the feature is weak": `harness-simplification-study.md`
found 13 of 28 entries are a content-free template, 0 entries ever contradicted, no promotions ever
observed. A capture rule keyed to first-try passes will mostly record that nothing went wrong.

`/adev:learn` can capture a failure lesson, but only when a human thinks to invoke it.

## Defect 2 — retrieval is skill-entry only, never on error

Every call site fires once, at skill start, keyed on module slug:

```
adev heuristics retrieve --module <charter-module> --tier summary --format text
```

`skills/debug/SKILL.md:70-71` is the only site passing `--keyword <token>...`, so the retrieval API
already has the error-matching axis — seven of eight callers ignore it, and none re-queries when
something actually fails. A test fails inside `/adev:implement`, a tool errors, a gate trips, and
the injected context is whatever the module scope returned minutes earlier, capped at 8 entries.

The hook layer is wired for the write side only: `hooks/post-validate-extract-heuristics.mjs` runs
PostToolUse to extract. There is no counterpart that retrieves on an error signal, though
`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse` and `Stop` are all registered events.

The schema is already error-shaped for this — `/adev:learn` stores an `anti-pattern` field, the
explicit "don't do this" counter-rule derived from the lesson's failure case.

## Defect 3 — nothing halts a batch repeating one systemic failure

Phase 2 item 3 of the harness simplification roadmap, never filed. The rule: if the same finding ID
fails N specs in a batch, halt the batch and escalate once. This is the batch-level analogue of
`lib/loop-convergence.mjs`'s NO_PROGRESS, which already detects non-progress within a single loop.

Cost evidence, 2026-05-15 retro: ~2.5 hours and ~$40-50 on 10 implement+validate dispatches sent
knowing each would fail on the same pre-existing test failure. Related: 40% of validate reports
contain the phrase "pre-existing failure", and all 6 current FAILs trace to harness instability
rather than implementation defects.

## Why these are one spec, not three

They share a key. A breaker that halts on N identical finding IDs is doing error-signature matching
— the same key an error-triggered retrieval would look up, and the same key the resulting heuristic
would be filed under. Fixing retrieval alone gives a fast lookup into an empty index; fixing capture
alone fills an index nothing queries at the right moment; the breaker without either has nothing to
consult and nowhere to record what it learned.

Proposed behaviors:

1. Error-signature keying — a stable, matchable identity for a recurring failure.
2. Retrieval on error, via hook, keyed by that signature (the `--keyword` axis already exists).
3. Capture on failure, especially recurring failure, with the breaker's escalation as trigger.

## Related

`harness-simplification-study.md` Phase 2. Discussion in
`.context-index/research/lean-review-validation.md` F1 (roadmap cross-check).

title: BeadsAdapter never reads dependencies back — _toIssue() omits the field entirely
description: Found 2026-08-13 by a round-trip fidelity check after migrating this repo's 311-issue board. IMPORTANT: this is a READ gap, not data loss. The edges are correctly stored in beads -- 'br list -s all --json' shows 31 items with dependency_count > 0, and issue-628 correctly reports 2 (its edges to issue-626 and issue-627), matching what the migration reported (dependencies_replayed: 44). But every issue returned by BeadsAdapter.list() and .get() comes back with dependencies undefined/empty, because _toIssue() maps title/status/priority/type and the agent_context fields and never populates dependencies. MEASURED: source board has 44 dependency edges; 44 of 44 are absent on read-back through the adapter. CONSEQUENCE: anything that reasons about blocking relationships is silently wrong on the beads backend. '/adev:issues ready' is specified as 'open AND unblocked' and filters on dependencies -- with none visible, every blocked issue reports as ready. The wave sequencing recorded on epic-108 (554->552, 555->552, 615->555, 614->559, 557->585/586, 623->557, 625->552/554) would vanish from every query while remaining perfectly intact in the database. That is the dangerous shape: the data is right, the view is wrong, and nothing errors. title: adev install/upgrade: plugin enabled user-wide before the user/project scope prompt; domain picker runs at install instead of init
description:
The install/upgrade sequence performs two irreversible actions before (or instead of) the point at which the user gets to decide them.

DEFECT 1 — plugin is installed AND enabled user-wide before the scope prompt.
cli/index.mjs:605-615 (claude-code branch of installProviders()):
  1. `await provider.install()` is called with NO opts, so providers/claude-code/adapter.mjs:53 defaults `scope = "user"`, and adapter.mjs:85 calls `this.enable("user")` — writing `enabledPlugins["adev@agentic-development"] = true` into ~/.claude/settings.json (adapter.mjs:123-136).
  2. ONLY THEN does cli/index.mjs:613 ask "Install for all projects (user) or this project only (project)?".
  3. cli/index.mjs:614 calls `provider.enable("project")`, which writes <cwd>/.claude/settings.json — but nothing ever REMOVES the user-scope entry written in step 1.

Consequence: answering "project" does not produce a project-scoped install. The plugin stays enabled for every project on the machine, and the user is never told. The prompt is effectively cosmetic for the "project" answer.

Related: adapter.mjs:99-117 `updateRegistry()` hardcodes `scope: existing?.scope || "user"` in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, so a fresh install records "user" regardless of the answer.

In-repo precedent for the correct shape: the codex branch at cli/index.mjs:667-678 asks for scope FIRST, then calls `provider.install({ scope: targetScope })`. The claude-code branch should match it. (The cursor branch at cli/index.mjs:680 hardcodes `scope: "user"` with no prompt at all — worth deciding intentionally rather than leaving implicit.)

DEFECT 2 — domain-extension picker runs at install/upgrade time, not at init time.
cli/index.mjs:975 (cmdInstall) and cli/index.mjs:1128 (cmdUpgrade) both call runDomainPicker(), which installs a domain extension into the project and writes `domain: <name>` into .context-index/manifest.yaml. This happens during CLI install — before the user has run /adev:init and before any project configuration exists (install has only scaffolded pristine templates at that point). Picking a domain is a project-configuration decision and belongs with the rest of them.

Documented intent already disagrees with the wiring: lib/cli/domain-extension-picker.mjs's module header calls it the "Init-time domain-extension picker helper" while documenting cmdInstall()/cmdUpgrade() as its consumers.

Note on scope of the fix: skills/init/SKILL.md has a "Domain Extension Picker" section (~lines 950-992), but it only DOCUMENTS the picker as an `adev install`/`adev upgrade` step — /adev:init does not itself run the picker. So the fix is not merely "delete the call from install/upgrade"; it also needs a picker step added to the init flow, plus the SKILL.md section rewritten to describe init-time behavior.

SCOPE
- cli/index.mjs installProviders() claude-code branch (605-615); decide cursor branch (680) too
- providers/claude-code/adapter.mjs install()/enable()/updateRegistry() — scope must be honored end to end, including removing/never-writing the user entry when "project" is chosen
- cli/index.mjs cmdInstall() (975) and cmdUpgrade() (1128) — remove runDomainPicker()
- skills/init/SKILL.md — add the picker as an init step; rewrite the Domain Extension Picker section
- Tests for both paths (install and upgrade), asserting that answering "project" leaves ~/.claude/settings.json untouched

ACCEPTANCE
1. No user-wide write of any kind occurs before the scope answer is collected.
2. Answering "project" writes only <cwd>/.claude/settings.json; ~/.claude/settings.json gains no enabledPlugins entry for adev. (The extraKnownMarketplaces user-level write at adapter.mjs:138-172 is a separate concern — decide explicitly whether it is exempt, and document the decision.)
3. installed_plugins.json records the scope the user actually chose.
4. `adev install` and `adev upgrade` do not run the domain-extension picker.
5. /adev:init runs the picker and writes `domain:` to manifest.yaml.
6. Both defects covered by tests on the install AND upgrade paths.

Found 2026-08-14 during a walkthrough of the install/upgrade UX.
notes: Fix in PR #274 (fix/cli/install-scope), CI green after a re-run of an unrelated flaky CAS-concurrency test. AC-6 per operator: user entry REMOVED on project scope. Prompt audit found 3 misplaced prompts (domain picker, sync targets, provenance) all writing context-layer config from the CLI; all moved to /adev:init. 10 new tests. Two bugs found in the fix itself by the tests (write ordering vs marketplace block; /var vs /private/var path identity) kept as regressions. Not closed until merged.

title: Validator ID prefix mismatch — skill prose drops the "validate." prefix
description:
Surfaced by lifecycle-event audit on 2026-05-17 (LIFE-2). Partially negates PR #130.

PR #130 routed validator-severity lookups from gates.yaml to validate.yaml. validate.yaml entries use the prefixed form `validate.check-2-spec-compliance`. But skills/validate/SKILL.md (lines 363–374 and elsewhere) tells operators to emit `adev report --type validator --validator check-2-spec-compliance` (NO prefix). The severity-resolution lookup then misses every entry and defaults to severity: warning, suppressing blocker-severity FAILs in the aggregation table.

Effectively re-introduces the UNKNOWN_VALIDATOR_DEFAULTED symptom that issue-507 + PR #130 were supposed to eliminate.

Fix (pick ONE):
- A. Update skill prose to use the prefixed form consistently (cheapest; pure markdown).
- B. Strip the prefix from validate.yaml and the domain starter (touches more files; risks breaking the loader if other code references the prefixed form).

Option A is recommended.

Acceptance:
- skills/validate/SKILL.md emits validators with the same ID strings declared in validate.yaml.
- After emitting a real validator_report event, no UNKNOWN_VALIDATOR_DEFAULTED warning is printed.
- Add a CI test that walks every id in governance/validate.yaml and asserts the skill prose calls `adev report --type validator --validator <id>` verbatim.; Closed: PR #133 merged; validator IDs in skill prose match validate.yaml prefix

title: Skill Validation Improvements
description:
Nothing in this repo validates the 30 SKILL.md files against the Agent Skills
specification. Filed 2026-08-18 after running agent-ecosystem/skill-validator
v1.6.0 across all of them for the first time.

=== HOW THIS WAS MEASURED ===

  go install github.com/agent-ecosystem/skill-validator/cmd/skill-validator@latest
  for d in skills/*/; do skill-validator check "$d" -o json; done

All 30 exit 1. That number is misleading: the errors are two systemic issues
repeated 29 times plus one genuine per-skill fault, not 60 independent problems.
Read the children for the split.

Installed via 'go install' rather than the documented Homebrew tap, because
'brew install' refuses the tap without 'brew trust agent-ecosystem/tap', which
grants that third-party tap persistent trust on the machine.

=== WHY AN EPIC ===

Five findings share one root cause: the skills were authored against adev's own
conventions and never checked against the published spec. They need to be
resolved together, because deciding the naming and layout questions determines
what the CI gate can enforce. Wiring the gate first would either fail on all 30
skills or need suppression flags that hide the very drift it exists to catch.

=== SEQUENCING ===

5yfz.1 (link escape) is independent and can land immediately — it is a real
fault with no policy question attached.

5yfz.2 (naming) and 5yfz.4 (layout/frontmatter) are POLICY DECISIONS, not
defects. Each needs a human ruling on whether adev deliberately diverges from
the spec or was accidentally non-conformant. Both block the gate.

5yfz.5 (CI gate) lands LAST. Its --allow-dirs / --allow-flat-layouts /
--allow-extra-frontmatter flags encode whatever 5yfz.2 and 5yfz.4 decide, so
authoring it first bakes in an unreviewed answer.

5yfz.3 (token budgets) is independent of the gate and belongs as much to the
token-cost epic adev-plugin-04jr as to this one.

=== WHAT skill-validator DOES AND DOES NOT COVER ===

Recorded because it was initially overstated in the session that filed this.

COVERS: structure, frontmatter fields, token/line budgets, unclosed fences,
internal link resolution, orphan files, external links, content-density metrics,
and LLM-as-judge scoring (not run — needs a provider and makes API calls).

DOES NOT COVER: content semantics. It cannot check that a SKILL.md documents a
particular flag, section, or step.

This matters for adev-plugin-test-suite-per-behavior-granularity-usiy. Lever 1
there needs a replacement for ~718 artifact-prose test cases before they can be
deleted. skill-validator subsumes only the STRUCTURAL subset — measured at 35 of
219 artifact cases under tests/skills, against 184 that assert on content. It
does NOT unblock Lever 1. Behavioural coverage would need promptfoo or the
trigger evals shipped in the skill-creator plugin.

title: using-adev SKILL.md links escape the skill directory — three ../../docs references break self-containment
description:
skill-validator v1.6.0 reports three errors on skills/using-adev/SKILL.md:

  internal link escapes skill directory: ../../docs/skill-reference.md
  internal link escapes skill directory: ../../docs/cli-reference.md
  internal link escapes skill directory: ../../docs/README.md

All three are on one line (skills/using-adev/SKILL.md:72), a paragraph pointing
readers at the docs index for per-skill usage, the full CLI verb surface, and
end-user topics.

WHY IT IS A REAL FAULT AND NOT A CONVENTION QUIBBLE

using-adev is the ONLY skill of the 30 with this error, so it is not an adev-wide
pattern being flagged — it is one file diverging from the other 29.

It also matters more here than it would elsewhere, for two reasons:

1. using-adev is injected at SessionStart, not invoked on demand. It is the
   gateway skill every session receives, so a broken relative reference in it is
   the first thing an agent sees.
2. Agent Skills are meant to be self-contained and portable. A '../../docs'
   reference resolves only when the skill sits inside this repository at exactly
   this depth. Anywhere the skill is copied, installed, or vendored — which is
   the whole point of the plugin distribution path — those links dangle.

FIX OPTIONS, no ruling made

  a. Point at the published docs URL instead of a relative path.
  b. Name the paths as plain text ('see docs/skill-reference.md in the adev
     repo') without making them markdown links, so nothing pretends to resolve.
  c. Copy the needed material into skills/using-adev/references/.

(a) or (b) keep the skill small, which matters because using-adev is loaded every
session. (c) contradicts adev-plugin-5yfz.3 by adding weight to an always-loaded
skill.

Independent of the rest of the epic: this is a fault with no policy question
attached, so it does not need 5yfz.2 or 5yfz.4 to be settled first.

REPRO
  skill-validator check skills/using-adev

title: Skill name frontmatter: 29 of 30 carry an adev: prefix the spec rejects, and using-adev proves the bare form works
description:
skill-validator reports two errors on 29 of the 30 skills, both from the same
frontmatter field:

  name "adev:debug" must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, no
      leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens
  name does not match directory name (expected "debug", got "adev:debug")

THIS IS A POLICY QUESTION, NOT A CONFIRMED DEFECT. Do not mass-rename on the
strength of a validator exit code.

=== THE EVIDENCE THAT MAKES IT WORTH ASKING ===

skills/using-adev/SKILL.md is the sole exception. Its frontmatter reads
'name: using-adev' — no prefix — and it still surfaces to the agent as
'adev:using-adev' in the session skill list. So for at least one skill, the
harness applies the namespace itself and the frontmatter prefix is redundant.

If that generalises, 29 skills are non-conformant to the published spec for no
functional benefit, and the odd one out is the only correct one.

=== WHAT MUST BE ESTABLISHED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING ===

1. Does Claude Code derive the '<plugin>:<skill>' invocation name from the plugin
   manifest and directory, or from the frontmatter 'name' field? using-adev
   suggests the former, but n=1.
2. Does anything in this repo READ the prefixed name? Check .claude-plugin/,
   hooks, lib/skill-ext (which is invoked as 'adev skill-ext load --skill <slug>'
   with a BARE slug per CLAUDE.md), and the provider mirrors under providers/.
3. Do the other providers (cursor, copilot, opencode) resolve skill names the
   same way? A rename correct for Claude Code could break a mirror.
4. Is the Agent Skills 'name' rule even normative for plugin-provided skills, or
   only for standalone ones? The validator does not distinguish.

=== RISK ===

Renaming the frontmatter of 29 skills is a wide, low-visibility change with a
plausible failure mode: skills silently stop being discoverable or stop matching
their extension lookups. It also touches tests/skills-extension-coverage.test.mjs
and anything asserting on skill names. If the answer to (1) is 'frontmatter', the
prefix is load-bearing and the correct fix is the reverse — give using-adev the
prefix the others have.

BLOCKS adev-plugin-5yfz.5: the CI gate either enforces the spec rule or passes
--allow-* suppression, and that choice is exactly this decision.

REPRO
  skill-validator check skills/debug     # 2 errors
  skill-validator check skills/using-adev # no naming error

title: 16 of 30 SKILL.md bodies exceed the 5,000-token spec guidance — 194,898 tokens total, hygiene at 3.2x
description:
Measured 2026-08-18 with skill-validator v1.6.0. The Agent Skills spec recommends
a SKILL.md body under 5,000 tokens and under 500 lines. 16 of 30 exceed the token
guidance; 11 also exceed the line guidance.

  tokens  lines  skill
  16018   1260   hygiene
  15304    956   build
  14935   1133   specify
  13939    852   implement
  13524    711   validate
  11648   1072   init
  11460    908   plan
   9220    517   review-specs
   8284    642   brainstorm
   7052    589   write-test
   6025    524   retro
   6004         recover
   5763         status
   5417         debug
   5230         work
   5188         prototype

TOTAL ACROSS ALL 30 SKILL.md BODIES: 194,898 tokens.
Largest compliant skill: sync at 4,071. Smallest: document at 1,299.

=== WHY THIS IS A COST FINDING, NOT A STYLE NIT ===

A SKILL.md body is loaded in full when its skill is invoked. hygiene at 16,018
tokens is 3.2x the guidance, and per the measurement recorded on
adev-plugin-04jr, cache_read was 98.1% of one real lifecycle's token cost — every
loaded token is re-read on all subsequent turns in that context, so body size is
multiplied by turn count, not paid once.

RELATED, and should be read together with this:
  adev-plugin-04jr.1 — the same SKILL.md is loaded in full more than once per
      session. Deduplication and body size multiply: fixing one without the other
      leaves most of the cost.
  adev-plugin-gkfv.4 — orchestrator loop norms.

This issue is filed under the skill-validation epic because that is how it was
found, but the payoff belongs to adev-plugin-04jr. Cross-link rather than
duplicate.

=== CAUTION ===

Do NOT treat this as a mandate to cut prose. Progressive disclosure is the
spec-sanctioned move: relocate material an agent needs only sometimes into
references/ and load it on demand, keeping the always-read body small. That
interacts with adev-plugin-5yfz.4, which is about the ~30 files currently sitting
at skill root instead of references/ — several of those (mode files, reviewer
prompts) look like exactly the material that should be split out, so the two
issues should be sequenced together.

Also note the biggest bodies are the most load-bearing skills (hygiene, build,
specify, implement, validate). Aggressive trimming there is the highest-risk
edit in the repo. Measure before and after with 'adev cost summary', which works
in a worktree again as of adev-plugin-882a.1.

REPRO
  for d in skills/*/; do skill-validator check "$d" -o json; done

title: Skill layout diverges from the spec: mode files and reviewer prompts at skill root, two unknown directories, non-spec context frontmatter field
description:
skill-validator warnings across the 30 skills, all variants of 'the layout is not
the one the spec describes'. POLICY QUESTION, like adev-plugin-5yfz.2 — the
validator is reporting divergence, not proving harm.

=== 1. ~30 files at skill root instead of references/ ===

The spec expects only SKILL.md at root, with supporting material under
scripts/, references/ or assets/. adev puts mode files and reviewer prompts at
root, e.g.:

  build/       milestone-mode.md, epic-mode.md, feature-mode.md, release-mode.md,
               resume-mode.md, mode-router.md, workspace-mode.md
  research/    internal-researcher-prompt.md, web-researcher-prompt.md,
               github-researcher-prompt.md, synthesis-prompt.md
  review-specs/ structural-architect-prompt.md, security-reviewer-prompt.md,
               consistency-analyzer-prompt.md, quick-synthesized-reviewer-prompt.md
  implement/   tdd-mandate.md, integration-gate.md, code-quality-checklist.md,
               failure-path-exit-event.md, parallel-mode.md
  write-test/  detect-framework.{mjs,sh}, detect-gaming.{mjs,sh},
               write-handoff.{mjs,sh}
  plan/        plan-reviewer-prompt.md, charter-mode.md
  brainstorm/  charter-reviewer-prompt.md
  eval/        default-rubric.yaml

The validator's stated concern is that agents assuming the standard layout will
not find them. Whether that is real depends on whether anything other than adev's
own skills reads these paths — adev names them explicitly in SKILL.md prose, so
for adev they resolve. The portability cost lands on anyone consuming these skills
outside this repo.

Two of these are shell/mjs pairs (detect-framework, detect-gaming, write-handoff)
which per the spec belong in scripts/, and that is the least contentious subset.

=== 2. Unknown directories ===

  validate/ checks/     13 files
  issues/   adapters/    1 file

=== 3. Non-spec frontmatter field ===

  skills/deploy/SKILL.md and skills/research/SKILL.md declare 'context:',
  which the spec does not recognise. Either it is load-bearing for adev and the
  gate must allow it, or it is vestigial in two files and should go. Check
  whether anything reads it before deleting.

=== SEQUENCING ===

Do this WITH adev-plugin-5yfz.3, not separately. That issue needs oversized bodies
split into references/; this issue is about material already sitting outside
SKILL.md but in the wrong place. Same edit, same review, and doing them apart
means touching every large skill twice.

BLOCKS adev-plugin-5yfz.5. The gate's --allow-dirs / --allow-flat-layouts /
--exclude-token-paths / --allow-extra-frontmatter flags are the encoding of
whatever is decided here. Authoring the gate first bakes in an unreviewed answer
and, worse, suppresses the drift it exists to detect.

DO NOT mass-move files on the strength of a warning. Every mode file and prompt
is referenced by path from SKILL.md prose; moving one without updating its
references breaks the skill at runtime with no test catching it — the skills tests
assert on SKILL.md content, not on whether referenced paths resolve.

title: Add skill-validator as a CI gate — nothing currently checks the 30 SKILL.md files against the Agent Skills spec
description:
Nothing in this repo validates the 30 SKILL.md files against the Agent Skills
specification. The gap was invisible until skill-validator was run by hand on
2026-08-18 and every skill exited 1.

Existing skill tests do NOT close this gap. They assert on SKILL.md CONTENT
('documents the --full flag', 'declares Full Pipeline as a mode') via substring
matching. Nothing checks frontmatter validity, token budgets, link resolution,
unclosed fences, or orphan files — the failure classes this gate covers.

=== TOOL ===

agent-ecosystem/skill-validator v1.6.0, Go, MIT.
  https://github.com/agent-ecosystem/skill-validator

  skill-validator check <skill-dir> [--only structure,links,content,contamination]
                                    [-o json|text|compact|markdown]
                                    [--emit-annotations]   # GitHub Actions ::error
                                    [--strict]             # warnings become exit 1

Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 errors, 2 warnings (inverted by --strict).
--emit-annotations makes findings appear inline on the PR diff.

NOT an npm dependency — a standalone binary. It therefore does not require the
ADR that the constitution mandates for new external dependencies, unlike a
devDependency would. Install in CI via 'go install ...@v1.6.0'. PIN THE VERSION:
a floating @latest turns an upstream release into a surprise red build, and this
tool's warning set is not stable across versions.

INSTALL CAVEAT: the documented 'brew install' path refuses the tap without
'brew trust agent-ecosystem/tap', which grants that third-party tap persistent
trust. 'go install' avoids that and is the better CI path anyway.

=== BLOCKED BY 5yfz.2 AND 5yfz.4 — DO NOT LAND FIRST ===

Today the gate would fail on all 30 skills. The only way to make it green now is
--allow-extra-frontmatter, --allow-flat-layouts and --allow-dirs, which suppress
precisely the drift the gate exists to catch. Those flags are the encoding of the
naming and layout decisions, so the decisions come first.

Land 5yfz.1 (real fault, no policy attached) before the gate regardless.

=== DESIGN NOTES FOR WHOEVER BUILDS IT ===

1. Errors and warnings need different treatment. Fail the build on errors; report
   warnings without failing, at least initially. --strict on day one would block
   every PR on the 16 oversized bodies from 5yfz.3, which are a real but separate
   piece of work.
2. Token budgets are better as a RATCHET than a threshold: fail when a skill grows,
   not when it is already over. Otherwise the gate is red until 5yfz.3 completes
   and gets ignored or bypassed in the meantime — the failure mode where a gate
   trains people to skip it.
3. Decide the scope of providers/*/skills/** mirrors. CLAUDE.md puts them out of
   scope for the inline-Node pre-commit hook; the same call probably applies, but
   it should be explicit rather than incidental.
4. Consider fitting this to the existing gate surface (adev gate / gates.yaml,
   see adev-plugin-3sw and adev-plugin-8ekd.2) rather than adding a standalone
   workflow, so there is one place to look for what gates the repo.
5. 'skill-validator score' adds LLM-as-judge dimensions (clarity, actionability,
   token efficiency, scope discipline, directive precision, novelty). NOT run yet,
   and it makes API calls — keep it out of the blocking gate; a scheduled
   advisory run is the sane placement.

title: `adev worktree merge` reports any git failure as MERGE_CONFLICT, and aborts a clean merge
description:
ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED. `mergeWorktree` (lib/worktree.mjs:226-247) wraps `git merge`
in a try/catch that treats ANY non-zero exit as a merge conflict. The caught `err`
is never inspected — git's stderr, which carries the real reason, is discarded.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, the second worse than the first.

1. MISLEADING DIAGNOSIS. On a non-conflict failure, `git diff --diff-filter=U`
   returns nothing, so the thrown message reads:

     MERGE_CONFLICT: merge of adev/fix-513 conflicts on 0 file(s):

   A conflict on zero files is a contradiction, and it sends the operator
   looking for conflicted files that do not exist.

2. IT DISCARDS A CLEAN MERGE. Line 239 runs `git merge --abort` unconditionally
   in the catch. When the merge itself succeeded and only the COMMIT was rejected,
   the staged, conflict-free merge is thrown away. The caller is told it conflicted
   and is left with nothing.

OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-14 merging adev/fix-513. The real cause was the commit-msg
hook rejecting the merge commit for a missing `Spec:` trailer — a hook this repo
ships and enforces on every commit, so this is not an exotic path. The merge had
no conflicts at all: retrying with plain `git merge --no-ff` produced a clean
staged merge and the hook's actual message, and completing it with a Spec: trailer
succeeded on the first try.

COST OF THE MISDIAGNOSIS: believing the verb, I ran `scripts/sync-provider-skills.mjs`
on top of what I thought was a completed merge, generating provider mirrors from
pre-merge skills that then had to be reverted.

PROPOSED FIX
  (a) Only report MERGE_CONFLICT when `--diff-filter=U` is NON-EMPTY. Otherwise
      surface the underlying git failure verbatim with a distinct code, e.g.
      MERGE_FAILED, carrying err.stderr.
  (b) Do not `merge --abort` when there are no conflicted paths. A hook-rejected
      merge is recoverable by fixing the message and committing; aborting destroys
      that. Leave the tree staged and say so.
  (c) Name the commit-msg hook case explicitly if detectable, since this repo
      requires a Spec: trailer on merge commits touching spec-manifest files —
      making it the most likely failure the verb will ever hit here.

Verified by reading lib/worktree.mjs:224-248 and reproducing both the failure and
the clean retry.

title: Author one regression rubric per skill epic-102 intends to change, BEFORE changing it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13. 32 rubric files exist across 7 eval directories, which overstates coverage badly. Only THREE are per-skill compression-regression rubrics — tests/evals/skill-compression/rubrics/{brainstorm,plan,specify}.yaml — covering 3 of 30 skills, and one of those three (plan) sits on the broken variant matrix in issue-620. The other 29 rubrics score different things: whole-workflow scenarios (work-tracking, configurable-governance), domain-level project comparisons (comparison/), infrastructure honesty (integration-sandbox), and a data-domain set (data-engineering). A rubric that scores a six-step lifecycle scenario tells you the pipeline ran; it cannot tell you that /adev:route's scoring degraded after its prose was compressed.

THIRTEEN skills have no rubric mention at all: codehealth, deploy, init, learn, prototype, reconcile, recover, repomap, research, retro, sample, sync, using-adev.

THE OVERLAP THAT MAKES THIS URGENT: the skills epic-102 queues for demotion, merging and deletion are almost exactly the skills with no coverage. issue-573 targets codehealth, repomap, document, deploy, sync; issue-574 targets learn and issues; issue-575 merges eval into validate --score, assess into init --brownfield, and reduces using-adev; issue-576 deletes skills/standalone; issue-571 rewrites prototype. Of those, codehealth / repomap / deploy / sync / learn / using-adev / prototype / standalone have NO rubric, and issues / eval / assess / document are touched only by scenario rubrics. That is not a coincidence — they are the peripheral skills, which is both why they look expendable and why nobody built evals for them. The consequence is that the simplification sweep would run exactly where the regression net is thinnest.

SCOPE: not 30 rubrics. One rubric per skill epic-102 intends to touch — roughly 10 — each authored BEFORE that skill is modified, so the comparison is against a captured baseline rather than a memory of how it used to behave. Cheap to write: the existing scenarios (tests/evals/skill-compression/scenarios/*.md) are self-contained prompts carrying simulated user responses, so runs are reproducible without a human in the loop. Follow the existing rubric shape — regex-matched required_elements (deterministic, 50%) plus weighted quality_dimensions (50%) — with the judged half restructured into BINARY per-criterion verdicts rather than 1-5 scales, per the external research on judge reliability.

SEQUENCING: this is the real gate on epic-102, not a nice-to-have. A rubric authored after a skill is compressed measures the compressed skill against itself. Priority order should follow epic-102's own: 573 and 575 first (they touch the most skills), then 574, 571, 576.

NUANCE for issue-576 (delete skills/standalone): a deleted skill needs a different test, not a compression rubric — assert that the CLI path it wrapped still works and that no caller is stranded. Worth stating explicitly so nobody writes a rubric for a file that is about to vanish.

Reference target from the research digest: 20-50 tasks drawn from real failures, each with a reference solution, outcome-graded, held near 100% as a regression gate. Three compression rubrics is roughly a tenth of that floor.

title: MIN_BR_VERSION floor is 0.2.0, but the merge-driven database-corruption fix landed in br 0.2.19
description:
lib/issues/beads-adapter.mjs:52 sets MIN_BR_VERSION = "0.2.0", enforced by a
`br --version` preflight at :189. The floor was chosen because 0.2.x moved `--db`
semantics — a compatibility boundary, not a safety one.

But beads_rust v0.2.19 shipped an engine upgrade fixing **deterministic database
corruption from merge operations** (per the upstream release notes surveyed in
.context-index/research/issue-board-merge-conflicts.md).

So the range 0.2.0 through 0.2.18 passes the preflight and is exposed to
merge-driven corruption — on a backend whose entire purpose is surviving
concurrent branches. Related 0.2.x fixes in that window: v0.2.20 schema-migration
upgrade path and sync data-loss guards, v0.2.21 a macOS/Windows "database is busy"
regression fix.

This matters more now than when the research was written: this repo switched
tasks.backend to beads on 2026-08-13 (535c4a9a), so adev's own board is on it, and
the shipped default is what users inherit.

Local install is 0.2.22, so this machine is not exposed — the gap is the floor
admitting versions that are.

PROPOSED FIX: raise MIN_BR_VERSION to 0.2.19 (0.2.21 preferable, to clear the
busy-regression too), with the corruption fix named in the error message so the
reason is legible rather than looking like arbitrary version churn. Document the
minimum in docs/configuration.md alongside the backend fix in issue-0qtm6x.

Verified 2026-08-14: MIN_BR_VERSION = "0.2.0" at beads-adapter.mjs:52; local br
reports 0.2.22.
close_reason: Fixed in ae8cd8fd. MIN_BR_VERSION raised 0.2.0 -> 0.2.19 (beads-adapter.mjs:52) with both boundaries documented at the constant so it is not lowered again: compatibility (why not 0.1.x) and safety (the v0.2.19 merge-corruption fix). The preflight error message was also factually wrong for the newly-rejected range and now names the corruption fix. Stale references updated in backend-adapters.spec.md:41,56 and docs/cli-reference.md:496. Verified: 233+30 issue-board tests pass, plus 18 live constructions against real br 0.2.22. Known coverage gap recorded on the commit — nothing regression-tests the constant itself.

title: /adev:route mutates plan files — sibling .routing.md fix + cursor-provider 5-plan migration
description:
Source: cursor-provider retro 2026-05-19 + /adev:debug subagent transcript (agent ID affc19ea4ef7212c7).
Consolidated re-filing after the prior issue-525 + issue-528 entries were lost in an external rollback of the shared tasks.json.

## The bug

/adev:route Step 4 (skills/route/SKILL.md:108-133) is explicitly instructed to write **Routing:** / **Scores:** / **Rationale:** blocks into each task header inside the plan markdown file. This runs AFTER /adev:plan Step 7 (skills/plan/SKILL.md:678-701) has already emitted plan_task pending events to the lifecycle log.

This directly violates the authoritative-channel invariant CON-8 in agent-reliable-state-artifacts/plan-task-events.spec.md:50-58 ("Plan markdown is read-only after authoring ... /adev:plan writes the plan file once") and AC bullet 5 ("Plan markdown files are not mutated by /adev:plan or /adev:implement after initial authoring").

The detector in lib/plan-immutability.mjs correctly catches this for untracked plans. Cursor-provider plans A-E currently "pass" the detector only because they were committed as a single add (no --diff-filter=M history), which masks rather than fixes the violation.

Reproduction (during cursor-provider session 2026-05-19): both Spec D (cli-install-integration.plan.md) and Spec E (sync-target-output.plan.md) plans had filesystem mtime 2-3 minutes later than their first plan_task pending event in the lifecycle log. Once the plans were committed in d0f8303 and 199928a, the detector relaxed (relied on git history instead of mtime). The underlying violation persists.

## Design decision required

Two viable approaches:
  (a) Sibling .routing.md — /adev:route writes <plan-stem>.routing.md keyed by task ID; /adev:implement reads from it. Preserves human readability, adds one file per plan. Matches the .blockers.md pattern already adopted in commit 7e333fd for review BLOCK handling.
  (c) Lifecycle-log plan_task_routing event — /adev:route emits one event per task into the existing JSONL; /adev:implement reads it like other lifecycle state. No new file, but harder for humans to inspect routing decisions at a glance.

Variant (b) auto-commit-after-plan was rejected during /adev:debug — it silences the immutability detector via git history but still violates CON-8 prose ("read-only after authoring"), and forces an uncommitted-plans-impossible workflow.

Recommendation: variant (a) for consistency with the .blockers.md sidecar pattern.

## Files to change (variant a)

  - skills/route/SKILL.md:108-133 — Step 4: rewrite to write sibling .routing.md instead of mutating plan
  - skills/route/SKILL.md:168-174 — Integration with /adev:implement: point reader at sidecar
  - skills/route/SKILL.md:193 — Red Flag: tighten to "never modify the plan file"
  - skills/implement/SKILL.md — reader change: load routing from sibling .routing.md
  - .context-index/specs/features/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/plan-task-events.spec.md:50-58 — CON-8: enumerate .routing.md as a permitted peer artifact (alongside .review.md, .validate.md, .blockers.md)

## Migration of 5 already-mutated cursor-provider plans

Once the fix lands, the existing plans on the cursor-provider/cursor-adapter branch will have stale inline annotations. Affected:
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/hook-config-generator.plan.md (Spec A)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/cursor-adapter.plan.md (Spec B)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/plugin-manifest-and-parity.plan.md (Spec C)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/cli-install-integration.plan.md (Spec D)
  - .context-index/specs/features/cursor-provider/sync-target-output.plan.md (Spec E)

Two migration options:
  (i) Extract: parse each plan, lift the **Routing:**/**Scores:**/**Rationale:** blocks into a new sibling .routing.md, rewrite the plan body without them, stamp the M-commit hash into manifest.yaml hygiene.plan_immutability.exempt_commits[]. Cleanest end state, more work.
  (ii) Leave as historical noise: do not rewrite. New /adev:route invocations on these plans would refuse to write (plan is locked), so any re-routing requires manual extraction. Simpler, but leaves the plans with inline annotations that future readers may mistake for the canonical format.

## Followups flagged in /adev:debug

  1. Draft an ADR titled "Plan-adjacent sidecar artifacts" documenting the .routing.md and .blockers.md sidecar pattern with rationale grounded in the authoritative-channel invariant. The pattern is now used twice (route + review BLOCK in commit 7e333fd) so a single ADR captures both.
  2. Extend lib/plan-immutability.mjs to catch the "mutate-then-single-add-commit" pattern by checking plan body for inline **Routing:** blocks when no sibling .routing.md exists. Would have caught Specs A-E despite their clean git history.
  3. Audit /adev:validate, /adev:review-specs, /adev:debug for any other plan-file writers — same invariant applies.

## History note

The original /adev:debug invocation that produced this diagnosis was filed in this session against issues that were subsequently lost when the shared tasks.json was rolled back externally. The diagnosis is preserved in the /adev:debug subagent transcript (agent ID affc19ea4ef7212c7) and in the retro at .context-index/hygiene/retros/2026-05-19-cursor-provider.md.

Re-filed on 2026-05-19 (consolidated from prior lost issue-525 + issue-528).

title: Resolve execution state across worktrees like the issue board already does
description:
Root cause established 2026-08-12 after two agents independently fixed the same p0 vulnerability an hour apart (PR #214 and duplicate PR #215, both for issue-582), and after a whole concurrent epic (epic-102, issues 568-581, PRs #210-#214) stayed invisible to a study pursuing the same goal. The issue board resolves storage via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs) and IS shared across worktrees. Execution state does NOT: lib/execution-state.mjs reads <projectRoot>/.context-index/.execution-state.json, which is worktree-local. Measured live: /adev:work Step 1 reported status "idle" in this worktree while four epic-102 issues were in_progress and five PRs were open. Second, behavioural half: the board DID carry the signal (issue-582 was already in_progress) and nothing re-reads an issue at the moment work begins, so stale local knowledge won over the shared record.

Smallest change with the largest effect: point lib/execution-state.mjs at resolveStorageRoot() from lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs (already written, already tested, already handles the --git-common-dir case), or scan sibling worktrees and merge. Today the state scan is blind by construction, not by accident. Decide deliberately whether execution state should be SHARED (one lease per repo) or MERGED (per-worktree records, aggregated for display) — sharing changes semantics for legitimate parallel worktree work, which /adev:implement --parallel depends on.

RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (epic-107): Closed by 36f84fd6 (resolver) + a3687935 (the two shadow-path sites it exposed: session-capture read local while the writer wrote shared; migrateExecutionState guarded local and wrote shared, so a worktree run overwrote main live state).
