title: Session Capture & Leak Prevention
encodeCwd drops dot-directories, so token-cost logging is silently inert in every .claude/worktrees worktree
description:
Found 2026-08-17 during a token retro. NOT the schema gap first suspected — token-cost-logging.spec.md (status: validated, revision 2) is correct, and its Behavior 1 specifies exactly the fields that are missing. The feature is silently DEGRADED, and the degradation is invisible because Behavior 2 makes absence legal.

ROOT CAUSE — one-line encoding mismatch.

lib/session-capture.mjs:92
  function encodeCwd(cwdReal) { return cwdReal.replace(/\//g, "-"); }

It replaces `/` with `-` only. Claude Code ALSO replaces `.` with `-` when deriving the transcripts-root segment. For a worktree cwd the two disagree:

  encodeCwd produces:  -Users-dpavancini-Development-adev-plugin-.claude-worktrees-j7pq6-context-pack-paths
  Claude Code uses:    -Users-dpavancini-Development-adev-plugin--claude-worktrees-j7pq6-context-pack-paths
                                                                ^^ ".claude" -> "-claude", so "/.claude" -> "--claude"

Verified both strings directly: the encoded candidate directory does not exist; the actual one does and holds the live transcript.

CONSEQUENCE CHAIN, all observed this session:

1. The hook resolves a transcripts path that does not exist.
2. Behavior 2 fires ("session data NOT accessible -> entry written WITHOUT usage, exit 0, no error surfaced"). Correct per spec, and SILENT by design.
3. Behavior 7's format warning never fires — this is a missing FILE, not a format change. Confirmed: .context-index/.token-cursor.json has format_warning_emitted: false.
4. The cursor sits at last_offset: 0 with every cumulative counter at 0, despite carrying the CORRECT session_id (eef96958-b24d-4d3a-99a9-81a5fd4484b7). Note last_offset 0 is not an end-of-file init per Behavior 4 — the real transcript is large.
5. .context-index/.session-tracking.jsonl entries carry only {tool, files, timestamp, session_id, operator}. No usage object on any line.
6. `adev cost summary --spec <s> --include-checkpoints` therefore reports "cost: (no usage data yet)" and exits 0.
7. The /adev:build cost ticker — which build SKILL.md instructs the orchestrator to run after every recorded step — has nothing to aggregate and prints nothing.

PROOF THE DATA WAS THERE ALL ALONG: reading the real transcript directly yields 1,224 assistant messages carrying message.usage, totalling 342,250,852 processed tokens for this session (cache_read 335,935,349 / cache_creation 5,353,678 / output 959,542 / input 2,283). Behavior 1's preconditions were satisfied in reality — only the path lookup failed.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: the encoding is correct for a plain checkout. /Users/dpavancini/Development/adev-plugin has no dot segment, so -Users-dpavancini-Development-adev-plugin resolves fine, and both project dirs exist side by side. It breaks ONLY when cwd contains a dot-directory — which is precisely every worktree under .claude/worktrees/. Since worktrees are a first-class adev workflow (EnterWorktree, `adev worktree`, and CLAUDE.md guidance all steer toward them), the most-advanced workflow is exactly the one where cost tracking dies.

FIX: make encodeCwd match Claude Code exactly — replace both `/` and `.` (/[/.]/g -> "-"), not just `/`. Add a test asserting a dot-containing cwd resolves to the real transcripts dir, using a worktree-shaped path as the fixture. Consider also emitting a ONE-TIME advisory on the not-found path naming the attempted directory: Behavior 2's silence is right for a missing-permission case, but it hid a hard bug here, and a debug-level breadcrumb would have caught this immediately.

CHECK FOR SIBLINGS while fixing: any other code deriving a Claude Code transcripts path from cwd carries the same latent defect. Verify validateTranscriptPath (lib/session-capture.mjs:101) does not share the assumption.

RELATED: adev-plugin-hl0m (P1) is adjacent but different — it is about eval suites DEPENDING on session JSONL and failing on a clean checkout (tests/evals/token-optimization/, "Real Token Analysis"). It confirms prior token-measurement work exists and would be worth re-pointing at a fixed resolver. This issue is about the production hook silently failing to WRITE usage, not about tests reading it.

BLOCKS MEASUREMENT WORK: this is the prerequisite for adev-plugin-tdd-cycle-simplification-xprl, adev-plugin-gyad, and any other cost-optimization issue — none can be measured from adev's own instrumentation while the writer is inert in worktrees.

title: Validation & Gates Unification
Governance config ships empty and nothing populates or migrates it — populate boundaries/transitions and make the checks deterministic
description:
adev's governance config ships empty, nothing populates it, and nothing migrates it. Four filed
issues are four views of that one root cause. This absorbs them.

**Reframed 2026-08-14.** This issue previously proposed *gating checks 8 and 9 off* when their
rulesets are empty. That was the wrong disposition. Boundary rules and transition gates are part of
adev's original design; the checks are not the defect, the empty config is. The fix is to populate
the config and move execution from an LLM to code.

## The evidence that reframed it

`skills/validate/checks/validate.check-8-boundaries.md` is a deterministic algorithm written as an
LLM prompt:

> Run regex `pattern` against file contents, respecting `exclude` globs.
> `severity: error` → FAIL. `severity: warning` → WARN.

That is roughly ten lines of code, dispatched to a subagent at ~95K tokens per validate run
(against implement's ~25K). It "structurally cannot fail" only because `boundaries: []` gives it
zero rules to iterate — not because the design is wrong.

## The rules already exist, in the wrong format

`boundaries.yaml` takes `{id, severity, pattern (regex), exclude (globs), description}`. This
project's `CLAUDE.md` Anti-Patterns section is already a boundary ruleset written as prose:

| CLAUDE.md rule | As a boundary rule |
|---|---|
| No CommonJS (`require`, `module.exports`) | `pattern: "\\brequire\\s*\\(\|module\\.exports"`, severity error |
| No hardcoded paths to `~/.claude/` | `pattern: "~/\\.claude/"`, exclude docs |
| No inline Node in SKILL.md | already enforced deterministically by `.githooks/pre-commit-no-inline-node` |

The inline-Node rule is the proof of concept: it was written as a git hook precisely because prose
did not bind agents. `boundaries.yaml` is where it belongs — from there it runs at plan, implement
*and* validate time, not only pre-commit.

`transitions` is ready here too. The gates template warns "populate this only after the gates it
names carry real argv commands"; this project's do — `test: [npm, test]` and
`integration-test: [npm, run, test:evals]`. So `implement-to-validate: {required_gates: [test]}` is
safe today, and hygiene Pass 8 already enforces that named gates exist.

## Scope

1. **Populate `boundaries.yaml`** from the constitution / CLAUDE.md anti-patterns. Start with the
   regex-decidable rules above.
2. **Populate `transitions`** in `gates.yaml` with the gates that already carry real argv commands.
3. **Move Checks 8 and 9 from `subagent-review` to `deterministic-check`.** A populated ruleset
   evaluated by an LLM is still ~95K tokens to run a regex. Deterministic execution also makes
   these runnable in CI and pre-commit, where subagent checks cannot go. The runner protocol,
   tiering and severity already exist in `lib/diagnostics/`.
4. **Wire `require_hitl_approval` and `approver_role`**, or delete them with `additional_gates`.
   ADR-0010 cites them; no code reads them (verified: 0 references under `lib/`).
5. ~~Uncomment the tiered gates in the shipped templates.~~ **DONE before this issue was written**
   — `unified-gates/tiered-gates-default.spec.md` is status: validated (PR #253). Templates now
   ship uncommented `test` (fast) + `integration-test` (integration) entries, and the software
   domain starter carries a real argv command on both. `adev-plugin-n8ko` was merged here in error;
   its record has been corrected. No work remains under this item.
6. **Cross-repo scope** (from `2kc5`): shared boundary rules and transition gates across repos in a
   workspace. Depends on Context Resolution (validated). Lower priority than 1-5; sequence last.

## Absorbs

- `adev-plugin-03du` (P2) — four governance config fields with zero code consumers
- `adev-plugin-n8ko` (P2) — ship tiered gates by default. **Absorbed in error: already delivered.** See scope item 5.
- `adev-plugin-2kc5` (P3) — workspace-level governance (shared boundaries/transitions)

Deliberately **not** absorbed: `adev-plugin-ogjm` (P1) — scaffolds silently lose string-command
gates and upgrade never migrates them. That is a shipped user-facing defect since adev-cli v0.25.0
with its own urgency, and it should not wait behind a config-population effort.

## Working definition of simplification (set 2026-08-14)

**Faster and more cohesive checks — even if there are more checks in quantity.** Not fewer checks.
This resolves the apparent tension between populating rulesets (more rules) and simplifying: many
cheap deterministic checks beat few expensive LLM dispatches, provided each check sits in its
ADR-0010-correct surface and declares its own applicability.

Three mechanisms, in dependency order:

1. **Skip before dispatch** (`adev-plugin-l7gu`). A check declares an applicability predicate the
   orchestrator evaluates deterministically; non-applicable checks record SKIP with a reason rather
   than PASS. This is what makes "more checks" affordable.
2. **Read once** (`adev-plugin-gyad`). Every check currently re-reads the same spec, charter and
   manifest inside its own subagent context. Measured: 11 validate dispatches at ~95K tokens vs 11
   implement dispatches at ~25K — validate costs ~3x implement while doing strictly less work.
3. **Run deterministically where the role permits** (ADR-0010 step 4: regex over changed files →
   `boundaries.yaml`; step 5: artifact invariants → `diagnostics.yaml`). A check that a regex can
   answer must never be a subagent.

Under this definition the populate-vs-simplify sequencing worry is void: `boundaries.yaml` can be
filled with as many constitution-derived regex rules as are useful, because the surface that runs
them is deterministic by role.

## Related

`.context-index/research/lean-review-validation.md` recommendations 2 and 5;
`harness-simplification-study.md` Part 2 (measured no-op table) and Phase 4.

title: Two check surfaces, three ID conventions, two composition models — unify the check and gate registries
description:
adev has two parallel check surfaces with different schemas, three registries with three ID
conventions and two opposite composition models, and a verdict vocabulary that is neither closed
nor documented. Four filed issues are four views of that. This absorbs them.

## The two surfaces (from adev-plugin-hhf6)

1. **Quality gates** (`governance/gates.yaml`) — tier-organized commands (fast | integration | e2e),
   each with kind (deterministic | probabilistic), severity, required flag, triggers (post-task |
   post-implement | pre-merge), group. Run by validate Check 1, the implement post-task hook,
   plan's context loading, and CI directly.
2. **Validation checks** (`governance/validate.yaml`) — a registry with kinds (quality-gate |
   subagent-review | deterministic-check | observational), profile, fail-fast, `after` dependencies,
   severity. Run by `/adev:validate` only.

Check 1 of validation **is** the quality-gate tier sweep — a wrapper around `gates.yaml`. Same
logic, two entry points. "What must pass before X" has no single answer: quality gates, validation
checks, or transition gates, and all three are configured differently.

## The ID scheme (from adev-plugin-paky)

Seven validate checks occupy ordinal space 1.5 to 14:

```
validate.check-1.5-source-manifest      validate.check-9-transition-gates
validate.check-2-spec-compliance        validate.check-11-visual-verification
validate.check-4-constitution           validate.check-14-gate-executability
validate.check-8-boundaries
```

Every pathology of ordinal-in-identifier naming at once: decimal interpolation (`1.5` exists to
sort between 1 and 2, though real ordering comes from the `after:` graph); gaps as tombstones
(3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, 13 — some relocated to review-specs and hygiene, some deleted, and the gaps
are the only record); a `RESURRECTED_CHECK_ID` warning that exists because the space is not
append-only, making removal unsafe; and an ordinal that carries no information about what the check
does, depends on, or costs.

At the logging boundary `adev report` takes free text, so the same check has been logged under four
spellings (`check-1.6-code-drift | drift | drift-detection | drift-warning`).

The good scheme already exists in the same directory. `diagnostics.yaml` uses namespaced semantic
IDs — `adev/event-schema-valid`, `adev/status-enum-legal`, `adev/frontmatter-present`,
`adev/validated-without-report` — extensible as `<vendor>/<aspect>`, with first-wins duplicate
handling. Validate simply predates it.

## The composition models

Three registries in `.context-index/governance/`, three semantics:

| Registry | Model | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `validate.yaml` | replace-all; no bundled defaults, no overlay merge; missing file is a hard error | `lib/governance/validate-config.mjs:74` |
| `review.yaml` | three-layer overlay: bundled → domain → project, merged by `id` | `lib/governance/review-config.mjs:53-79` |
| `diagnostics.yaml` | append, first-wins, bundled entries unshadowable | registry header |

Consequence: because validate is replace-all, a new bundled check added upstream can never reach an
existing project — the project's file is authoritative and does not know the check exists. This is
the same defect class as `adev-plugin-ogjm` for gates, unfiled for checks.

## Scope

1. One ID namespace for checks, matching `diagnostics.yaml`'s (`adev/<aspect>`), with an explicit
   alias table for relocated IDs instead of ordinal tombstones — so history is readable and removal
   is safe.
2. Enum-enforce IDs in `adev report`. Once IDs are a closed namespaced set, the enum *is* the
   registry and free-text drift becomes unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.
3. One composition model across all three registries — the overlay model, plus explicit
   `disabled: true` / `disabled_reason` so opting out is a statement in the file rather than an
   absence indistinguishable from never having seen the check.
4. Decide whether gates and checks remain two surfaces or become one, and document the answer.
   `hhf6` is filed as research; this is where its output lands.
5. Close or document the lifecycle gate verdict vocabulary (from `adev-plugin-5vnb`).

## Absorbs

- `adev-plugin-hhf6` (P2) — research: unify quality gates and validation checks under a single logic
- `adev-plugin-paky` (P2) — enum-enforce check IDs in `adev report`
- `adev-plugin-5vnb` (P2) — lifecycle gate verdict vocabulary: broaden or document
- `adev-plugin-qf2` (P1) — restructure `/adev:validate` around real-signal checks

**Caveat on `qf2`.** It carried no description — its entire scope was its title. It is folded here
because "real-signal checks" is the same restructuring seen from the outcome side, but that is an
inference from a title, not from a stated scope. If `qf2` meant something narrower or different,
this issue has silently swallowed it. Reopen it if so.

## Related

`.context-index/research/lean-review-validation.md` findings F3 and F4, recommendations 3 and 4.

title: source-manifest verifies declared files changed, never that the right files were declared
description:
`source-manifest` verifies that the files a spec DECLARED have not changed. It never verifies that the
spec declared all the files it should have. Omission passes clean, and the declaring party is the one
under review.

## Mechanism

`verifyManifest` (`lib/source-manifest.mjs:207-243`) reads `manifest.files`, hashes each listed file,
folds them into a composite SHA-256, and compares against the stored `sha`:

```js
const compositeSha = createHash("sha256")...
return { matches: currentSha === manifest.sha, currentSha };
```

The declared list is both the input and the scope. A file the spec touches but does not list is not
hashed, not compared, and not reported. `adev source-manifest verify` exits 0.

## Why it matters now

Three consumers are about to treat the manifest as ground truth:

1. **`adev-plugin-j7pq.5`** proposes a `<source-manifest>` token that expands the declared files into
   the reviewer's context pack. A pack scoped strictly to that list can be starved by omission — the
   reviewed party chooses what the reviewer sees.
2. **`adev-plugin-j7pq.3`** proposes gating on the review's `file-sha` so a passed spec re-opens the
   gate when it drifts. Drift detection over an incomplete list has the same blind spot.
3. `/adev:validate` Check 1.5 already reports PASS on manifests that may be incomplete. Observed live:
   `spec-behavior-ids` validated with `sha: 3539b26` over five files while the branch touched seven,
   the two provider mirrors having been regenerated but never added to the manifest. The agent that
   noticed called it a "declaration gap" and it was correct.

## The check

Deterministic, no LLM, and the data already exists on both sides:

- **At implement/validate time:** diff the files changed on the branch since the spec's base against
  `source-manifest.files`. Any changed file absent from the manifest is a finding.
- **At review time (weaker but cheap):** for every repo-relative path and exported symbol the spec
  names in backticks, check whether its owning file appears in the manifest. A spec that discusses
  `lib/foo.mjs` without declaring it is either under-declared or citing something out of scope.

Both are checkable from the artifacts alone. Neither needs a reviewer.

## Scope note

This is NOT "make the manifest exhaustive automatically." Auto-stamping every touched file would
paper over the signal — a spec touching files outside its charter is exactly what you want surfaced,
not silently absorbed. The check reports the discrepancy; a human or the reviewer decides whether the
file belongs in the manifest or the change belongs in a different spec.

## Where it belongs

`adev-plugin-kast` owns the diagnostics registry work and is the natural home for the runner. Sequence
behind `adev-plugin-8ekd.2`, which is open to unify the check surfaces — do not add a fifth surface
while that is in flight.

## Acceptance

- A branch that modifies a file absent from the spec's `source-manifest.files` produces a finding.
- The finding names the undeclared file and the spec that should have declared it.
- A spec with an intentionally narrow manifest can record the exclusion rather than re-triggering
  every run.
- `spec-behavior-ids` (five declared, seven touched) is the first regression fixture.

title: work-tracking eval fixture generates pre-standardization spec names, so the reverse index is always empty
description:
ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED, and it is one line in a shell script.

tests/evals/work-tracking/setup-fixture.sh generates spec files with the
PRE-STANDARDIZATION naming — `login.md`, `widgets.md` — while
lib/source-manifest.mjs:145 requires the `.spec.md` suffix:

    } else if (entry.name.endsWith(".spec.md")) {

So `buildReverseIndex` walks the fixture, matches nothing, and returns an empty
map. Every assertion built on it fails.

PROVEN, not inferred. Against the generated fixture:
  buildReverseIndex(...) -> size = 0        (test expects 3)
After copying the two specs to `.spec.md` names, with no other change:
  size = 3
  lib/login.mjs        -> .../auth/login.spec.md
  tests/login.test.mjs -> .../auth/login.spec.md
  lib/drifted.mjs      -> .../dashboard/widgets.spec.md
Exactly the three pairs the test asserts.

The fixture content is otherwise correct — it declares source-manifest.files
properly. Only the filenames are stale, left behind by the spec-suffix
standardization (epic-48, closed). The fixture is generated and gitignored-in-
effect (0 tracked files), so nothing flagged it when the suffix rule changed.

FAILURES THIS ACCOUNTS FOR — 5 of 32 when the suite runs alone:
  builds correct reverse index from fixture specs
  drifted.mjs maps back to widgets.md via reverse index
  identifies claiming spec for drifted file via reverse index
  fully traced files are not false-positived
  unclaimed file count matches expected
plus the three parent describes (Scenario B Lifecycle Bypass Detection,
Scenario C Reverse Index, Scenario F Issue Chain Tracing).

WHY IT HAD NO ISSUE UNTIL NOW: it lives in the eval tier, which `npm test`
excludes (scripts/run-tests.mjs makes the tiers disjoint). It only surfaces under
`npm run test:evals`, and when it was noticed the failures were assumed to belong
to issue-591 (integration-sandbox) or issue-592 (token-budget). They belong to
neither — this is a third, previously unattributed bucket.

FIX: update setup-fixture.sh to emit `<name>.spec.md`, and update the expected
paths in work-tracking.test.mjs to match. Worth checking whether any other
generated fixture carries the pre-standardization naming for the same reason.

title: No concurrent-write protection on shared tasks.md — cross-session writes lose data
description: lib/issues/file-adapter.mjs _write() does a plain readFileSync → mutate-in-memory → writeFileSync sequence with no locking, no atomic rename, and no version check.  Observed failure mode (2026-05-11 during 0.25.0 reconcile session): Three concurrent Claude sessions on the same project directory mutated tasks.md. The background agent (in a separate session) created epic-72 and re-parented issues 274/374 — those changes were visible briefly on disk, then completely wiped by a subsequent write from a different writer that had read an earlier version. Other concurrent changes (epic-65/66/69 closure, epic-70 milestone move, issues 456-458 creation) survived. The pattern is unpredictable last-writer-wins lost-update behavior.  Impact: every multi-session scenario (worktrees, parallel agents, user-plus-agent edits) silently loses work. Issue board state cannot be trusted under concurrent access. This is structurally severe because the issue board is the canonical source of truth for plan/issue/epic state across the lifecycle.  Possible fixes (need spec discussion): 1. File lock via proper-lockfile or fs/promises advisory flock around _read+_write critical section. 2. Atomic write via temp file + rename, plus a version/etag check (compare-and-swap) — read returns a version token; write fails if disk version != staged version, triggering a re-read-and-retry. 3. Move to JSON-with-CAS or SQLite — both give atomicity for free and unblock the json-issue-board-adapter spec (issue-457).  Fits under epic-71 (Agent-Reliable State Artifacts). Probably the highest-priority structural fix in that epic since it underpins all other state-artifact reliability work.; Closed: Validated 2026-05-17 — all 15 AC pass, npm test green, 3 commits on feat/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/concurrent-write-protection branch. CAS implementation exceeds original spec guarantee (now unconditional via O_EXCL lock-file).

title: Artifact Frontmatter & Schema Hygiene
Frontmatter preamble scan breaks on multi-line HTML comments — 129/254 specs read as {} by amend/revise/amendment-graph
description:
Discovered 2026-08-17 while routing adev-plugin-j7pq.3 through /adev:specify --amend. BLOCKS that route.

REPRODUCTION:
  adev specify amend --spec .context-index/specs/features/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/lifecycle-event-log.spec.md --descriptor review-gate-integrity --kind behavioral
  => INVALID_AMENDMENT_BASE: base spec missing/malformed revision: (got undefined)

The spec is NOT malformed. It carries revision: 4 at line 12, inside a well-formed fence at line 7.

ROOT CAUSE: three copies of an identical preamble scan skip blank lines, lines starting with #, and lines starting with <!-- , but never track an UNCLOSED comment. A multi-line HTML comment continuation line is non-blank, does not start with # and does not start with <!-- , so the loop breaks before reaching the fence and the function returns {}.

  lib/specify-amend.mjs:70     -> breaks adev specify amend
  lib/specify-revise.mjs:111   -> breaks adev specify revise (the BLOCK-to-revise loop)
  lib/amendment-graph.mjs:61   -> returns {} so no amends: relationship is seen; amendment links are silently dropped, no error

TRACE on lifecycle-event-log.spec.md:
  1: [# Live Spec: Lifecycle Event Log]            starts with # -> continue
  2: []                                            blank -> continue
  3: [<!-- Live Spec within the agent-reliable...]  starts with <!-- -> continue
  4: [     This defines a specific behavioral...]   NOT blank, NOT #, NOT <!-- -> BREAK
  7: [---]                                          never reached

BLAST RADIUS: 129 of 254 .spec.md files under .context-index/specs/ do not have --- on line 1; they open with the H1 + multi-line comment preamble. Every one is mis-read as {} by all three call sites. amendment-graph.mjs is the quietest and worst: it does not error, it just reports no amendment relationships.

Measured: find .context-index/specs -name "*.spec.md" | wc -l => 254; those whose first line is not --- => 129.

FIX: track open-comment state across lines (or reuse a single shared frontmatter parser instead of three near-duplicate copies — the copies are already labelled "mirrors lib/specify-revise.mjs" in a comment at lib/specify-amend.mjs:60). Add a regression fixture whose frontmatter sits behind a multi-line HTML comment.

NOTE: templates/spec-template.behavioral.md puts --- on line 1, so newly scaffolded specs are unaffected. This is legacy-shape only, which is why it went unnoticed.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-17 in worktree j7pq-review-gate (branch worktree-j7pq-review-gate). UNCOMMITTED.

TWO defects, not one. The second was found while fixing the first:
(a) no open-comment tracking (the reported bug);
(b) the scan capped at 10 lines, but 7 files carry a REVISION HISTORY comment pushing the fence to line 11 or 15. Comment tracking ALONE would still have missed those. Measured fence-line distribution across 254 specs: line 1 x125, 3 x54, 6 x8, 7 x47, 8 x9, 9 x1, 10 x3, 11 x6, 15 x1.

FOURTH call site found (issue body listed three): lib/cli/test-policy.mjs:120 imports parseFrontmatterFields from amendment-graph.mjs, so spec-level test_strategy / test_depth were also silently read as {} for those 129 specs and fell back to defaults with no error.

CHANGES:
- NEW lib/frontmatter.mjs — single shared reader. Tracks open-comment state; terminates at first real content; MAX_PREAMBLE_LINES=200 safety bound. Exports parseFrontmatter (rich: frontmatterText/body/fields/lines/openIdx/closeIdx) and parseFrontmatterFields (convenience).
- lib/specify-amend.mjs — deleted local copy, imports shared. Kept local FENCE (still used for WRITING frontmatter at lines ~193/204).
- lib/specify-revise.mjs — delegates to shared. NOTE: its rewriteFrontmatter depended on _lines/_openIdx/_closeIdx bookkeeping to splice the preamble through a rewrite byte-identically; the shared parser now returns lines/openIdx/closeIdx for this, and the consumer was updated. Delegating without that would have silently corrupted spec rewrites.
- lib/amendment-graph.mjs — now imports AND re-exports parseFrontmatterFields (a bare `export {x} from` creates no local binding, and the module uses it internally at line 77 — caught by its own suite). Removed its now-unused FENCE const.
- NEW tests/frontmatter.test.mjs — 11 tests: clean shape, single-line comment, multi-line comment with indented continuations, the line-15 case with `-->` on its own line, a `---` INSIDE a comment not being mistaken for the fence, plus the negative cases (real content before fence, no fence, unclosed fence, indent-0-only capture) and the frontmatterText/body split.

title: Surface domain extensions during adev init (extension picker / discovery hint)
description:
## Problem

A user installing adev into a new project sees only the bundled `software` domain. The framework has already moved non-software domains into installable extension packages (`extensions/data-engineering/`, `extensions/process-automation/`, both with validated specs PASS), and the install pipeline (`adev extension install <source>`) is fully implemented in `cli/index.mjs:956-997` and `lib/extensions/install.mjs`. But `adev init` (or the equivalent install wizard) does not mention extensions at all — there is no discovery surface telling the user that data-engineering, process-automation, or future domains are available.

Symptom: the user picks software-with-wrong-fit, or writes a custom domain from scratch (re-discovering `extends: software` + `.context-index/domains/<name>/` + `domain: <name>` in manifest.yaml), or simply does not realize extensions exist.

## Charter context

`.context-index/specs/features/domain-extensions/charter.md:29` *explicitly* lists "Auto-install during `adev init`" as out of scope for v1 of the extension work. The wording "for v1" was deliberate — that v1 was the content+pipeline; the install-UX bridge is the natural v2 follow-on. This issue is that follow-on.

## Recommended fix

Add an extension-discovery prompt to the init flow. Two implementation paths, ranked:

1. **First-party catalog with picker** *(preferred)*. After the providers prompt and before the context-index scaffold step, scan a known set of first-party extensions (start with the two that exist: `data-engineering`, `process-automation`). Present:
   ```
   Heading: Domain Extensions
   Select a domain extension to install (or skip for software-only):
     1. software (bundled) — general-purpose [default]
     2. data-engineering — pipelines, ETL, dbt, data quality
     3. process-automation — workflow automation, CI/CD orchestration
     4. skip
   ```
   On selection, call `installExtension(<path>, projectRoot, opts)` (the same function the CLI verb wraps). The first-party catalog can live as a small JSON manifest in `templates/` or embedded in `cli/index.mjs`. Multi-select also reasonable.

2. **Discovery hint only** *(minimal)*. After init completes, print a one-line note:
   ```
   Tip: To use a domain other than software, install an extension:
         adev extension install ./extensions/data-engineering
         adev extension install <git-url>
         (or browse: https://agentic-dev.org/extensions)
   ```
   No prompt, no install — just discoverability.

Option 1 fixes the UX gap; option 2 reduces it. Both close the report-symptom that prompted this issue.

## Scope

1. Decide between picker (option 1) vs hint (option 2). Picker recommended.
2. If picker: define the first-party catalog (which extensions ship as known options). Start with the two that exist in this monorepo.
3. Wire the catalog into `cli/index.mjs` init/upgrade flows.
4. Reuse `installExtension()` from `lib/extensions/install.mjs` for the actual install — no new install machinery.
5. Persist the choice in `manifest.yaml` (`domain: <name>` plus extension stamp via existing `readManifestStamps()` flow).
6. Update `skills/init/SKILL.md` to walk the user through the picker.
7. Update the install-completion message to confirm which domain extension (if any) was selected.
8. Test: integration test exercising init with each catalog choice.

## Acceptance criteria

- `adev init` surfaces available domain extensions to the user.
- User can select one (or skip) without leaving the init flow.
- Selected extension is installed via the existing `installExtension()` pipeline.
- `manifest.yaml` is stamped with the chosen domain and extension provenance.
- `adev upgrade` offers the same picker if no domain extension is installed.
- A new project where the user picks data-engineering has working `.context-index/domains/data-engineering/` after init (or whatever path the extension resolves to).
- The install-completion message shows the selected domain.

## References

- Charter (and out-of-scope note): `.context-index/specs/features/domain-extensions/charter.md:29`
- Install verb implementation: `cli/index.mjs:956-997`
- Install pipeline: `lib/extensions/install.mjs`
- Existing first-party extensions: `extensions/data-engineering/`, `extensions/process-automation/`
- Adjacent open issues: issue-447 (extract non-software domains), issue-448 (data-engineering package), issue-450 (remove from bundled templates) — those address packaging; this issue addresses discoverability/install UX, which they do not.
- Source of report: a user installing adev into a new project who only saw `software` and did not realize extensions were available.

title: A review verdict that cannot reach its requester is indistinguishable from a review that never ran
description: Observed live 2026-08-13 during epic-108 wave 2, twice, in the same session. Class: a review outcome is lost and NEITHER side sees an error. (1) Stranded verdict. A dispatched synthesized reviewer completed a re-review of hygiene-test-debt.spec.md rev 2 and returned PASS_WITH_NOTES, having verified all three round-1 blockers RESOLVED empirically against the real suite. It could not deliver that verdict to the session that requested it (SendMessage: 'no agent named general-purpose is reachable') so it returned the report one level up to the orchestrator. The requesting session, receiving nothing, reasonably concluded the review had been cancelled, wrote 'a re-review was deliberately NOT run' into the .review.md Disposition, and proceeded to implementation. The work was better-verified than its own record claimed. Recovered by hand in commit 18ee9e4b only because the orchestrator happened to be holding the report. At least three other nested agents in the same session hit the identical addressing failure (a plan review that returned Approved, a Task-1 implementation report, a spec-compliance PASS). (2) Same class, different mechanism, already fixed in ed84a277: /adev:review-specs SKILL.md emits 'adev report --type step --verdict BLOCK', which the verb rejects (PASS|PASS_WITH_NOTES|FAIL only), so the review step emitted 'started' with no terminal event. Silent because the validate gate checks 'implement', not 'review' — any later /adev:plan or /adev:review-specs on that spec would have blocked PERMANENTLY. That specific contract mismatch is issue-584; this issue is the general failure mode. Why P1: adev's entire gate model assumes a recorded verdict is a faithful record of whether review happened. Both failures break that assumption silently and in the UNSAFE direction — one loses a PASS (work looks less verified than it is, wasting effort), the other loses a BLOCK terminal (spec wedged forever). Directions worth considering: make a dispatched-review request carry a correlation id the requester polls for rather than relying on push delivery; have the report verb reject unknown verdicts LOUDLY at the call site rather than failing silently; and add a diagnostic for a lifecycle step that emitted 'started' with no terminal event within a run, which is the on-disk signature of both failures.

title: BeadsAdapter passes the .beads DIRECTORY as --db; br 0.2.22 requires the .db FILE, so every beads operation fails
description: Found 2026-08-13 attempting 'adev issues migrate --to beads --include-closed' on this repo (307 issues / 106 epics). The migration failed on the FIRST item and created nothing. REPRODUCTION: (1) br init -> creates a .beads/ DIRECTORY containing beads.db, beads.db-shm, and a .gitignore. (2) lib/issues/beads-adapter.mjs:29 sets this.dbPath = join(projectRoot, '.beads') -- the directory -- and line 54 passes it as ['--db', this.dbPath, ...args]. (3) Every br invocation then fails with: CONFIG_ERROR 'Refusing unsafe configured database leaf <database-authority sha256=...>: expected a regular file, not a symlink or special file'. VERIFIED the path is the whole cause, not the payload: 'br --db <root>/.beads create "plain test title" --type bug' fails identically to a title containing backticks and colons, while 'br --db <root>/.beads/beads.db create "migration probe title" --type bug --json' SUCCEEDS and returns a well-formed issue (id adev-plugin-ou0). MISLEADING SURFACE SYMPTOM worth noting for whoever picks this up: the migrate verb reports MIGRATE_PARTIAL_FAILURE naming the first issue it tried (here issue-582, whose title contains backticks and the word SECURITY), which reads exactly like a shell-quoting or injection bug in the title. It is not -- the adapter uses execFileSync with array args and never invokes a shell. Any title fails. Do not chase the quoting theory. LIKELY CAUSE: generational drift between bd (beads, Go) and br (beads_rust). title: milestone ship gates_pass auto-check broken — reads deprecated manifest.gates.test AND fails when populated
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-19 while running /adev:issues milestone ship 0.27.0. Two related defects in lib/milestones.mjs::evaluateShipCriteria (the gates_pass auto-check branch):

1. CONFIG-LAYOUT DRIFT: the check reads `manifest.gates.test` directly. The post-0.26.0 layout moved gate definitions to .context-index/governance/gates.yaml (see manifest.yaml line 123: 'The legacy top-level gates: block here is no longer read'). evaluateShipCriteria was not updated when the move landed. Reproduces with any milestone whose manifest follows the new layout — gates_pass fails with detail: 'No test command configured in manifest.gates.test' even when governance/gates.yaml correctly defines the test gate.

2. EXECUTION FAILURE WHEN POPULATED: workaround was to re-add `gates.test: "npm test"` to manifest.yaml. After that, gates_pass STILL fails with `passed: false, detail: ""` (empty stderr). The check uses `execFileSync("npm", ["test"], { stdio: "pipe" })`. Manual `npm test` from same shell returns 0 (3426/0/0 green), so the failure path is in evaluateShipCriteria's invocation — possibly buffer overflow on large stdout, PATH resolution under execFileSync, or signal-handling difference.

Blocks: /adev:issues milestone ship for any milestone using release-please/tag-only strategy with a real test suite. Workaround: `manual` strategy bypasses gates_pass (and skips release-please integration entirely).

Fix scope: (a) read `governance/gates.yaml` via the unified loader, OR (b) keep manifest.gates.test as the source but fix the execFileSync invocation. (a) is the right long-term fix per the post-0.26.0 architecture; (b) is the minimal patch.

Affects: lib/milestones.mjs::evaluateShipCriteria (gates_pass branch); skills/issues/SKILL.md milestone-ship documentation.

Reproducing the old branch found three failures, one worse than the reported crash: gates:{test:"a && b"} returned passed:true HAVING RUN ONLY the first command — a naive split(/\s+/) producing a FALSE PASS, so a milestone could ship on a gate that never fully ran. Gates now resolve through .context-index/governance/gates.yaml + mergeGates like every other consumer, and execute as argv via execFileSync with shell:false. Severity per the gates.yaml header; error-severity blocks the ship, warning-severity does not. Tests 104 -> 118 including two real-subprocess tests proving shell metacharacters stay literal. title: Lifecycle reducer silently drops code_drift_detected / code_drift_cleared / spec_amended into unknownEvents
description:
Drift IS detected and IS written to the event log, but the canonical projection
throws it away — so every consumer reading currentState() is blind to drift the
system successfully recorded.

MECHANISM
  - CANONICAL_EVENTS (exported from lib/lifecycle-events.mjs) DOES include
    code_drift_detected and code_drift_cleared, so appendEvent's gate at
    lib/lifecycle-state.mjs:1444 accepts them and they land in the JSONL.
  - The reducer switch at lib/lifecycle-state.mjs:1449 has NO CASE for either.
    They fall through to the default at :1564 and are bucketed into
    unknownEvents. Same for spec_amended.

VERIFIED ON MAIN, not just the working tree — lib/lifecycle-state.mjs currently
carries uncommitted edits from concurrent work, so this was checked against the
committed file. A grep for a code_drift_detected case in the reducer on main
returns 0; the same grep over lib/lifecycle-events.mjs returns 1. An event the
writer accepts as canonical and the reducer treats as unknown is a contract
split inside one module.

LIVE INSTANCE: .context-index/lifecycle-state/graduated-rigor-tiers.jsonl records
a code_drift_detected event against skills/work/SKILL.md dated 2026-08-13.
currentState() on that spec reports only the specify step — the drift is
invisible in the projection skills actually consume.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE OBVIOUS: this is the mechanism behind the "only one
direction of drift is detected" complaint in issue-c9j36w. Both directions ARE
detected; one is dropped on the way out. Fixing the reducer may make the
proposed hygiene rule unnecessary.

Found by a read-only investigation agent while checking whether issue-c9j36w was
already resolved; independently re-verified against main before filing.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause was not an oversight but a HALF-EXECUTED migration: jsonl-drift-events.spec.md Migration Step 0 required both canonical registration AND a documented variant row, and named the omission as the CON-4 blocker. The discriminators reached CANONICAL_EVENTS so appendEvent accepted them, but no reducer case and no spec row were ever written. Reducer now projects state.drift ({source, at, ts} | null, last-wins on detected, reset on cleared per Behavior 5, deliberately not an accumulating list because rev 3 rescinded multi-source history) and state.specAmendments[] (accumulating, mirroring specRevisions). status/currentStep untouched — both concerns are advisory, and a test asserts requireGate is byte-identical with and without drift. state.drift is documented as NOT authoritative for is-this-drifted, since the legacy fallback means a pre-migration spec can be drifted with zero events; frontmatter stays authoritative. Verified on the live graduated-rigor-tiers fixture: drift now projects, unknownEvents 0, status/currentStep unchanged. Tests 84 -> 95, 207/207 across nine lifecycle-adjacent suites. The recurrence guard is the strongest part: a test writes one bare line per CANONICAL_EVENTS member and asserts unknownEvents is empty, so any future canonical event without a reducer case fails immediately. Spec debt closed in the same change.

title: Issue-board ID allocation is not safe across git branches — two sessions minted the same issue-589
description:
Reproduced 2026-08-13. lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs derives new IDs via _nextIssueId(issues) — max(existing)+1 against the CURRENT FILE. _withCas protects concurrent writers of one file, and resolveStorageRoot() makes the board shared across worktrees, but nothing protects allocation across git BRANCHES: a session on chore/board-sync-epic-106 minted issue-589 (infra-gated suites decision, epic-105) while a session on main minted issue-589 (regression rubrics, epic-108) from the same 588 baseline. Both were valid locally; the collision only surfaced at merge time. Same hazard for epics (branch took 105-107 while main later referenced an epic-108 that exists on no board).

RESOLVED THIS INSTANCE by renumbering the branch-side entry to issue-612 during the merge (see the board-merge PR), but the mechanism will re-collide the next time board writes live on an unmerged branch.

OPTIONS: (a) make IDs merge-safe (monotonic clock/random suffix, or a per-session prefix) — breaks the human-friendly issue-N convention; (b) keep sequential IDs but add an `adev issues renumber --against <ref>` verb that detects and re-mints collisions at merge time, plus a CI check that fails a PR whose board adds IDs already present on the base branch; (c) policy: board writes only ever land on main via short-lived PRs, never accumulate on long-lived branches (the practice that failed here — this branch carried 26 entries).

Recommend (b)+(c): tooling to make the collision detectable and a policy to keep the window small. (a) is the only true fix but costs the readable IDs the whole framework quotes in prose, commits, and specs.

title: Dynamic workflow orchestration for adev skills
description:
Evaluate and (if validated) adopt Claude Code **dynamic workflows** (the `Workflow` tool) as an opt-in orchestration substrate for fan-out-heavy adev skills.

## Why

adev already has both halves the Workflow tool assumes: deterministic CLI verbs that emit JSON, and skills that fan out subagents by prose. Several skills (`/adev:hygiene`, `/adev:review-specs`, `/adev:research`, `/adev:codehealth`) run large read-only fan-outs inside a single degrading context, and parse subagent findings back out of prose.

## Integration seam

Workflow **scripts** are plain JS with no filesystem, no network, and no Node API — they can only spawn agents, loop, and return data (verified, see the spike). That constraint dictates the shape:

```
skill (main loop)  →  adev <verb> --json      (deterministic; reads files, writes state)
                   →  Workflow({name, args})  (fan-out only; returns structured findings)
                   →  adev gate / state write (back in the main loop)
```

The script never calls `adev` directly — it receives a work-list via `args`. This maps onto the cli-driver-surface charter: the skill *names* a workflow, the logic lives in a file. Scripts live in `.claude/workflows/*.mjs`, keeping CLAUDE.md's "no executable logic inside SKILL.md" intact.

Opt-in is not a blocker: "the user invoked a skill whose instructions tell you to call Workflow" is a sanctioned trigger.

## Constraints — verified by spike adev-plugin-wf-research-71qn

- **Gates cannot live inside a workflow.** Confirmed empirically: workflow subagents have no `AskUserQuestion` tool, and workflows launch background-only. A gate needing approval physically cannot prompt from inside. Gates bracket the call.
- **Workflow subagents have no `Agent` tool.** They cannot dispatch further subagents. Any nested fan-out must be expressed in the script, not by an agent. This is the hard blocker for `/adev:implement`, whose whole shape is an orchestrator dispatching implementer → spec reviewer → code-quality reviewer per task.
- **Subagents CAN write files** (`Write`/`Edit` present). "Nothing inside the workflow writes state" is a discipline enforced by prompt wording, not by the substrate — parallel agents can race, and adev must guard this itself.
- **Skill extensions DO load** inside workflow subagents (`adev skill-ext load` → exit 0). The universal-skill-extensions contract survives this path.
- **Claims acquire/release in the main loop.** An aborted workflow cannot release a lease.
- **Portability.** Workflow is Claude Code-only. `providers/{codex,cursor,copilot,opencode}` mirrors need a serial fallback — the workflow path can never become the only path.
- **Fan-out is not cheap.** ~44k subagent tokens per trivial agent measured. Any adoption must be justified against that floor.
- **Resume overlap.** `resumeFromRunId` duplicates part of `/adev:recover` + execution-state; risk of two competing sources of truth. Still open.

## Explicit non-goals

- **`/adev:implement --parallel`.** Beyond the worktree-ownership question (adev owns worktrees via `adev worktree` with claim leases and `adev parallel verify`, and skills/implement/SKILL.md:472 forbids harness `isolation: "worktree"`), the missing `Agent` tool means implement's per-task review chain cannot be expressed inside a workflow agent at all. Needs its own design issue if ever pursued.
- **Shipping workflows via `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.** No workflow slot exists in the plugin format today.

## Scope

Prototype on `/adev:hygiene` first (read-only, no state-write races, no gate inside the loop), measure, then decide whether to generalize.

The EMPTY_ASSERTIONS detector in lib/test-strategies/gaming.mjs produces false
positives that BLOCK legitimate edits. It runs as a PreToolUse hard-blocking hook
(hooks/gaming-gate.sh, registered on the Write|Edit matcher), so a false positive
is not advisory — it stops the edit.

Hit live 2026-08-14 editing tests/cli/install-session-capture.test.mjs:

  BLOCKED: this edit introduces a new gaming violation
  {"patternId":"EMPTY_ASSERTIONS","line":551,"match":"it (",
   "message":"Test block contains no assertion calls"}

TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS, both confirmed by bisecting against the real detector.

DEFECT 1 — `it (` is matched inside COMMENTS.
Line 551 of that file is prose: "...so symlink the plugin's lib/ in and exclude it
(+ the post-commit-mode manifest) from `git add -A`." The substring "exclude it (" is
read as an it(...) test-block opener. Nothing strips comments before matching.

DEFECT 2 — brace counting is NOT STRING-AWARE.
An unbalanced `{` inside a string literal shifts every subsequent block boundary, so
the phantom block from defect 1 closes before reaching any assertion and is reported
as empty.

MEASURED, four variants of the same edit against detectSharedGamingPatterns():
  assertion string "(async()=>{ const fs = await import('node:fs')"   -> 1 violation
  same, plus a second assertion                                        -> 1 violation
  assertion string with NO brace: "const fs = await import('node:fs')" -> 0 violations
  assertion string with BALANCED braces: "(async()=>{ ... }"           -> 0 violations
The unmodified file scores 0. So the trigger is precisely an unbalanced brace inside
a string literal, landing after a comment that contains "it (".

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL FALSE POSITIVE. This detector exists to stop
agents from weakening tests. When it fires wrongly on a legitimate edit, the cheapest
path available to an agent is to reword the assertion until the gate goes quiet —
which is indistinguishable from the gaming it is meant to prevent, and trains exactly
the bypass habit issue-610 warns about for claim leases. A blocking gate with
false positives is worse than an advisory one.

DISCLOSURE: the immediate edit was landed using the brace-free assertion variant.
That is not a weakening — "const fs = await import('node:fs')" proves the payload
flowed through as literal data exactly as the original did — but it IS shaped by the
detector bug rather than by the test's needs, and that is recorded in a comment at
the site so the next reader knows why the fragment is written that way.

FIX: strip comments and string literals before pattern-matching and before brace
counting. A tokenizer-lite pass would close both defects at once. Add the two
variants above as regression fixtures.

ADJACENT, worth checking while in here: the same non-string-aware scanning likely
affects the other SHARED_PATTERNS in that module, since they share the block-boundary
machinery.
close_reason:
Fixed on main by PR #267 (merged 2026-08-14). lib/test-strategies/gaming.mjs now blanks out comments, string literals, template literals and regex literals before pattern matching, and EMPTY_ASSERTIONS scans the mask rather than the raw source.

Verified against the issue's own live repro — the comment prose 'exclude it (+ the post-commit-mode manifest)' that blocked an edit to tests/cli/install-session-capture.test.mjs on 2026-08-14. Running the real detector (SHARED_PATTERNS EMPTY_ASSERTIONS.detect) over that exact line on merged main returns [] — zero hits. tests/lib/test-strategies/gaming.test.mjs: 46 tests, 46 pass.

Closed after a post-merge board audit, verified against merged code rather than the PR description.

title: Document worker-vs-orchestrator fork pattern in skill frontmatter
description:
## Background
The single most important architectural pattern in adev — coordinator/orchestrator skills must NOT fork; worker skills SHOULD fork — is currently undocumented in any skill frontmatter and in using-adev. This caused ~50K tokens + several round-trips of wasted debugging during the 2026-05-15 lifecycle-artifacts charter build before commit f635b6a removed `context: fork` from `skills/build/SKILL.md`.

## The pattern
When invoked via the Skill tool, a skill with `context: fork` in its frontmatter runs in a forked subagent execution context that does NOT inherit the Agent dispatcher tool. This is correct behavior for WORKERS (which are themselves dispatched by an orchestrator via Agent and run in a clean subagent context with its own tool list). It is INCORRECT for ORCHESTRATORS like /adev:build, which need Agent to dispatch their pipeline steps.

## Current state (verified post-fix)
| Skill | Role | context: fork | Correct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| skills/build | orchestrator | removed (f635b6a) | yes |
| skills/implement | worker | present | yes |
| skills/deploy | worker | present | yes |
| skills/research | worker | present | yes |

## Proposed scope
1. Add an explanatory comment to each affected SKILL.md frontmatter declaring its role:
   - build: `# role: orchestrator — must NOT use context: fork (needs Agent dispatcher)`
   - implement/deploy/research: `# role: worker — context: fork is required for context isolation when dispatched by an orchestrator`
2. Add a section to skills/using-adev/SKILL.md documenting the pattern with examples and the failure mode it prevents.
3. Optionally add an integration test that asserts orchestrator skills do NOT carry `context: fork` and worker skills DO carry it.

## Reference
See .context-index/hygiene/retros/2026-05-15-lifecycle-artifacts-build.md action item #8 and the f635b6a commit message for full context.

title: Gate-command repair never reaches plugin-cache upgrades: projects silently run zero quality gates
description:
Reported from: `agentic-migration-template`, adev `0.27.9` -> `0.28.0-next.2`
Component: `cli/index.mjs::migrateLegacyGateCommands`, `lib/domains/merge-gates.mjs`
Severity: High — a project silently runs zero quality gates, and the state is
indistinguishable from all gates passing.

## Summary

adev already ships the correct fix for legacy shell-string gate commands. It is
well written, carefully scoped, and its own docstring names this exact failure
mode. It is unreachable through the upgrade path this project actually took.

`migrateLegacyGateCommands()` is invoked once, from `cmdUpgrade`. A plugin-cache
upgrade — the normal way a Claude Code plugin moves versions — never calls it.
So the repair shipped and the broken projects stayed broken.

## Evidence

### The repair exists and is correct

`lib/migrate-gate-commands.mjs`:

> WHY THIS EXISTS. `lib/domains/merge-gates.mjs` rejects any gate whose
> `command` is a string ... That requirement first shipped in adev-cli v0.25.0.
> Every `governance/gates.yaml` authored before it declares
> `command: "npm test"` and is DROPPED AT LOAD with an INVALID_GATE warning.
> Nothing migrated those files. `cmdInstall`/`cmdUpgrade` scaffold templates
> with `if (!existsSync(destPath))`, so an existing gates.yaml is skipped
> entirely — the file that needs fixing is precisely the file the installer
> refuses to touch. The result is a project whose quality gates silently
> evaluate zero gates, which reads identically to a project that passed them.

Its scoping is right too: only unambiguous commands are rewritten; anything with
`&&`, `|`, `>`, `;`, `$`, backticks or quotes is reported as UNSAFE and left alone.

### It is reachable from exactly one place

    cli/index.mjs:1074   async function migrateLegacyGateCommands() {   <- defined
    cli/index.mjs:1290   await migrateLegacyGateCommands();             <- only call site, inside cmdUpgrade

`cmdInstall` does not call it. Nothing else calls it.

### The upgrade path that actually happened does not go through cmdUpgrade

This project's plugin moved `0.27.9` -> `0.28.0-next.1` -> `0.28.0-next.2` via
the Claude Code plugin cache. Two independent confirmations that `adev upgrade`
never ran in the project:

1. `manifest.yaml` still read `adev_version: "0.27.9"` while the plugin on disk
   was `0.28.0-next.1` — nothing had reconciled them.
2. The `process-automation` extension's `source_uri` still pointed at
   `.../adev/0.27.9-next/extensions/process-automation`, a directory that no
   longer existed. It pointed at a second dead path (`next.1`) after the next.2
   bump, so this recurs on every plugin upgrade.

### The observed result

Five gates — the entire Python suite, board unit tests, typecheck, and the
SQLite dialect parity check — were declared in `governance/gates.yaml` and
dropped at load. `adev gate doctor` reported:

> `gate-doctor/gate-set-divergence`: The raw gate set and the domain-merged gate
> set disagree — declared in `.context-index/governance/gates.yaml` but absent
> from the merged set every consumer reads: python-tests, board-unit-tests,
> board-typecheck, board-lint, sqlite-dialect-parity.

The file was generated by adev itself. `gates.yaml` header, commit `c662168`:
"Generated by /adev:init --brownfield, seeded from the constitution's Quality
Gates." The constitution lists those commands in a bash block, so init copied
shell strings into `command:`. adev produced a file its own loader rejects, then
later gained a repair that never ran.

## Why this is worse than an ordinary regression

The failure is shaped like success.

- A dropped gate cannot fail, so every lifecycle step consulting the gates gets
  back "no failures." Absence of a red light reads as a green one.
- `gates.yaml` still looks right to a human. Five gates, sensible commands, a
  file named governance.
- `INVALID_GATE` is a warning inside a library. It is collected into a returned
  `warnings` array (`merge-gates.mjs:104`) and surfaced only by consumers that
  choose to print it.

The only thing that reports it is `adev gate doctor`, which a user runs when they
already suspect something. Nothing in the normal `/adev:implement` or
`/adev:validate` path says a word.

## Suggested fixes, in order of value

1. **Do not gate the repair on `cmdUpgrade`.** A plugin-cache version bump is the
   common upgrade path and never calls it. Options:
   - run the migration lazily on first gate load when a version-skew is detected;
   - run it from `/adev:init`'s diagnostic mode, which is what a user does run
     after an upgrade;
   - detect skew between `manifest.project.adev_version` and the running plugin
     version and prompt.
2. **Make a dropped gate loud.** A governance file that fails to load should not
   degrade to silence. At minimum, any consumer that receives a non-empty
   `warnings` array containing `INVALID_GATE` should surface it on stderr.
   Better: refuse to report a gate tier as passing when the merged set is empty
   but the raw file declares gates — that specific divergence is already computed
   by `gate-doctor/gate-set-divergence`, so the detection logic exists and simply
   is not consulted on the hot path.
3. **Close the version-skew loop generally.** The same root cause left the
   extension `source_uri` pointing at a deleted plugin root twice in one session.
   Whatever reconciles `adev_version` should also re-resolve extension sources.
4. **Consider having `/adev:init` diagnostic mode check gate liveness**, not just
   gate presence. It currently reports the context index as healthy while every
   gate in it is inert.
