title: Reviewer panel and specify examples are templated for a web SaaS, not this artifact class
description:
Both ends of the spec pipeline are templated for a web SaaS this project is not. `/adev:specify`
guides authors toward web-shaped specs, and the reviewer panel is scoped to review web-shaped
concerns. Fixing only the reviewers leaves half the mismatch in place, so this is one issue.

## The authoring end

`skills/specify/SKILL.md` Step 4 — the ~30 lines governing every section that produces findings:

- Error-case guidance, verbatim: *"Any additional error cases? I have: lacks permission -> 403,
  column not found -> 404, conflict -> 409"*
- Behavior examples: *"When a user drags a card to a new position within the same column then the
  card's `position` updates and affected cards reindex."*

HTTP status codes and Kanban drag-and-drop, in the authoring skill for a zero-dependency Node CLI
plugin. Also: the quality bar is aspiration with no check — *"aim for 3-8 directly testable behavior
statements"*, *"concrete, checkable criteria"* — and nothing asks, per behavior, "how would an
implementer determine this?" That question is what `unverifiable-criterion` and
`undefined-determination` findings exist to catch after the fact.

## The review end

`security-reviewer-prompt.md` scope: authentication, authorization on endpoints, PII in responses,
SQL/NoSQL injection, file uploads, rate limiting, OWASP. Its opening line is *"You review the design,
not the code."*

Observed consequence: a reviewer warned that a field "becomes an injection surface if interpolated
into dynamic dispatch (`loadResumeParser(...)`)" — a function that has never existed anywhere in the
repo. The prompt asks for injection surfaces, none of the named kind exist, so it invented one. That
is a correctly-executing reviewer against an off-domain scope.

## The scope that actually fits

23 security-shaped issues on this board, including TWO p0 command injections
(`hookspath-command-injection-zvwj` — `core.hooksPath` interpolated unescaped into a generated,
committed git-hook wrapper; `jic` — post-commit hook interpolating the `Spec:` trailer into
`node -e`), two open symlink-containment escapes (`tjth`, `jukh`), and extension governance path
escape / forged provenance (`xg1f.1`, `xg1f.2`, both now shipped).

**Zero of those 23 match any of the six OWASP scopes. All of them match:** path containment / symlink
escape, subprocess and interpolation, input trust, privilege posture, leakage into committed
artifacts, destructive fs.

## Change

Panel (data change; the domain seam at `adev domain load-reviewers` -> `mergeReviewers` already
works end to end):

| id | dispatch | scope |
|---|---|---|
| `referent-integrity` | always | Enumerate every referent the spec names and state where each was verified |
| `wiring-reviewer` | always | PRODUCER / CONSUMER / TRIGGER / TEST per thing introduced; "no caller" and "write-only state" are blockers |
| `consistency-analyzer` | always | Rewritten with this corpus's real drift axes; absorbs structural-architect's two live scopes |
| `boundary-reviewer` | **always** | The scope above, delivered as data from a threat model |
| `termination-reviewer` | triggered | Loops need a cap + cap-trip verdict + unattended default |

`boundary-reviewer` is `always`, NOT triggered — security coverage must not decrease, and the
threat-model data file ships WITH the panel, not in a cuttable tail. A reviewer whose prompt says
"no threat model delivered -> emit one warning and stop" would silently disable security review if
its data file were deferred. Seed the threat model from the shipped `lib/extensions/` boundary
contract (`governance-registry.mjs`, `governance-splice.mjs`, `governance-values.mjs`,
`exec-consent.mjs`, `exec-payload.mjs`).

`structural-architect` and `security-reviewer` leave the software panel but their prompt FILES stay
on disk — `scripts/sync-provider-skills.mjs` copies but never prunes, and `validateReviewer` aborts
`loadReviewConfig` on an unresolvable `prompt`, so deleting them breaks consumer overrides. The OWASP
prompt moves intact to a `web-service` domain so consumer web apps still get it.

Prompts, all four:
- Delete the hand-computed `blocker_id` instruction. Reviewers run `execute: deny` and cannot compute
  SHA-256, so every emitted id is typed hex; `buildBlockerId` has zero production callers. Use the
  existing `adev heuristics signature --origin review-specs --blocker-id <id>` rather than adding a
  sixth copy of "derive a stable id by hashing something" (see `failure-signature-key.spec.md`).
- Replace "you review the design, not the code."
- Fix `consistency-analyzer-prompt.md`'s `## Input` list once the pack actually delivers it.

## Depends on

The empty-context-pack issue. A fitted reviewer with an empty pack is still guessing — sequence
after it.

## Falsification, stated before running

Declare ONE reviewer (`referent-integrity`) in this repo's `.context-index/governance/review.yaml`
with a hand-written pack — no plugin change needed, `mergeReviewers` honours governance-over-domain
on matching `id`. Re-run `/adev:review-specs` against the five specs whose defects are closed and
root causes known: `he2`, `r5sc`, `zx5`, `rftq`, `ysqd`.

**Fewer than 3 of 5 flagged as blocker with a resolving citation ⇒ the panel thesis is wrong** — the
reviewers were failing on reachability, not scope, and the effort belongs in context delivery instead.

## Human approval

Dropping `structural-architect` / `security-reviewer` from the default panel changes what
`/adev:review-specs` does on every consumer repo. Note also that if
`explicit-governance-registries.spec.md` (in flight on `adev/governance-checks-unbundle`) lands first,
`review.yaml` becomes explicit single-source with `enabled: true|false` per entry — under that model
this becomes `enabled: false` with a reason rather than entry deletion, which is the better mechanism.
New bundled reviewers would then reach existing projects only via the hygiene drift pass, opt-in.

## Context pack must deliver CODE, not only documents (added after j7pq.4 shipped)

`j7pq.4` populated the packs, but every glob in `templates/review-specs/defaults.yaml` resolves under
`.context-index/`. The only tokens are `<target-spec>` and `<charter-dir>`, both pointing into the
context tree. **No source code reaches any reviewer.** So the defect classes this panel exists to
catch remain unreachable by pack: "does `buildBlockerId` exist", "who calls
`lib/loop-convergence.mjs`", and the fabricated `loadResumeParser` injection surface.

**AC-A. A `<source-manifest>` token expands the spec's declared source files into the pack.**
`source-manifest.files` is present in 211 of 247 specs and is an explicit, bounded, already-authored
list of the source files each spec governs — the natural third token alongside `<charter-dir>` and
`<target-spec>`. Do NOT glob `lib/`: the consistency pack already sits at 246,798 B against a
262,144 B cap, so whole-file source inclusion overflows immediately. Prefer the generated surface
extract (exported symbols, CLI verbs, flags, event fields) for existence questions, and the declared
files themselves only where the spec's claims concern their content.

**AC-B. A greenfield spec renders an explicit empty state, not silence.**
A spec describing code that does not exist yet has an empty source manifest. That is correct, not a
failure — but the pack must say so ("greenfield: no existing source declared") rather than render
nothing. Silent-nothing is the exact failure mode `CONTEXT_PACK_NO_TARGET` was added to prevent.

**Trust boundary — the manifest is a starting point, not a fence.** `verifyManifest`
(`lib/source-manifest.mjs:207-243`) computes a composite SHA-256 over the files it LISTS and compares
it to the stored `sha`. It answers "have the declared files changed", never "were all the right files
declared". Omission verifies clean, and the author is the party under review. So `wiring-reviewer`
must retain Glob/Grep and reach past the manifest — a pack scoped strictly to declared files can be
starved by omission. The declared-vs-actual gap is tracked separately.

title: Context packs inline whole file bodies and lose 29-71% of matched files to the byte cap — send a path manifest instead
description:
Measured 2026-08-17 against .context-index/specs/features/agent-reliable-state-artifacts/lifecycle-event-log-rev-5-review-gate-integrity.spec.md, immediately after assigning the per-reviewer packs (architecture / security / consistency) that PR #279 shipped. renderPack eagerly inlines every matched file body, hits max_total_bytes (262144), and drops the tail.

MEASURED OMISSIONS (the truncation notice names them, so this is disclosed, not silent):
  architecture  250400 bytes  10 of 34 files omitted  (29%)
  security      250484 bytes  12 of 36 files omitted  (33%)
  consistency   261180 bytes  49 of 69 files omitted  (71%)

THREE DISTINCT DEFECTS.

1. EAGER INLINING WASTES THE BUDGET ON FILES NOBODY ASKED FOR. Includes are rendered in declaration order, so review-base (charter.md + <charter-dir>/*.spec.md — 13 sibling specs here) consumes the budget before the pack own distinguishing includes are reached. Every ADR from 0009 onward is dropped from BOTH architecture and security: 0009-lifecycle-artifact-taxonomy, 0010, 0011, 0012, 0014, 0015, 0016, 0017, 0018, 0019. Reviewers see only ADRs 0001-0008 plus .template.md. ADR-0009 is the one the spec under review explicitly reasons about ("no CANONICAL_EVENTS variant is added, so the ADR-0009 [BOUNDARY: human-approved] line is not crossed") — the reviewer cannot check that claim. Separately the target base spec is inlined truncated at max_file_bytes: "[adev: truncated 16384 of 41330 bytes]" — 60% of the base contract missing.

2. THE SECURITY PACK LOSES EXACTLY ITS TWO DIFFERENTIATING INCLUDES. security is defined as review-base + ADRs + governance/risk-policies.yaml + governance/gates.yaml. Both governance files land at the very end of the include order and are both omitted. Net result: security delivers 24 files / 250484 bytes and architecture delivers 24 files / 250400 bytes — functionally THE SAME PACK. The per-reviewer differentiation PR #279 shipped is nullified by the cap for any charter with a non-trivial sibling-spec count. This is why the divergence went unnoticed: adopting the per-reviewer packs changes almost nothing observable until the budget is also fixed.

3. THE CONSISTENCY GLOB SWEEPS LIFECYCLE SIDECARS. `.context-index/specs/cross-cutting/*.md` matches .blockers.md, .plan.md, .review.md and .validate.md alongside .spec.md — roughly 5 files per spec where 1 is wanted. That inflates ~14 cross-cutting specs into 69 matched files and is the direct cause of the 71% omission rate. Omitted includes graduated-rigor-tiers.spec.md, which the spec under review cites as its justification for scoping out one of its acceptance criteria. The glob should be *.spec.md (an independent one-line fix, worth doing regardless of the rest).

PROPOSED FIX — SEND A PATH MANIFEST, NOT BODIES. Reviewer profiles are already resolved read-only-compatible (no filesystem-write / shell categories, fs execute deny, network deny or read-only), so a reviewer can read what it needs. Deliver a manifest of resolved relative paths grouped by include title, and let the reviewer read on demand. Benefits: no cap, no omission, full untruncated sources (the reviewer reads all 41330 bytes of the base spec, not a 16KB prefix), a far smaller prompt, and the reviewer pulls only what is relevant to its lens.

CRITICAL CAVEAT — THE PACK IS DOING TWO JOBS AND ONLY ONE IS A BUDGET PROBLEM. Today the pack is also the SECURITY BOUNDARY:
  (a) the hard denylist (.env*, *.pem, *.key, id_*, profiles.yaml, **/secrets/**) is enforced at both glob-string and resolved-path layers, and matching globs FAIL LOAD rather than warn;
  (b) inlined content is wrapped in nonce-scoped <<<ADEV-PACK-<nonce>>>> fences, with literal fence tokens in file bodies neutralized (lib/governance/dispatch-shape.mjs:107), so a reviewer can distinguish repository content from text the artifact under review merely CLAIMS is a delimiter.
Switching to paths solves the budget and silently regresses (a): a reviewer handed paths can read .env itself unless denylist enforcement MOVES into the profile filesystem read policy. Do not ship the manifest without moving it. It also weakens reproducibility — an inlined pack is a fixed, auditable input, whereas free reads make a review non-deterministic; the dispatch record should capture which paths were actually read.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE (hybrid): keep inlining the TARGET SPEC only, fenced, because it must be exact and it is the untrusted artifact under review. Everything else becomes a path manifest with the denylist applied to the manifest itself so denied files are never even named. Enforce the denylist in the profile fs read policy. Keep max_total_bytes as a backstop for the inlined portion only.

RELATED: adev-plugin-j7pq.4 (closed — shipped the packs whose budget behaviour this issue addresses; its acceptance criterion 4 "bounded with an explicit truncation marker" IS satisfied, the notice names every omitted file), adev-plugin-j7pq.5 (reviewer prompts promise input they do not receive — defect 2 above is a concrete instance), adev-plugin-8ekd.3 (declared-vs-actual gap).

title: Path-manifest packs: fence-header attribute escaping, LF-in-path denylist evasion, target-spec inlining ownership, and unenforceable manifest caps
description:
DEFERRED FOLLOW-UP to adev-plugin-j7pq.6. These are the four substantive blockers from round 2 of the rev-5 amendment review that were NOT fixed before the operator approved the review to unblock the build on 2026-08-17. They are real findings from a full-tier three-specialist review, verified against source by the reviewers. They must be resolved before the path-manifest delivery model is considered complete.

Spec: .context-index/specs/features/review/configurable-reviewers-rev-5-path-manifest-context-packs.spec.md (revision 2, target-revision 5)
Sidecar at time of deferral: <spec-stem>.blockers.md, 5 entries. The fifth (consistency-analyzer:contract:0e9ae87e) WAS fixed — a one-line 22k row contradiction — leaving these four.

=== 1. security-reviewer:input-validation:f37df0ec @ behaviors-14 ===
BEH-14 scopes fence-token neutralization to section BODIES. BEH-10 introduces a NEW channel it does not cover: the `title=` fence-header attribute, whose value falls back to the include glob string and can contain a `<charter-dir>` expansion.
Source evidence: `fenceBlock` neutralizes only `body`; `attrs` is interpolated UNESCAPED at every call site.
Attack: a quote, a `>>>`, or a CR/LF in a directory name forges lines INSIDE a fence that the 22j provenance preamble declares repository-sourced — i.e. the exact trust boundary the nonce scheme exists to protect.
Fix direction: neutralize (or strictly allowlist) every attribute value, not just bodies. Consider a shared escaper applied at the fenceBlock boundary so no future call site can forget.

=== 2. security-reviewer:data-exposure:c6aabd22 @ behaviors-11 ===
BEH-11 asserts "a denied path is never named in the manifest". NOT ENTAILED.
LF is a legal character in a POSIX path component and passes `neutralizeFenceTokens` untouched. The denylist regexes anchor on `(^|/)`. So a file literally named `a.spec.md\n.env` is ADMITTED by the denylist and then renders as TWO lines in the one-path-per-line manifest format, the second being a bare `.env` — which BEH-7 explicitly instructs the reviewer to read.
This is a denylist bypass that produces a secret-read instruction. Note it is only reachable by an author who can create such a filename, but that is precisely the actor the fencing scheme distrusts.
Fix direction: reject or escape control characters (at minimum CR/LF) in any path entering the manifest, and/or move off a newline-delimited format so a path cannot span lines.

=== 3. structural-architect:ownership-ambiguity:0111fab5 @ behavioral-delta-beh-10 ===
Ownership of target-spec inlining is unassigned, and the spec may be legislating over machinery it has not mapped.
Source evidence: `lib/governance/dispatch-shape.mjs:98-103` ALREADY builds `specBlock` separately, and `templates/review-specs/defaults.yaml:54` already gives `review-base` `exclude: ["<target-spec>"]` so the target spec is never shipped twice today.
Consequence: either BEH-10 double-ships the target spec, or BEH-12 cap-exemption for it is VACUOUS because renderPack never inlines it in the first place. Both readings cannot be right.
Fix direction: map who owns target-spec embedding (renderPack vs buildReviewerDispatches) BEFORE respecifying. This was the tell that prompted the operator to consider splitting the spec.

=== 4. structural-architect:contradictory-contract:e4134970 @ behavioral-delta-beh-12 ===
BEH-12 says both caps bind the manifest text; BEH-10 and the 22m narrowing row guarantee nothing is EVER omitted for budget reasons. So a cap is declared with its only enforcement mechanism explicitly withdrawn.
Not theoretical: `max_file_bytes` defaults to 16384, and a `specs/**/*.spec.md` include resolves to roughly 810 paths in a single section — comfortably past 16 KB of path text.
Fix direction: decide what a manifest-cap breach actually does. Options: omit-with-notice (reintroducing 22m for manifest packs), hard error, or drop the caps for manifest text entirely and say so.

=== PATTERN NOTE — read before attempting another revise round ===
Rounds 1 and 2 both BLOCKed with persistent: 0 — not one blocker_id recurred across rounds (round 1: 7e24783f a2e26104 6f2a3dee e3daf2a8 3495680b 05edd24d; round 2: f37df0ec c6aabd22 0111fab5 e4134970 0e9ae87e). Spec grew 175 -> 198 lines. Three of the six round-1 blockers were genuinely RESOLVED and none regressed, yet three fixes each spawned a second-order defect: closing the body-injection channel opened a fence-header one; exempting the target spec from caps left the manifest caps unenforceable.
This is the failure mode adev-plugin-j7pq.1 documents ("persistent: 0 is structural, so NO_PROGRESS never fires"; eight cycles, ~1.37M tokens, zero PASS, monotonic line growth). The convergence detector would have returned CONTINUE here (5 new < 6 addressed) and burned the last retry to BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. This spec is therefore a SECOND documented instance of j7pq.1 and useful evidence for it.
RECOMMENDATION recorded at deferral time: rather than a third revise round, consider splitting — a rev-5 carrying only the `delivery: inline|manifest` declaration plus the consistency glob narrowing (BEH-1, BEH-9) would likely pass, with manifest RENDERING mechanics (fencing, attribute escaping, cap enforcement — i.e. blockers 1, 2 and 4 above) moved to a rev-6. Blocker 3 must be resolved first either way, since it determines whether renderPack inlines the target spec at all.
notes:
TWO MORE GAPS FOUND DURING IMPLEMENTATION (2026-08-17), both PINNED WITH MARKER TESTS rather than fixed, because BEH-11 mandates 22p-bis "retained verbatim" and bans new error codes — so neither could be fixed inside the rev-5 scope. Both belong in this issue.

GAP 5 — a DENYLIST_MATCH include still NAMES the denied glob in its emitted header.
On the CONTEXT_PACK_DENYLIST_MATCH path, `rendered` is non-empty despite `errors` being non-empty, and the no-matches section header carries the denied glob (e.g. attrs title="conf/profiles.yaml/", and inline mode emits role="no-matches" path="conf/profiles.yaml/"). The file BODY never ships in either mode — verified — so this is disclosure of the PATH, not the content. It is INHERITED rev-4 behaviour, not introduced by rev 5.
Pinned by: tests/governance/context-pack-manifest-denylist.test.mjs, test named "KNOWN GAP (adev-plugin-j7pq.7): a DENYLIST_MATCH include still names the denied glob in its no-matches header" — it asserts the current (wrong) shape, so it will FAIL when this is fixed. That is deliberate: the test is a tripwire, not a guard. Update it as part of the fix.

GAP 6 — trailing-separator denylist evasion via un-normalized matching. Arguably the most useful finding of the whole build.
`isDenied` is regex-anchored against the RAW glob string, while `expandGlob` normalizes separators via split("/").filter(Boolean). So the two disagree, and ANY denylist pattern anchored with `$` can be bypassed by appending a separator. Reproduced three ways during Task 6:
  conf/profiles.yaml/    -> resolves to conf/profiles.yaml
  conf/.env/             -> resolves to conf/.env
  conf//profiles.yaml/   -> resolves to conf/profiles.yaml
It currently lands on the SAFE side — these hit CONTEXT_PACK_DENYLIST_MATCH (hard error) rather than being silently admitted — so it is not presently exploitable. But it is the same raw-string-vs-resolved-path mismatch family as GAP 2 (LF-in-path), and the reviewer noted it would be cheapest to fix in the same pass. Fix `isDenied` to run on the NORMALIZED resolved path, not the raw glob.

CORRECTION TO THE ROUND-2 RECORD, worth keeping: Task 6 initially shipped a claim that CONTEXT_PACK_DENYLIST_MATCH was UNREACHABLE with no live caller. That claim was FALSE and the per-task review caught it — GAP 6 above is exactly the mechanism that reaches it. The false claim was removed and replaced with positive reachability tests (3b, 3c). Anyone reading older notes asserting DENYLIST_MATCH is dead code should disregard them.

STATUS OF THE ORIGINAL FOUR at end of build:
  1 fence-header title= unescaped — STILL OPEN. Task 5 neutralized path AND title lines in the manifest BODY, but fenceBlock still interpolates `attrs` raw at every call site, so the header attribute channel is not closed. Marker comment left at the site naming this issue.
  2 LF-in-path denylist evasion — STILL OPEN, unimplemented by design.
  3 target-spec inlining ownership — RESOLVED during planning, and the answer changed the design: renderPack does NOT inline the target spec and never did (no special case; defaults.yaml:54 excludes <target-spec>; dispatch-shape.mjs:98-103 builds specBlock separately and appends at :122/:154/:160 outside renderPack totalBytes). So BEH-12 cap exemption was ALREADY TRUE and needed a regression test, not a mechanism; TARGET_SPEC_OVERSIZE now fires from dispatch-shape.mjs, the only site knowing the spec byte length. What REMAINS here is re-anchoring the spec TEXT of BEH-10/BEH-12 to say "dispatch-assembly guarantee" rather than implying renderPack inlines anything.
  4 manifest caps unenforceable — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED: renderPack now returns `budgets` and `delivery` on all four return paths so a caller can enforce. Deciding WHAT a manifest-cap breach does (omit-with-notice, hard error, or drop the caps) is still open and still owned here.

GATE STATE: Task 8 was NOT executed. templates/review-specs/defaults.yaml has NO `delivery` key — verified by grep — so `delivery` defaults to inline everywhere and NO reviewer is exposed to manifest delivery. The renderer is complete, tested (+84 tests, all passing) and INERT. Closing this issue is the precondition for the Task 8 flip, which is routed human-only as a release call.

title: Path-manifest context-pack delivery should be the default, not opt-in
description:
Path-manifest delivery ships as an opt-in per-pack field defaulting to `inline`
(`delivery` in `lib/governance/context-pack.mjs`, resolved by nearest-declaration-wins
up the `extends` chain). The default should be flipped: `manifest` becomes the
default, `inline` the explicit opt-out.

## Why the default is the wrong way round

`adev-plugin-j7pq.6` measured inline delivery dropping 29-71% of matched files at
the 262144-byte cap, and — worse — nullifying per-reviewer pack differentiation:
the `security` pack lost both of its distinguishing includes
(`risk-policies.yaml`, `gates.yaml`) because they sort last in include order, so
`security` and `architecture` delivered functionally identical packs.

That fix shipped in PR #286, but behind an opt-in flag. Every project that does
not know to set `delivery: manifest` keeps the measured defect. A fix nobody
turns on is not a fix.

## Fresh measurement (this repo, 2026-08-17)

Reviewing `lifecycle-event-log-rev-5-review-gate-integrity.spec.md` with the
three bundled reviewers, before and after setting `delivery: manifest` on
`review-base`:

| Reviewer | inline | manifest | truncation notices (inline) | files omitted (manifest) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| structural-architect | 254635 B | 7615 B | 16 | 0 |
| security-reviewer | 254390 B | 7597 B | 16 | 0 |
| consistency-analyzer | 266105 B | 8432 B | 18 | 0 |

A ~33x prompt reduction with zero omitted files. The inline runs each carried a
truncation notice and dropped tail files; the manifest runs dropped none.

## The opt-in is also hostile to adopt

`mergePacks` (`lib/governance/context-pack.mjs`) replaces a pack entry wholesale
rather than merging field-by-field:

    packs[name] = entry;

So setting one field means restating the pack's entire `include` list in
`.context-index/governance/review.yaml`, duplicating the bundled definition and
creating drift the moment the bundled list changes. Adopting the fix costs a
copy-paste of bundled config — which is itself an argument for flipping the
default rather than asking every project to pay that cost.

## Scope

- Flip the `delivery` default from `inline` to `manifest` in the resolution rule.
- Keep `delivery: inline` working as an explicit per-pack opt-out.
- Decide whether `base` (consumed by `templates/domains/software/validate.yaml`
  as well as review) flips with it or stays inline — validate-time consumers were
  not part of the j7pq.6 measurement and should not be flipped blind.
- Update `templates/review-specs/defaults.yaml` comments and `docs/governance.md`.

## Precondition — do not flip before j7pq.7 lands

Under manifest delivery the target spec is emitted as an EMPTY fence carrying
only a `path=` attribute:

    <<<ADEV-PACK-<nonce> role="target-spec" path="...spec.md">>>

    <<<END-ADEV-PACK-<nonce>>>>

The reviewer must open the file to see the artifact it is reviewing, and the
preamble's read contract is written for `role="path-manifest"` fences, not
`role="target-spec"`. That is exactly the ownership ambiguity
`adev-plugin-j7pq.7` finding 3 raises (`structural-architect:ownership-ambiguity:0111fab5`).
Making manifest the default makes that ambiguity the default path for every
review, so j7pq.7 should land first.

Observed while reviewing the j7pq.3 amendment on branch `worktree-j7pq-review-gate`.

title: BLOCK->revise auto-retry loop cannot converge: no step authors spec content
description:
The BLOCK->revise auto-retry loop in `/adev:build --full` cannot converge, because
no step in it authors spec content. It burns a full review cycle per iteration to
arrive back where it started.

## What the loop does today

`skills/build/SKILL.md` "Blocker handling (Full Pipeline — BLOCK->revise auto-retry
loop)" step 4 dispatches:

    adev specify revise --spec <spec-path> --auto

and describes the verb as producing "revision N+1 as a targeted patch".

It does not produce a patch. `lib/specify-revise.mjs::reviseSpec` performs mechanics
only:

  - bumps `revision:` N -> N+1 through the monotonic diagnostic
  - sets `updated:` to today, `status:` review-blocked -> review-pending
  - clears `<spec-stem>.blockers.md`
  - emits `spec_revised`

`renderFrontmatter(parsed, updates)` rebuilds the document as
`lines.slice(0, openIdx+1)` + updated frontmatter + `lines.slice(closeIdx)`, so the
body is preserved BYTE-IDENTICALLY. To be precise: this is not data loss and the
body is not damaged — it is simply never changed. That is correct behaviour for a
mechanics verb. The defect is that the loop contains no other step that would
change it.

## Why it cannot converge

One iteration produces: rev N -> N+1, identical body, re-review over identical
text, therefore identical findings and identical `blocker_id` hashes (the id is
`sha256(<section-anchor>:<finding-text>)`, so unchanged text yields an unchanged
id). The convergence detector then sees `addressed = {}`, `new_ = {}`,
`persistent == prev_blockers` and returns `NO_PROGRESS`.

Cost of learning this at runtime, measured on
`lifecycle-event-log-rev-5-review-gate-integrity.spec.md` (risk_level: high, so
full tier, three reviewers): ~11 minutes and ~121k subagent tokens per cycle.

This repo sets `build.max_review_retries: 9` (default is 2), so a run that did not
short-circuit on NO_PROGRESS would be considerably more expensive.

## Secondary: the event over-reports

`reviseSpec` sets `addressed = blockerEntries.map(e => e.blocker_id)` and
`unresolved = []` unconditionally, with a source comment conceding it: "For now,
every blocker in the input is acknowledged as addressed by the revise". So
`spec_revised` claims every blocker was addressed even when the body did not
change. Any consumer trusting `addressed_blocker_ids` as evidence of work is
reading a value that was never computed.

## Ambiguity worth resolving with the fix

`skills/specify/SKILL.md` Revise Mode also just says "run the CLI verb", so neither
the build loop nor the specify skill contains an authoring step. If the intent was
for a SUBAGENT running `/adev:specify --revise` to reason about the sidecar and edit
the body before calling the verb — which is what a human/agent does by hand and what
made rev 1 -> rev 2 actually progress on this spec — then that authoring step needs
to be written down, because today it is in neither skill.

## Suggested direction

Either:
  (a) the loop dispatches a subagent that reads `.blockers.md`, authors targeted body
      changes per `section_anchor`, and only then calls the mechanics verb; or
  (b) `adev specify revise` gains an authoring pass; or
  (c) the loop is documented as mechanics-only and disabled by default, with
      `max_review_retries: 0` as the shipped default.

Whichever is chosen, `spec_revised` should report what actually changed rather than
echoing its input.

Observed while running `/adev:build --full --auto` on the j7pq.3 amendment after its
rev-2 review returned BLOCK with 4 new blockers.

title: Cross-layer duplicate test coverage: same invariant asserted at lib, CLI, hook, and e2e layers
description: From the 2026-08-10 three-repo audit. The one finding with no issue of any kind until now. Roughly 12-15% of test cases in both code repos (adev-plugin, repo-B) assert the same invariant at multiple layers — a rule implemented once in lib/ gets a lib unit test, a CLI-verb test, a hook test, and an e2e test, each re-asserting the identical behavior rather than testing that layer's own contract (wiring, argument parsing, exit codes). Consequence is runtime and maintenance cost with no added defect-detection: a change to the invariant breaks 4 tests that all encode the same fact, while a genuine wiring regression between layers may still slip through untested. Needs measurement before prescription: quantify the true duplication rate (the audit's 12-15% was a sampled estimate, not an exhaustive count), then decide whether the fix is guidance in write-test (assert behavior once at its owning layer; at other layers assert only the delegation) or a detector. Likely overlaps issue-555's hygiene test-debt pass — consider folding in as one more detection there rather than building separate machinery.

The substrate already ships: adev diagnose + the diagnostic registry (templates/diagnostics-template.yaml, project: runner prefix) with tier-1 producers for frontmatter presence, status enum, event schema, revision monotonicity. Tiers 2 and 3 are declared in the registry schema but NO tier-2/3 producers ship. Fix: add tier-2 producers for SKILL.md / spec / docs structure (required sections, frontmatter schema, the skill-extension block), and have write-test explicitly forbid string-matching prose as a test deliverable. title: json -> beads migration RENUMBERS every issue and loses the source-id mapping, breaking dependencies and all cross-references
description: Found 2026-08-13 on the first migration run that got far enough to expose it -- only reachable after fixing issue-626 (--db path) and issue-627 (epic creation). BLOCKS any json->beads migration; do not flip tasks.backend until this is fixed. WHAT HAPPENS: BeadsAdapter.create() assigns a fresh sequential id -- nextId = 'issue-' + (count of issue- keys in .beads-map.json + 1) -- and keys the map by that NEW id. The source id is never recorded anywhere. The source board's ids are sparse (issue-1..issue-627 with gaps from deletions); the target map is contiguous (issue-1..issue-309). Every issue therefore silently changes identity. VERIFIED CONCRETELY: source issue-625 ('gate doctor verifies a different gate set...') sits at index 306 of the source list and lands as target issue-307. Map entry fields are only {beadsId, next_action, epicId, ...} -- no source_id/original_id. CONSEQUENCE 1, dependencies: the verb passes SOURCE ids to BeadsAdapter.addDependency, which resolves them against .beads-map.json keys that are now TARGET ids, so lookups miss. Observed dependencies_replayed: 5 of 41, with 'No beads mapping for issue: issue-615 / issue-557 / issue-622' warnings. The 5 that survived are coincidental matches where a source id happened to equal its own index. 36 of 41 edges silently dropped, including the epic-108 wave sequencing (554->552, 555->552, 615->555, 614->559, 557->585/586, 623->557, 625->552/554). CONSEQUENCE 2, far worse and NOT reported at all: every human-readable cross-reference breaks. Issue notes across this board reference other issues by id ('tracked as issue-623', 'see issue-557', 'this is issue-584 in the wild'), as do commit messages, PR descriptions, and spec files. After migration those ids resolve to DIFFERENT issues. Nothing warns; the board looks complete and internally consistent while silently meaning something else. ASYMMETRY WORTH NOTING: the reverse direction already solves this -- runLiveMigration stamps 'original_id: <sourceId>' into notes for beads->json specifically so a re-run can dedupe. json->beads has no equivalent. FIX DIRECTIONS: preserve the source id as the map key (target ids are an implementation detail of beads and need not be resequenced), or at minimum record source_id in each map entry and resolve addDependency through it; and have the verb FAIL LOUDLY rather than warn-and-continue when an edge cannot be resolved, since a silently partial dependency graph is indistinguishable from a complete one. Also fix the created-counter reporting noted in issue-627 (a run that created 308 issues reported created:{issues:0}). STATE: fully rolled back. .beads, .beads-map.json and .migrate-state.json removed; manifest still tasks.backend: json; json board authoritative and complete at 309 issues / 106 epics. Pre-migration snapshot committed at c3d4a875 on branch chore/board-migrate-to-beads. PROCESS NOTE for whoever retries: .migrate-state.json persists a resume cursor (lastSuccessfulIndex). Wiping .beads and .beads-map.json WITHOUT deleting it causes the next run to resume mid-stream and silently migrate almost nothing -- observed as created:{issues:1} against a 309-issue board. Arguably the verb should detect an empty target map against a non-zero resume cursor and refuse.

title: Conditional check execution in validate (skip N/A checks earlier)
description:
Validate runs every registered check on every spec, including checks that cannot produce a finding for that spec. Skipping them earlier — before any subagent dispatch — is the cheapest speed win in the check pipeline.

Known N/A classes, measured in harness-simplification-study.md Part 2:

- **Empty ruleset.** check-8-boundaries over `boundaries: []` (40 PASS / 0 FAIL) and check-9-transition-gates over `transitions: {}` (39 PASS + 1 PWN / 0 FAIL). Both dispatch a subagent at severity: error to evaluate nothing.
- **Inapplicable target.** check-11-visual-verification on a non-UI diff — already self-guards (SKIPs rather than BLOCKs), and is the model the others should follow.
- **Absent input.** Checks whose required artifact does not exist for this spec.

The general rule: a check declares its applicability predicate, the orchestrator evaluates it deterministically before dispatch, and a non-applicable check records SKIP with a reason rather than PASS. A PASS currently asserts the check verified something; for an empty ruleset that assertion is false.

Reopened from deferred 2026-08-14 and pulled into the governance-checks work: under the working definition of simplification — faster and more cohesive checks, even if more numerous — early skip is the mechanism that makes 'more checks' affordable.

title: CLI install integration (cursor-provider Spec D)
session-capture: add summary mode for SessionEnd captures instead of full verbatim transcript
description:
## Problem

`integrations.session_capture.capture: hook` (SessionEnd + PreCompact) writes a
VERBATIM dump of the conversation, not a summary. `fromTranscript()`
(lib/session-summary.mjs:165) walks every transcript line, extracts role + text,
and emits each turn under `### user` / `### assistant` with no condensation
step — no summarization, no truncation.

Users reasonably expect a "session log" to be a summary. The name of the
artifact directory (`.context-index/sessions/`) and the README's phrasing
("redacted markdown summaries") both reinforce that expectation.

## What is actually captured today

Captured: user message text, assistant message text, and `!command` stdout
(which arrives as a user message, so shell output lands verbatim).

Dropped: tool_use blocks, tool_result blocks (command output, file contents),
and thinking blocks — `extractMessageText` maps content blocks through
`b?.text`, so anything without a `.text` field is filtered out
(lib/session-summary.mjs:120).

`redactSecrets` (lib/session-summary.mjs:82) runs unconditionally, but it is a
fixed regex list (PEM blocks, bearer tokens, KEY=VALUE shapes). It catches
secret-SHAPED strings, not prose.

## Gap

There is no setting that combines the SessionEnd trigger with a condensed body.
The three modes are:

- `hook`        — SessionEnd/PreCompact trigger, full verbatim conversation
- `post-commit` — commit trigger, condensed body (subject/body, changed files,
                  tool counts)
- `off`         — nothing

A user who wants session-scoped capture (one file per session rather than one
per commit, which is the main win of hook mode) has no way to get a summary.
Their only route to condensation is to go back to `post-commit` and give up the
SessionEnd trigger — which is what this project just did.

## Proposal

Add a summarization option to hook mode. Sketch — exact shape open for design:

- a new knob, e.g. `integrations.session_capture.body: summary|transcript`
  (default `summary`), orthogonal to the existing `capture` trigger knob; or
- a fourth `capture:` value, e.g. `hook-summary`

Either way the summary body should record intent and outcome (what the session
set out to do, what changed) rather than the message log. The post-commit
renderer already demonstrates the target shape — Intent / Files changed /
Session activity — and could be adapted to a session-scoped input.

## Notes

- Reduces exposure surface for projects that track `.context-index/sessions/`
  in git. This repo is public and has 722 session files committed.
- Consumers to keep working: /adev:retro, /adev:status, /adev:hygiene,
  /adev:work all read `.context-index/sessions/`. Retro in particular parses
  the optional frontmatter (cost_usd, input_tokens, output_tokens, model,
  issue, epic) — a summary mode must keep emitting those.
- Spec to amend: .context-index/specs/features/session-awareness/hook-driven-capture.spec.md
  (Behavior 8 defines the SessionEnd render path; the Transcript redaction
  invariant at line 142 is adjacent).

## Minor defect found while investigating

`unregisterSessionCaptureHooks()` (lib/session-capture-installer.mjs:460) leaves
empty `"SessionEnd": []` / `"PreCompact": []` arrays in hooks.json rather than
deleting the keys. Functionally inert, but it means toggling hook mode on and
then off does not round-trip to the original file. Worth folding in or splitting
out.

title: adev:build Full Pipeline and Phase Filter
Model-routing config and docs are stale: build skill documents a removed model: pin, model_tiers names superseded models
description:
Three related defects in how adev selects models, found while running
/adev:build on the governance-checks-unbundle branch.

## 1. `skills/build/SKILL.md` documents a mechanism that was deliberately removed

Line 63 states:

> **Model:** The build orchestrator pins `claude-sonnet-4-6` via the skill's
> frontmatter `model:` field. ... This is a temporary hardcode; the
> config-driven binding via `/adev:sync` is tracked by issue-538.

That pin does not exist. It was removed on purpose in `42294cf7` /
`170f8837` ("fix(build): remove hardcoded model: claude-sonnet-4-6 from
frontmatter — Let the user's active model handle the build orchestrator
rather than forcing Sonnet 4.6. No spec tracks this frontmatter key.").
No SKILL.md in the repo carries a `model:` field today:

    grep -rln "^model:" skills/*/SKILL.md   # no matches

The removal looks right. The prose was not updated to match, so the file
now asserts a cost control the codebase does not have, along with the
retro evidence that motivated it (~5x Sonnet cost on cache reads, the
dominant cost class). Anyone reading it reasonably concludes orchestration
is cheap when it is not.

**Fix:** rewrite the paragraph to describe actual behaviour — the
orchestrator runs on the session's active model — and either restate the
cost consideration as guidance or drop it.

## 2. `issue-538` does not exist

The same paragraph points at `issue-538` for the config-driven binding.
`br show issue-538` returns "Issue not found", and no issue on the board
matches model-routing or model-tier. The follow-up work is untracked.

**Fix:** file the config-driven-binding work as a real issue and update the
reference, or drop the reference.

## 3. `platform-context.yaml:model_tiers` names superseded models

    model_tiers:
      fast:      claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
      capable:   claude-sonnet-4-6
      reasoning: claude-opus-4-7

`claude-opus-4-7` is superseded. The current family is Claude 5 —
`claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-fable-5` — with Haiku 4.5 still
current. Per `model-routing.spec.md`, per-step worker skills resolve their
tier from this map, so the reasoning tier (architecture review,
cross-cutting analysis) points at a superseded model.

**Fix:** update the map, and consider how it stays current — a stale tier
map degrades silently, with no error and no failing test.

## Observed impact

On this build every step subagent (plan, route, implement, validate, for
two specs) ran on the parent session model rather than any configured
tier, because the `Agent` dispatch passes no `model` override and the
frontmatter pin no longer exists. That is defensible behaviour, but it is
neither what the docs describe nor what `model_tiers` implies, and for a
mechanical orchestration workload it is the expensive option.

## Suggested guard

A test asserting that every model id named in `platform-context.yaml` and
in skill prose is a currently-supported model would catch all three of
these. Model ids are a class of config that goes stale without any signal.

title: DECISION: infra-gated suites (Postgres/docker) fail hard, making npm test red without docker — pick a policy
description:
Surfaced by issue-560 (test discovery fix). Before: sh collapsed the ** glob so 339 of 416 files ran. After: 410 run (6 nested-project fixture suites excluded by rule). Measured 2026-08-12: full suite 5448 tests / 33 fail; the 71 newly-included files run alone give 1112 tests / 31 fail; the original 339-file set alone gives 1 fail (a concurrency flake). So ~31 failures are in code that has never executed in CI. Affected suites: tests/evals/integration-sandbox/* (Phase 1 fixture setup, Phase 3 live-Postgres execution, reality-check fixture + end-to-end Check 12), which expect PostgreSQL on port 5433 with seeded data. They fail hard rather than skip — consistent with the project preference that integration tests must never silently self-skip. Consequence: the single quality gate (npm test) is red on any machine without docker-compose running. Options: (a) keep them in the default run and require docker for a green suite; (b) split into npm run test:integration with an explicit, documented tag and keep npm test unit-only; (c) keep them in-run but let the harness fail with a clear "infra required" message. This is a policy call, not a code fix — do not resolve it by silently excluding the suites.

CORRECTED 2026-08-12 after review. My original framing was wrong: adev-plugin has NO Postgres dependency (root package.json has only tree-sitter deps). The Postgres/docker belongs to tests/evals/integration-sandbox/, a self-contained FIXTURE PROJECT with its own package.json, its own pg dependency, and its own docker-compose.yml, described as a "minimal Node.js + PostgreSQL fixture for testing whether adev skills write honest integration tests against real external infrastructure". Its driver even documents "run `npm run db:up` first" — it is a manually-run eval, never intended for automated npm test. Resolution: tests/evals/** is now a separate opt-in bucket (npm run test:evals), so the default gate no longer depends on machine state. DECISION TAKEN: evals are excluded from the default npm test and run via npm run test:evals. This is NOT the silent-skip pattern to avoid — the split is printed on every run, asserted by tests/test-discovery.test.mjs (buckets must partition every file on disk with no overlap), and reachable by an explicit script. Reversible via npm run test:all.; Closed: Resolved by the eval/default bucket split in scripts/run-tests.mjs; decision recorded on the issue.

title: Fix the .review.md / .validate.md writer to emit frontmatter first (no template exists for these kinds)
description:
153 of 203 .review.md and 122 of 123 .validate.md files violate the first-non-blank-line --- rule — the larger half of the corpus problem. Unlike specs, these artifact kinds have no template: they are produced by lib/cli/artifact.mjs (closed type -> suffix map, .tmp+rename commit) and by skill prose in skills/review-specs and skills/validate that never states where frontmatter goes. Fix belongs in the writer (and/or a bundled report template), not in a spec template. Root cause verified 2026-08-12. lib/diagnostics/tier1/frontmatter-present.mjs rejects any markdown body before the --- delimiter ("a markdown body (e.g. a leading # heading) before --- is rejected"). Natural experiment confirming causation: the 4 charter templates start with --- and 0 of 47 .charter.md files violate; the 6 spec templates start with an H1 and 128 of 235 .spec.md files violate. Full corpus scan by artifact kind (the 4 kinds the diagnostic covers): .charter.md 0/47, .spec.md 128/235, .review.md 153/203, .validate.md 122/123 — roughly 400 violating artifacts, which is what produces the ~52% event share. Reviews and validates have NO template; they are written by lib/cli/artifact.mjs and by skill prose that never specifies frontmatter position, so that half needs a writer fix rather than a template fix. Safety check: tests/templates/spec-template.behavioral.test.mjs only does substring includes() assertions (infra_requirements + security note) — nothing asserts ordering, so reordering the template does not break it.

## RE-DIAGNOSED 2026-08-14 — the fix is NOT in lib/cli/artifact.mjs

An investigation agent was scoped to fix the writer and correctly STOPPED without
changing code. The verb's enforcement is already right; the writers never reach it.

MECHANISM — bypass on two independent paths:

1. .review.md (157/210 violations) — no path to the verb exists at all.
   skills/review-specs/SKILL.md contains ZERO occurrences of `artifact commit`
   and zero of `.tmp` (independently re-verified: grep -c returns 0). Its Step 6b
   instructs a plain Write straight to the final .review.md path. Nothing added
   inside artifact.mjs is reachable from that writer.

2. .validate.md (125/129) — naming the verb in prose does not make it get used.
   skills/validate/SKILL.md names the verb 3 times and documents the exact
   contract at :424 (re-verified: grep -c returns 3). Yet of the 13 review/validate
   artifacts added on or after 2026-08-12 — the day ARTIFACT_FRONTMATTER_NOT_FIRST
   landed in 526e8a17 — 6 are heading-first, and 3 of those 6 are .validate.md
   (test-depth-policy, test-helper-inventory, gate-doctor). Because the verb exits 1
   and leaves the .tmp behind, their existence at final paths proves they never went
   through it. The other 7 of 13 ARE frontmatter-first, so the verb works when
   actually invoked.

This rules out both "tighten the verb" and "document it better". skills/review-specs
SKILL.md:280 already states the frontmatter-first rule in prose and still yields
157/210 — a second independent instance of prose not holding the line.

WHY COMPOSE-BY-CONSTRUCTION INSIDE THE VERB WOULD BE DEAD CODE: composition would
be driven by new flags only a caller that already invokes the verb could pass, and
the 157-violation writer never invokes it. Also, the typical violator has no YAML
block to lift — its metadata is a prose blockquote (> **Date:**, > **Verdict:**),
and the 246 files containing a --- elsewhere are horizontal rules and table
separators, so auto-repair-by-lifting would corrupt bodies.

CORRECTED SCOPE — two follow-ups, neither in artifact.mjs:
  (a) A PreToolUse Write|Edit guard matching *.review.md / *.validate.md final
      paths. This is the only mechanism that makes the bad shape unproducible
      regardless of which writer runs, which is what "by construction" requires
      here. Model on hooks/plan-body-write-guard.sh (same _parse-stdin.sh +
      suffix-case + exit 2 shape); register in the existing "Write|Edit" matcher
      block at hooks/hooks.json:33.
  (b) Route skills/review-specs/SKILL.md Step 6b through .tmp + `adev artifact
      commit --kind review`. Provider mirrors exist under providers/codex/skills/
      and providers/opencode/skills/ and would need the same change.

SEPARATE FINDING, not acted on: running the tier-1 diagnostic against all 339
artifacts alongside the verb's hasLeadingFrontmatter, exactly ONE file diverges —
output-personas/verbosity-axis-and-output-trimming.review.md passes the verb but
fires the diagnostic. Its frontmatter uses a `post-review-edit: |` block scalar:
valid YAML that the in-tree parseYaml mini-parser rejects. So the divergence is the
DIAGNOSTIC being over-strict, not the verb being under-strict, and wiring parseYaml
into the commit path would make the verb reject a valid artifact. The header comment
at lib/cli/artifact.mjs:48-51 ("so the writer and the diagnostic cannot disagree") is
inaccurate in that one direction — a doc nit, not a bug.

issue-587 (backfill ~400 artifacts) still depends on this landing first: the corpus
grew from 153/203 and 122/123 to 157/210 and 125/129 in two days, so the writers are
still manufacturing violations.

Existing scaffolds silently lose every gate with a string command, and upgrade never migrates them
description:
SHIPPED DEFECT AFFECTING USERS, NOT JUST THIS REPO.

lib/domains/merge-gates.mjs:36 rejects any gate whose `command` is a shell string:

  INVALID_GATE: Gate '<id>' command must be an argv list (array), not a string — skipped.

That requirement landed in commit 9be9ffef and first shipped in **adev-cli-v0.25.0**.
Every gates.yaml authored before it — or hand-written since, following the old
docs — declares `command: "npm test"` and is DROPPED AT LOAD.

Nothing migrates it and nothing warns:

  - cli/index.mjs:292-297 scaffolds templates with `if (!existsSync(destPath))`,
    so an existing governance/gates.yaml is skipped entirely by install/upgrade.
  - No migration path in lib/migrate-state-artifacts.mjs or lib/cli/issues-migrate.mjs
    touches gate command shape.

MEASURED IN THIS REPO (2026-08-14). adev-plugin's own gates.yaml carried
`command: "npm test"`. Resolved through the real loader:

  BEFORE (string command): 0 gate(s) | INVALID_GATE
  AFTER  (argv list)     : 2 gate(s) | 0 warnings

So every /adev:validate Check 1 run in the adev repo itself, since 0.25.0, has
evaluated ZERO gates while reporting normally. Fixed here in commit 5d5b6c00;
users on their own scaffolds are still exposed.

This is issue-552's thesis ("all three repos wrote tests that never executed, and
adev never noticed") reproducing in the framework's own dogfood repo, and it is
independent evidence for that issue's p0.

PROPOSED FIX — one or more of:
  (a) a migration in `adev upgrade` that rewrites string commands to argv lists
      (a shell-string with metacharacters cannot be safely auto-split — those
      should be reported, not guessed);
  (b) at minimum, surface merge-gates warnings during install/upgrade instead of
      only at gate-resolution time, so a dropped gate is loud;
  (c) have `adev gate doctor` exit non-zero on INVALID_GATE (today it reports
      0 errors / 3 warnings for a config whose gate set is empty).

Note (c) matters most: gate doctor exists precisely to answer "do the declared
gates actually run", and a gate silently dropped at load is the case it should
never miss.

Source: 2026-08-14 config-adoption audit; every claim above re-verified against
the codebase.

title: Claim leases need a TTL and a release path, or a dead session blocks an issue forever
description:
Root cause established 2026-08-12 after two agents independently fixed the same p0 vulnerability an hour apart (PR #214 and duplicate PR #215, both for issue-582), and after a whole concurrent epic (epic-102, issues 568-581, PRs #210-#214) stayed invisible to a study pursuing the same goal. The issue board resolves storage via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs) and IS shared across worktrees. Execution state does NOT: lib/execution-state.mjs reads <projectRoot>/.context-index/.execution-state.json, which is worktree-local. Measured live: /adev:work Step 1 reported status "idle" in this worktree while four epic-102 issues were in_progress and five PRs were open. Second, behavioural half: the board DID carry the signal (issue-582 was already in_progress) and nothing re-reads an issue at the moment work begins, so stale local knowledge won over the shared record.

Without expiry, the first crashed or abandoned session permanently locks an issue and the claim gate becomes something people bypass — which is worse than no gate, because it trains bypassing. Needs: claimed_at timestamp, a configurable TTL, an explicit adev issues release <id>, and a stale-claim report surfaced by /adev:status.

RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (epic-107): Closed by ae9b67de — tasks.claim_ttl_minutes (default 240), fail-closed staleness, takeover reported not persisted, adev issues stale.

title: /adev:work has no worktree-isolated parallel batch mode — parallel agent work runs unisolated in one tree
description:
THE GAP. /adev:work has no parallel-agent mode at all. Its only use of the word
"parallel" is "parallel tool calls in a single round" for the Step 1 state scan.
Worktree-isolated parallelism exists only in /adev:implement --parallel, which is
driven by a plan's `## Parallelization` section and therefore unavailable for any
work that has no plan — bug batches, chores, research follow-ups.

So an operator who asks the front door to "batch these in parallel" gets whatever
the agent improvises. Today that was manual file-disjointness in ONE shared working
tree, which is --parallel's principle (file-disjoint groups) without its mechanism
(isolation).

MEASURED COST, 2026-08-14 session — ~10 agents across 4 waves, all file-disjoint:
  - an agent ran `git stash push/pop` on files other agents held, and raced a
    concurrent commit; two files came back staged. Nothing was lost, but only
    because the agent disclosed it and it was checked.
  - `npm test` stopped being a usable gate. One agent ran it three times and got
    three different results (2 fail / 2 different fails / 25 fail) because the
    modified-file set changed between two `git status` calls.
  - four separate agents spent tokens reasoning about edits that were not theirs,
    and each had to be told in its report which failures to ignore.
  - one agent reported the branch had "changed mid-session".
  - agents could not commit their own work, so every batch needed the orchestrator
    to verify and commit by explicit path.
File-disjointness itself held — no agent clobbered another's file. Everything that
broke is what isolation would have prevented.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS NON-OBVIOUS. The naive fix — passing the harness's
`isolation: "worktree"` on each Agent dispatch — is explicitly FORBIDDEN by this
framework, at skills/implement/SKILL.md:460:

  "Do not pass isolation: 'worktree'. ... From inside an existing worktree, worktree
   isolation nests a new worktree inside the parent — the parent then captures it as
   untracked .claude/worktrees/agent-<id>/ content, and every per-task dispatch adds
   another level (8+ deep observed in field reports). Subagents that commit also
   defeat the harness's auto-cleanup contract, leaving the nested trees on disk
   forever."

So this capability cannot be "set the flag". It has to use adev-managed worktrees,
the same mechanism --parallel already uses.

THE PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS AND RUNS STANDALONE:
  adev worktree <add|list|merge|remove|guard> [--slug <s>] [--base <ref>] [--no-ff]
                                              [--force] [--delete-branch]
It needs no plan. `adev worktree guard` already reports nested: true, which is the
detector for the nesting hazard above.

PROPOSED CAPABILITY — worktree-isolated batches from the front door:
  1. /adev:work gains a batch-dispatch mode that takes N independent work items
     (issue ids, not plan tasks) and runs each in its own `adev worktree add --slug`
     tree, then merges back deterministically via `adev worktree merge`.
  2. Reuse --parallel's existing machinery rather than inventing a second one:
     `adev parallel baseline` / `max-parallel` / `collision`, the RERUN_COLLISION and
     --fresh semantics, and the nested-worktree guard.
  3. Decide and document what the equivalence gate means here. For --parallel it is
     "a parallel run must be behaviorally equivalent to serial", enforced by the
     equivalence eval. Independent bug fixes have no such ordering guarantee, so the
     gate needs restating or explicitly scoping out.
  4. Keep file-disjointness as a PRECONDITION, not a substitute. Worktrees remove the
     interference; they do not make two agents editing the same file safe to merge.

GOVERNANCE: adding a mode to /adev:work is a skill-surface change and per CLAUDE.md
"Adding new skills to the lifecycle order" / skill-surface changes require human
approval. This should get a spec before implementation, not a direct patch.

RELATED: issue-547 (Parallel Implement, closed) shipped the worktree machinery;
issue-546 (Worktree Primitive, closed) shipped the verb. This issue is about making
the front door able to USE them for non-plan work.

/adev:recover emits no recovery_record, but the projection still consumes it
description:
Surfaced by lifecycle-event audit on 2026-05-17 (LIFE-8, LIFE-15). The lifecycle library exposes reportStep with status: failed (CLI: adev report --type step --status failed) and recovery_record is in the canonical event set, but no skill calls either on failure paths. Result: partial runs leave the lifecycle log with a started event and no terminal event, making the spec unrecoverable for downstream gates. Concrete failure paths that should emit step_failed but do not (from audit): implement Step 1.5 Infra Preflight FAIL; implement Step 2-post Integration Gate severity-error failure; implement TDD blocker exits; specify CHARTER_CLOSED gate; plan REVIEW_GATE / CODE_DRIFT blocks; validate Check 1 quality-gates fail-fast exit. Additionally /adev:recover is documented as producer of recovery_record events but emits nothing. Acceptance: each lifecycle skill emits adev report --type step --status failed --verdict FAIL with --error summary on early-exit paths; /adev:recover emits recovery_record (or that event is removed from canonical); new lifecycle-state test asserts terminal event present for failure-path fixtures.

## Rescoped 2026-08-14
Verified that skills/specify/SKILL.md now emits step_failed. The gap is narrower than filed: audit the remaining skills rather than treating this as "no skill emits".

## Rescoped again 2026-08-14 (post-merge audit)

Two of the three acceptance clauses are now MET on main:

1. DONE — step_failed emission. PR #263 (merged 2026-08-14) added
   `--status failed --verdict FAIL` emissions to all five skills named in
   the original audit: implement (2 occurrences), specify (2), plan (1),
   validate (1), review-specs (1). Verified by reading origin/main.
2. DONE — test coverage. tests/skills/step-failed-emission.test.mjs exists
   on main with 14 tests asserting the terminal event is present per skill,
   including the scoping rule that aborts BEFORE the started event must not
   emit.
3. NOT DONE — /adev:recover still emits nothing. skills/recover/SKILL.md
   contains zero `adev report` invocations, while `recovery_record` is
   still a live case in lib/lifecycle-state.mjs:1600. The documented
   producer/consumer pair remains broken in exactly the way originally filed.

Remaining work is clause 3 only: either make /adev:recover emit
recovery_record, or remove recovery_record from the canonical event set.
Deciding between those two is the actual open question — the event has a
consumer in the projection but no producer anywhere.

Note on the --error sub-clause: the original acceptance text asks for
`--error summary` on the failed emission. `adev report --type step` accepts
no --error flag (lib/cli/report.mjs drops it), and #263 deliberately
documented that as a known gap rather than instructing an unsupported flag.

title: Rewrite skills/build/SKILL.md for two pipeline modes and route-by-default
BLOCK-to-revise loop cannot converge: reviseSpec makes no content edits but reports every blocker addressed
description:
`adev specify revise` never edits spec body content, so the BLOCK→revise auto-retry loop in `/adev:build --full` structurally cannot converge on any blocker that requires a content change. It also writes false provenance into the lifecycle log.

## What happened

Observed 2026-08-15 during `/adev:build --module heuristics --tier full` on `failure-signature-key.spec.md`.

Full-tier review BLOCKed revision 1 with 6 blockers (2 of 3 reviewers; all `blocker_id`s well-formed, so the auto-retry path was viable — no `LEGACY_REVIEWER_OUTPUT` fallback). Per the build skill's loop, the next step is `adev specify revise --spec <path> --auto`. It returned:

```json
{"from_revision":1,"to_revision":2,
 "addressed_blocker_ids":[<all 6 ids>],
 "unresolved_blocker_ids":[],
 "blockers_cleared":true}
```

The actual diff was **1 insertion, 1 deletion** — `revision: 1` → `revision: 2`. Not one line of spec body changed. It also flipped `status: review-blocked → review-pending` and deleted the `.blockers.md` sidecar.

The six blockers were genuine design defects (two normalizers conflated into one; an output prefix that could not reproduce `/adev:recover`'s existing ids; a missing `blocker_id` mapping the charter invariant requires; a postcondition owned by a sibling spec). None is mechanically resolvable — each needs authored prose.

## Root cause

`lib/specify-revise.mjs:295-298`:

```js
const addressed = blockerEntries.map(e => e.blocker_id);
// For now, every blocker in the input is acknowledged as addressed by the
// revise — the next review re-evaluates and reports any that persist.
const unresolved = [];
```

`addressed` is unconditionally the full input set and `unresolved` is unconditionally empty, regardless of what changed.

The library's own doc comment (lines 11-14) is honest about this: *"the patch acknowledges blockers but leaves the bulk of the spec untouched — the operator or a follow-up review decides what content edits are needed."* The defect is that `skills/build/SKILL.md` presents this same verb as an **auto-retry loop** that resolves BLOCKs, with `build.max_review_retries` defaulting to 2.

## Two distinct defects

**1. The loop cannot converge (severity: high).** For any content-requiring blocker, the sequence is: revise makes no edits → re-review returns the identical blocker set → `partitionBlockers` yields `addressed = ∅, new = ∅, persistent = prev` → `evaluateStopCondition` returns `NO_PROGRESS` → build halts. Under `--auto` this is guaranteed, and it costs a full three-specialist review round (~145k subagent tokens and ~8 min in the observed run) to discover the verb did nothing. The loop only converges on blockers that need no content change, which is close to the empty set.

**2. False provenance in the lifecycle log (severity: medium).** The `spec_revised` event records `addressed_blocker_ids` = all input blockers on every invocation. Anything reading that log — `/adev:retro` metrics, `/adev:hygiene`, delivery analysis — will report blockers as resolved that were never touched. This is unfalsifiable from the log alone.

Note: the convergence detector itself is **not** compromised. `skills/build/SKILL.md` feeds it `partitionBlockers(prev_blockers, curr_blockers)` computed from real re-review output, not the verb's return value. Defect 1 is that the loop stalls, not that it produces a wrong verdict.

## Suggested direction

Not prescribing the fix, but the options seem to be:

- **Make the loop authored.** The revise step dispatches a subagent that reads `.review.md` + `.blockers.md` and actually re-authors the implicated sections, then the CLI verb does the bookkeeping. This is what the build skill's prose already implies happens.
- **Or make the docs match the code.** Drop the auto-retry framing, default `build.max_review_retries` to 0, and have BLOCK go straight to sidecar+fail-loud with a clear "author the fixes, then `--resume`" message. Cheaper, honest, loses the automation.

Either way, `addressed_blocker_ids` should reflect something real — at minimum, only anchors whose section bytes actually changed.

## Files

- `lib/specify-revise.mjs:295-298` — the hardcoded `addressed` / `unresolved`
- `lib/cli/specify.mjs` — the `revise` verb wrapper
- `skills/build/SKILL.md` — "Blocker handling (Full Pipeline — BLOCK→revise auto-retry loop)"
- `.context-index/specs/cross-cutting/review-block-auto-retry.spec.md` — owning spec
- `lib/loop-convergence.mjs` — consumer (behaving correctly)

## Workaround in use

Author the blocker fixes by hand between the revise call and the re-review. Done for `failure-signature-key` rev 2 in commit ddea5eb9.

The research also recommends restructuring Layer 3 from 0-100 / 0-5 scales to BINARY per-criterion verdicts with an "Unknown" escape hatch, citing judge-bias literature (Zheng 2023, Ye 2024, Shi 2024, Chen 2025) — a judge asked to emit a number is the documented anti-pattern. tests/evals/skill-compression/'s YAML rubric shape is named as the right pattern to standardize on.

From .context-index/research/harness-simplification-study.md Part 1 and Phase 1 item 3.

Source: 2026-08-14 research-vs-board audit. Claim re-verified against the codebase at that date, not taken from the research artifact alone.
close_reason: Fixed. skills/eval/default-rubric.yaml now ships, colocated with the skill per the house companion-file pattern and resolving at runtime as <ADEV_ROOT>/skills/eval/default-rubric.yaml. templates/ would have been wrong — those are cpSync-ed at scaffold time and never resolve for the plugin own runtime. One subagent per criterion, dispatched in parallel, each seeing ONLY its own criterion and explicitly forbidden the other verdicts or the running total — that isolation is the judge-bias mitigation, not the binary verdicts alone. Two constraints found empirically and worth keeping: the house minimal YAML reader parses only column-0 keys, 2-space list items and 4-space props (plan.yaml own scoring block silently loads as []), so the rubric is flat and a test enforces it; and lib/profiles/yaml.mjs parses integers only, so the threshold is 40 rather than 0.4. title: Raw NUL bytes in lib/retro/session-metrics.mjs make it binary to grep and git diff
description:
`lib/retro/session-metrics.mjs` contains three raw NUL (U+0000) bytes, at lines
394, 415 and 421. They are written literally into the source rather than as the
`\0` escape sequence.

## Impact

`file(1)` classifies the module as `data`, not text. Consequences:

- **grep silently returns nothing** instead of erroring. `grep -c "" lib/retro/session-metrics.mjs`
  exits 1 with no output, a pattern that matches every line of every readable file.
- **`git diff` renders it as binary**, so a reviewer of any change to this file sees
  no line-level diff.

The silent-grep behaviour is not theoretical. The identical defect in
`lib/extensions/exec-payload.mjs` manufactured a false security finding during the
extension-governance-merge-hardening build: an agent grepped for an import, got
nothing, and reported an unwired security guard (SEC-6a). The finding propagated
three hops before a node-based read disproved it. The import had been present the
whole time.

## Fix

Replace each literal NUL with the two-character escape `\0` inside its template
literal. The NUL-as-composite-key-separator idiom is fine and should be kept — the
runtime value is unchanged. This is exactly what commit `c8d57c0b` did for
`exec-payload.mjs`; verified there by `file` reporting UTF-8 text afterwards and
by diffing a NUL-normalised copy of the pre-fix file against the post-fix file.

## Scope

A sweep of all 2850 tracked source files (`*.mjs`, `*.js`, `*.json`, `*.md`) found
this to be the only remaining file with raw NULs.

## Worth considering alongside

A cheap guard would prevent recurrence: a test, or a pre-commit check, asserting no
tracked text-extension source file contains a NUL byte.

Found during the extension-governance-merge-hardening build, 2026-08-15. Out of
scope for that spec, hence filed separately.

title: Symlinked parent directory defeats the settings-write symlink guard (leaf-only lstat)
description:
`writeJson()` in providers/claude-code/adapter.mjs lstat-checks only the FINAL
path component. A symlinked PARENT directory is still followed.

DEMONSTRATED BY EXECUTION during /adev:review-specs re-review, against the real
public API (adapter.enable("project"), not a reconstruction):

  .claude -> ~/.claude   : enable("project") wrote the USER settings file while
                           reporting the project path. sameFile()'s realpathSync
                           correctly sees them as one file, so the project-scope
                           revoke no-ops and the entry stays. Result: a
                           PROJECT-scoped enable leaked into the user file —
                           silently defeating the exact consent boundary
                           installer-consent-boundary.spec.md exists to
                           establish, invisible in the installer output.

  .claude -> ~/.ssh      : no throw; ~/.ssh/settings.json clobbered with adev's
                           JSON. Arbitrary-directory write of a fixed-name file.

Squarely inside the spec's own stated threat model: "the clone is
attacker-controlled and the write happens before the operator has made any
trust decision". .claude/ is routinely tracked, and git tracks symlinks.

readJson() at adapter:190 reads through the same link before the write.

FIX DIRECTION
Validate the whole path, not the leaf: realpathSync the parent chain and require
the settings file to resolve under the intended root (process.cwd() for project
scope, getClaudeHome() for user scope). The pattern already exists in this repo
at lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs:57-66 and is tested in
tests/milestones-integration.test.mjs:196. Alternatively O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf
AND compare realpathSync(dirname(path)) to the expected root.

CWE-59 / CWE-22. Partial fix shipped in PR #274 (leaf only); AC-15 of
installer-consent-boundary.spec.md rev 2 records this as a known gap rather
than claiming the stronger property.

title: Chained git-hook wrapper fails open silently and embeds an absolute path; chaining guts tracked .githooks/ without warning
description:
Chained git-hook mode (`setupGitHooks()`, cli/index.mjs:385-473, wrapper generated by `buildChainedHook()` at cli/index.mjs:351-378) has three defects. It is reached whenever a project already has a foreign `core.hooksPath` (husky, lefthook, ...) at `adev install`/`adev upgrade` time — and it is the DEFAULT choice ("[1] Chain hooks", cli/index.mjs:402-406), so pressing Enter selects it.

Sibling of issue-uji735 (same install-flow area: the installer takes irreversible action ahead of, or instead of, the user's decision). Distinct defects — file separately, do not fold.

DEFECT A — the wrapper fails OPEN, silently.
buildChainedHook emits two guards:
  cli/index.mjs:361  if [ -x "$HOOK_DIR/<name>.adev" ]; then ... fi
  cli/index.mjs:371  if [ -x "$ORIGINAL" ]; then ... fi
  cli/index.mjs:376  exit 0
If either file is missing or merely loses its executable bit, the wrapper skips it and exits 0. No message, no non-zero exit. A hook that has been silently disabled is indistinguishable from a hook that passed.

What stops enforcing locally when this happens:
  - protected-branch blocking (commits straight to main)
  - conventional-commit-type validation
  - Author-type / Operator provenance trailer injection
  - the inline-Node policy check (pre-commit-no-inline-node)

Not hypothetical. Observed in this repo 2026-08-14: the `.githooks/*.adev` files were mode `-rw-r--r--` (NOT executable), which is exactly the state that triggers the silent skip — even though cli/index.mjs:438 chmods them 0o755 at write time. The exec bit does not survive every round trip (archive/restore, zip, some CI checkouts, Windows/WSL). The CI-side provenance gate would eventually catch missing trailers at PR time, but every local guard is already off by then.

Fix direction: a missing-or-non-executable `.adev`/original must be a loud failure (non-zero exit with a diagnostic naming the path and the fix), not a silent `exit 0`. If a fail-open escape hatch is wanted, it must be explicit and announced.

DEFECT B — the committed wrapper embeds a machine-specific absolute path.
cli/index.mjs:415  chainFromPath = resolve(cwd, existingHooksPath)   // absolute
cli/index.mjs:432  originalHookPath = join(chainFromPath, hookName)  // absolute
cli/index.mjs:370  the wrapper writes it literally: ORIGINAL="<absolute path>"

`.githooks/` is normally tracked, so that absolute path gets committed. On a teammate's machine or in CI the path does not exist, guard 371 fails, and (per Defect A) the wrapper exits 0 — so the project's ORIGINAL husky/lefthook hooks silently stop running for everyone except the person who ran the installer.

Fix direction: emit a repo-relative path resolved at run time from `$HOOK_DIR` / `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, never an absolute path from the installing machine.

DEFECT C — chaining mutates tracked files massively with no warning.
cli/index.mjs:437 copies the real hook body to `<name>.adev`; cli/index.mjs:445 then OVERWRITES the tracked `.githooks/<name>` with the ~26-line wrapper. In this repo that presented as 639 deleted lines across four tracked hooks (commit-msg -174, post-commit -169, pre-commit -133, prepare-commit-msg -210) plus four untracked `.adev` files.

The `created` array does report ".githooks/<name> (chained with <path>/<name>)", but nothing warns that tracked, committed files were just gutted. A user seeing that diff cannot easily distinguish it from repo corruption, and `git add -A` pushes stub hooks to the whole team.

Fix direction: warn explicitly that tracked hooks are being rewritten, show the scope, and state that `.adev` files must be committed alongside the wrapper (or gitignored) for chaining to work for anyone else.

SCOPE
- cli/index.mjs buildChainedHook() (351-378) — fail-closed guards, relative path resolution
- cli/index.mjs setupGitHooks() chaining branch (428-453) — user-facing warning about tracked-file rewrite
- Decide and document whether `.githooks/*.adev` is meant to be committed or gitignored; the answer determines whether Defect A is a portability bug or a local-only one
- Tests: wrapper behavior when .adev is absent, present-but-non-executable, and present-and-executable; assert non-zero exit + diagnostic for the first two
- Test: generated wrapper contains no absolute path

ACCEPTANCE
1. A missing or non-executable `.adev` hook causes a non-zero exit with a diagnostic naming the path — never a silent `exit 0`.
2. Same for a missing/non-executable chained original.
3. The generated wrapper contains no absolute filesystem path; chaining works from a fresh clone on a different machine.
4. Chaining prints an explicit warning that tracked hooks in `.githooks/` are being rewritten.
5. The commit/gitignore policy for `.adev` files is documented (docs/hooks.md) and enforced by the installer.
6. Tests cover all three guard states and the no-absolute-path invariant.

Found 2026-08-14 while diagnosing a working tree in which all four tracked hooks had been reduced to stubs with non-executable `.adev` siblings.
notes: Fix in PR #273 (fix/cli/hook-chaining), CI green, MERGEABLE CLEAN. All three defects reproduced before fixing and re-verified after: exec-bit loss and missing .adev now exit 1 with a diagnostic (was exit 0); a relocated clone runs both hooks (was silently skipping the original). AC-5 resolved per operator decision: .githooks/*.adev gitignored, wrapper stays tracked. 9 new tests; suite 5997 pass / 2 pre-existing mtime failures. Not closed until merged.
