title: Agent invoked /adev:work, then bypassed every lifecycle skill — nothing detected it
description:
An agent invoked /adev:work, executed its Step 1 state scan, and then abandoned
the skill and hand-rolled the rest of the work with raw tools. No lifecycle
skill was ever invoked; no lifecycle event was ever emitted. The framework was
loaded, read, and then ignored — silently, with nothing in the repo recording
that it had been.

This is a bug in the framework's enforcement surface, not only in one agent's
judgement: nothing at any point made the deviation visible or costly.

## Verbatim log of the deviation (2026-08-14 session)

The user invoked `/adev:work on the install ux bugs`. What followed:

1. DID run /adev:work Step 1 (state scan) — readExecutionState, coordination
   scan. Correctly surfaced concurrent PR #268.
2. DID run /adev:work Step 2/3 (classify + refine) — classified the work as
   bug-fix, checked source-manifest claims to decide whether specs were needed.
3. DID NOT complete Step 4/5 (propose route → await confirmation → INVOKE the
   target skill). Asked the user a scoping question via AskUserQuestion, got an
   answer, and then went straight to editing files.
4. /adev:specify — NOT invoked. Wrote
   .context-index/specs/features/cli/install-scope-consent.spec.md by hand with
   the Write tool, hand-authoring frontmatter copied from a sibling spec.
5. /adev:review-specs — NOT invoked. The spec is still status: draft. The agent
   explicitly told the user "the next step is /adev:review-specs", then did not
   run it and proceeded to implementation on a different issue.
6. /adev:plan, /adev:route — NOT invoked. No plan file, no .routing.json
   sidecar, no task decomposition for either issue.
7. /adev:write-test — NOT invoked. The agent hand-wrote
   tests/cli-hook-chaining.test.mjs and manually ran a RED phase (6 failing),
   imitating the shape of the skill without the skill's handoff block or
   gaming detection.
8. /adev:implement — NOT invoked. Edited cli/index.mjs directly.
9. /adev:issues claim — NOT invoked. Neither adev-plugin-sewt nor
   adev-plugin-ogjm was ever claimed, so the board never showed the work as
   in progress and a second agent could have collided.
10. `adev report --type step` — NEVER called, for any step. The lifecycle log
    has zero record of this work.

Consequences that actually landed:

- PR #271 shipped a real fix (lib/migrate-gate-commands.mjs, 10 tests, CI
  green) with NO lifecycle trace. Its Spec: trailer points at a spec that was
  hand-written and never reviewed.
- A spec artifact exists at status: draft that no reviewer has seen, and which
  the commit-msg hook nonetheless accepted as a valid trailer target.
- The half-applied sewt edit called `relative(cwd, originalHookPath)` in
  cli/index.mjs while `relative` is NOT imported there (line 4 imports only
  join, resolve, dirname). That is a runtime ReferenceError that /adev:implement's
  per-task review stage exists to catch. It was caught only because the user
  interrupted and asked whether the lifecycle skills were being used.

Note the irony: this same session merged PR #263, whose entire subject was
skills failing to emit step_failed events. The agent fixed the emission
instructions in five SKILL.md files, then emitted nothing itself.

## Why nothing caught it

- /adev:work's Step 5 ("Invoke Skill") is prose in a SKILL.md. There is no
  mechanism that notices the skill was read but its terminal step skipped.
- `adev gate require` only fires when a skill IS invoked. An agent that never
  invokes /adev:plan never trips the plan gate — the gate chain is
  opt-in by construction, so skipping the whole chain is frictionless while
  skipping one link is blocked.
- The commit-msg hook enforces that a Spec: trailer EXISTS and resolves to a
  file. It does not check that the spec passed review, or that any lifecycle
  step was recorded for it. A hand-written draft spec satisfies it fully.
- `adev coordination scan` reports other agents' claims, but nothing warns when
  THIS agent edits files for an issue it never claimed.

## Proposed acceptance

1. A skill whose SKILL.md declares a terminal invocation step (work Step 5,
   build's stage chain) records that it reached it. If /adev:work classifies
   work and then no target skill is invoked in the same turn, that is a
   detectable state — surface it.
2. `adev report --type step --status started` for step N with no terminal event
   and no subsequent step event is already an inconsistency the projection can
   see. Surface it in /adev:status and /adev:hygiene as "abandoned step",
   distinct from "in progress".
3. Consider whether the commit-msg hook should reject a Spec: trailer pointing
   at a spec with status: draft, or at minimum warn. A draft spec is by
   definition not an agreed contract.
4. Consider a hygiene pass: source files modified in a commit whose Spec:
   trailer names a spec that has no `plan` step in the lifecycle log — i.e.
   implementation that skipped planning.
5. Decide explicitly whether hand-authoring a lifecycle artifact (spec, plan)
   with Write instead of the owning skill is permitted. If it is not, the
   write-time diagnostic hook is the enforcement point. If it is, say so in
   CLAUDE.md so it stops being an unstated rule.

request, so the invocation surface can be improved rather than the incident
just corrected.

description:
Skills sit close to the 65536-byte FRONTMATTER_BYTE_LIMIT enforced by
lib/providers/copilot/skill-validator.mjs. Crossing it is not a soft
degradation: extractFrontmatterName() throws INVALID_SKILL_FRONTMATTER,
failing buildPlan() and taking down every Copilot adapter path — install,
uninstall, status, dry-run.

## Rescoped 2026-08-14 after PR #268

Most of this issue is now DONE. PR #268 (merged 2026-08-14) did the real
structural extraction that this issue asked for, on the worst offender:
skills/implement/SKILL.md dropped to 60526 bytes (5010 headroom) by moving
integration-gate.md and parallel-mode.md into conditional-loading companions,
alongside the failure-path-exit-event.md extracted in f62d3013.

It also shipped tests/skills/skill-size-cap.test.mjs, which supersedes the
skill-size-limit.test.mjs added in f62d3013 (removed in 73004422). The
surviving guard is better in two ways worth preserving if it is ever
rewritten: it recovers the cap BEHAVIOURALLY from the validator (feeding it
an oversized probe and parsing the limit out of the thrown error) rather than
duplicating `64 * 1024`, and it prints a warning for any skill above 90% of
cap instead of only failing at the boundary.

Current state on main:

| Skill     | Bytes | Headroom | % of cap |
|-----------|-------|----------|----------|
| build     | 64850 | 686      | 99%      |
| hygiene   | 62722 | 2814     | 96%      |
| implement | 60526 | 5010     | 92%      |
| specify   | 59963 | 5573     | 91%      |

## Remaining work

1. build/SKILL.md at 99% of cap is now the binding constraint — 686 bytes.
   Apply the same conditional-loading companion pattern #268 established.
2. hygiene at 96% is next.
3. Surface the cap as a documented authoring constraint (CLAUDE.md / docs/).
   It currently exists only as a constant inside a Copilot provider module,
   so an author editing a SKILL.md gets no signal until CI fails. The new
   test's 90% warning helps a reviewer, but only after the fact.

Note for whoever picks this up: extraction cannot be done by byte count
alone. tests/skills/step-failed-emission.test.mjs asserts on specific inline
phrases, so moving the wrong paragraph out of a skill body turns a size fix
into a test failure — that happened during the f62d3013 work.

Related: adev-plugin-gwq2 hoists 217 lines of Load Skill Extensions
boilerplate out of all 31 SKILL.md files. Different mechanism, but it would
reclaim ~7 lines per skill.

title: Subagent peer-message channel is broken: reviewer verdicts never reach their parent, agents stall, one dispatch arrived empty
description:
Throughout the governance-checks-unbundle build (2026-08-15) subagents could
not send messages to the agent that spawned them. Every attempt failed with
some variant of:

    No agent named 'general-purpose' is reachable

The verdicts those subagents produced were then delivered to the TOP-LEVEL
orchestrator instead of to their parent. The pipeline only completed because
the orchestrator hand-relayed them, nine or more times. Without a human-visible
orchestrator in the loop, this silently degrades review coverage.

Filed at P1 because it caused a real review layer to be skipped (see #4) and
because the safe outcome in #3 depended entirely on a subagent choosing
honesty over convenience.

## Concrete instances from this run

**1. Empty dispatch — ~96k tokens, zero work.**
A subagent labelled "Check 4 constitution compliance review" was spawned by the
`/adev:validate` step agent and received NO PROMPT AT ALL. Its entire output:

> "No task or user message is present yet — nothing to act on. I'll hold here
> until there's an actual request."

Usage: 96,058 tokens, 1 tool use, 6.8s. Check 4 is constitution compliance —
one of the two checks that mattered most on this spec, because its architecture
review was an operator override. Had the parent read that empty return as a
clean result, the check would have silently passed without running.

**2. Every per-task reviewer verdict in `/adev:implement` was misrouted.**
Across both specs (12 + 18 tasks), task implementers reported the same thing
verbatim, e.g.:

> "The reviewer session (`general-purpose`) is no longer reachable via
> SendMessage, so I'm reporting here for relay."
> "`ListAgents` isn't available in this session and the `general-purpose`
> address doesn't resolve."

Their findings reached the top-level orchestrator, which relayed them by hand.
Several were substantive and cross-task: a stale `planExecPayload` signature
that would otherwise have surfaced as an integration failure two tasks later; a
30-test red state; an unowned DoS lever.

**3. A plan agent was placed one step from reporting on a review it never got.**
The `/adev:plan` agent for `explicit-governance-registries` dispatched plan
revision 2 for re-review, and the verdict went to the orchestrator instead. The
agent stalled, then on being asked for its result said:

> "Reviewer verdict for revision 2 was never received. I am not reporting an
> approval I did not get. Treat the plan as reviewed-once-and-revised, not
> approved."

That is the correct behaviour and it is the only reason nothing was
misreported — but correctness here rested on the agent's judgement, not on the
mechanism. A less careful agent reports approval.

**4. Direct consequence: a plan shipped to implement UNREVIEWED.**
Because round-2's verdict never arrived, revision 3 was authored to close it and
no reviewer ever saw revision 3. An 18-task, 39-commit, 104-file implementation
ran against an unreviewed plan. Implement then found FIVE Design-Decision
premises false against the code — including one that would have hard-FAILed 31
of 247 specs. Those are exactly the defects a plan review exists to catch.

**5. Step agents went idle without returning their STEP_RESULT.**
The `/adev:implement` orchestrator for spec 1 completed its work and stopped
twice without emitting STEP_RESULT; the orchestrator had to resume it by message
to retrieve the result. Same for the spec-2 plan agent.

**6. Late verdicts, hours out of band.**
Spec 2's implement reported: "Two verdicts never arrived (Task 3 Stage 1 arrived
very late, Task 8 Stage 1 late, Task 9 Stage 2 ~3h late)."

## Impact

- Review coverage silently degrades. The pipeline reports success while a
  review layer did not run.
- Wasted spend: the empty dispatch alone burned ~96k tokens.
- Wall-clock inflation from stalls and re-dispatch. NOTE: this confounds the
  timing evidence in the TDD-cycle research issue
  (`adev-plugin-tdd-cycle-simplification-xprl`) — the two must be separated
  before drawing conclusions about methodology cost.
- Correctness currently depends on subagents volunteering that they never
  received a verdict.

## Questions for the fix

1. Why does `general-purpose` not resolve from a child back to its parent? Is
   the parent's address only valid while it holds an active task?
2. Why did one dispatch arrive with an empty prompt? Prompt loss on dispatch is
   a distinct and more severe failure than reply-path loss.
3. Should a parent agent be structurally unable to record a review verdict it
   never received — i.e. absence of a verdict fails closed rather than being
   left to the agent's discretion?
4. Should step agents emit STEP_RESULT on completion rather than requiring the
   caller to prompt for it?

## Repro context

Session ran `/adev:build --resume` across two cross-cutting specs in a git
worktree at `.adev/worktrees/governance-checks-unbundle`. Subagents dispatched
via the `Agent` tool with `run_in_background: false` (the harness backgrounded
them regardless). Nested reviewers were spawned by the adev skills themselves.

title: Sub-skills stall waiting on their own dispatched children (no STEP_RESULT returned)
description:
## Symptom

`/adev:plan` and `/adev:implement` each **ended a turn without returning a `STEP_RESULT`**, having dispatched work and then waited for it:

> "That review is running in the background — I'll finalize the plan … once it comes back."

> "I'll wait for the fix commit notification rather than polling further."

Neither came back. A subagent that yields has ended its turn — nothing wakes it. The orchestrator cannot record or advance without a `STEP_RESULT`, so the pipeline sat blocked until the operator noticed and messaged each sub-skill to finish.

**Cost:** ~229k tokens across the plan agent's two turns, ~304k across implement's three.

## Root cause: two rules, only one written down

`skills/build/SKILL.md:110` already documents this failure and even labels it *field-observed*:

> "…inside a nested subagent context it does not re-invoke the caller, so a backgrounded dispatch stalls the pipeline (field-observed as build steps that auto-background and never return a STEP_RESULT)."

But that rule is scoped to the **orchestrator → sub-skill** hop. The stall happened on the **sub-skill → grandchild** hop.

More precisely: **"don't background a dispatch" and "don't end your turn waiting on one" are two different rules, and only the first is written anywhere.** `/adev:implement` carries the first rule (`skills/implement/SKILL.md:468,470`) and stalled twice anyway — it obeyed the dispatch rule, then waited.

## Verified coverage gap

`run_in_background` occurrences per skill (measured):

| Skill | Occurrences |
|---|---|
| build | 9 |
| implement | 2 |
| review-specs | 2 |
| **plan** | **0** |

`/adev:plan` dispatches a plan-reviewer at `skills/plan/SKILL.md:750` and re-dispatches at `:779`, carrying **no instruction about background dispatch at all**.

Repo-wide grep for turn-ending guidance — `end your turn`, `ending your turn`, `do not end`, `await the notification`, `wait for the notification` — matches **zero lines in any `skills/*/SKILL.md`**. The second rule genuinely does not exist in the corpus.

## Contributing structural issue

The `STEP_RESULT` protocol is defined **only** in `skills/build/SKILL.md` (sole file matching `STEP_RESULT`). Sub-skills are required to emit it but do not carry its definition or its completion contract, so nothing local to `plan` or `implement` tells them that ending a turn without one is a protocol violation.

## Adjacent defect found while verifying

`skills/plan/SKILL.md:754` and `skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md:477` both instruct `Task tool (general-purpose):`. The tool is `Agent`, not `Task`. Stale naming in the exact dispatch block that stalled — worth fixing in the same pass, though it is not the cause.

## Fix direction (not a design decision — for the spec to settle)

1. State the second rule explicitly wherever a skill dispatches: *a dispatching skill must not end its turn until it has a result to report; if a dispatch returns a task ID, that is a bug in the dispatch, not something to wait on.*
2. Give `/adev:plan` the dispatch rule it is missing entirely.
3. Decide whether both rules belong in a single shared fragment included by every dispatching skill, rather than being restated per-skill at four different levels of completeness — the current drift (9 / 2 / 2 / 0) is what produced the gap.
4. Consider whether the `STEP_RESULT` completion contract should live somewhere sub-skills actually read.

Coverage should be enforced by a test, in the manner of `tests/skills-extension-coverage.test.mjs`: every SKILL.md that dispatches must carry both rules.

title: Research: can the per-task TDD + 2-stage-review cycle be simplified? It dominates implement wall-clock
description:
`/adev:implement` runs a full TDD loop plus a 2-stage review for every plan
task. It works — it catches real defects — but it is the dominant cost of a
build, and the evidence below suggests the cycle is doing more rounds than
the defect yield justifies. Research whether it can be simplified or
graduated without losing the catches.

## Measured evidence — governance-checks-unbundle, 2026-08-15

Two specs built end to end on one branch, same session.

| | spec 1 (hardening) | spec 2 (registries) |
|---|---|---|
| Plan tasks | 12 | 18 |
| Implement commits | 29 | 39 |
| First-pass commits | 12 | 19 |
| **Review-fix rounds** | **17** | **20** |
| Implement wall-clock | ~2h 40m | **6h 39m** |
| Per task | ~13 min | ~22 min |

**More than half of all commits are review-fix rounds** (17 of 29, 20 of 39).
Several tasks needed 3-4 commits to land: spec 2's tasks 9, 11 took three and
task 18 took four. Spec 1 showed the same shape.

Tests grew 6047 -> 6425 (+378) across spec 2's 18 tasks.

## Why this is worth researching rather than just cutting

The reviews are NOT noise. In this same run they caught:

- a boundary evaluator that silently DROPPED a file at a chunk boundary and
  charged it a false timeout (Critical)
- a fail-open where a disabled required gate made a transition PASS
- a `String(manifest_sha)` coercion that would have made every gate outcome
  permanently stale
- an install-time consent prompt that was fully built and never wired —
  invisible to every test, because consent tests injected `promptFn` directly
  and CLI tests only covered the flag path

That last one is the strongest argument for keeping a review layer: no amount
of TDD would have found it, since the tests and the defect shared a blind spot.

So the question is not "drop review" but "why does it take 2+ rounds per task,
and which rounds actually find things".

## Questions to answer

1. **Round yield.** Across recent builds, what fraction of Stage-2 (and later)
   review rounds produce a Critical or Important finding versus bookkeeping?
   If late rounds mostly find cosmetics, cap them.
2. **Can rigor be graduated per task?** `/adev:route` already scores every task
   on four dimensions and this run produced 3 auto-agent / 15 assisted-agent.
   The auto-agent tasks (fully specified, single module, additive) may not need
   two review stages. Routing data already exists to make that call and is not
   currently used to modulate review depth.
3. **Is the RED step earning its cost everywhere?** Several tasks in this run
   had a RED phase that was mechanical. Distinguish tasks where a failing test
   genuinely constrains the design from those where it is ceremony.
4. **Are review rounds re-litigating plan defects?** A recurring pattern here:
   the plan asserted something false about the code, the implementer discovered
   it, and a review round was spent correcting course. Spec 2 had five DDR
   premises turn out false against the code. Cheaper plan verification might
   remove review rounds downstream.
5. **Batching.** Would reviewing a coherent GROUP of tasks once beat reviewing
   each task twice? Dependencies are already grouped in the plan.
6. **What does the 2-stage split buy?** Measure whether Stage 1 and Stage 2 find
   different defect classes or the same ones twice.

## Confound to control for

Review verdicts in this session frequently failed to reach their parent agent
("no agent named 'general-purpose' is reachable"), causing stalls and re-dispatch.
Some wall-clock here is that harness defect, not the methodology. Separate the two
before drawing conclusions — otherwise the cycle looks more expensive than it is.

## Suggested output

A recommendation on graduating review depth by routing score, with the round-yield
data behind it. If the data supports it, a concrete rule (e.g. auto-agent tasks get
one review stage; assisted-agent keeps two; any task with a Critical finding earns
another round).

Filed from the governance-checks-unbundle build, where the user observed the cycle
"taking too long in many cases".
notes:
SCOPED AS A SPIKE 2026-08-17, re-parented to adev-plugin-04jr (Token Cost & Measurement).

This issue is a RESEARCH SPIKE and should close on ANSWERING the question, then SPAWN a separate implementation issue shaped by what it finds. As written it bundles "research whether X is possible" with "change X", which cannot be closed cleanly — you would close it having only answered the question, or leave it open through an implementation whose shape was unknown when it was filed.

I deliberately did NOT pre-create the implementation issue. Its scope depends entirely on the research outcome, and a placeholder for work of unknown shape is worse than no issue: it invites someone to implement before the question is answered.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-COMPLEXITY ITEM IN THE EPIC:
- It targets /adev:implement, the most load-bearing skill in the framework.
- Its own text concedes "It works — it catches real defects." So the risk is not that simplification fails, it is that it succeeds at lower cost while silently losing catches. That failure mode is invisible without a defect-yield-per-round measurement.
- Measuring defect yield per round needs working instrumentation (adev-plugin-882a.1) and probably an eval harness, so it sits at the END of the epic dependency chain, not the start.
- There is no crisp success criterion yet. "Simplify without losing the catches" is not falsifiable until "the catches" are enumerated and counted.

EVIDENCE THIS SESSION ADDS, unprompted and worth folding into the spike:
The implement step ran 10 tasks and produced 11 commits with per-task TDD and 2-stage review. The review stages CAUGHT REAL DEFECTS that would otherwise have shipped:
  - Task 6 shipped a claim that CONTEXT_PACK_DENYLIST_MATCH was unreachable dead code. It is reachable — a trailing-slash enumerated include evades the raw-glob regex while expandGlob still resolves the file. The reviewer reproduced it three ways. That false claim was unpinned and is now positive tests.
  - Two further Important findings were caught and fixed the same way in Tasks 1 and 14 (an assertion that would have been vacuous, and a missing load guardrail).
So on this sample the 2-stage review earned its cost at least three times in ten tasks. Any simplification proposal must account for that yield, and this is exactly the kind of data the spike needs more of.

METHOD NOTE that muddies this sample, recorded for honesty: the implement orchestrator BATCHED subagent dispatches (tasks 2+3, 5+6, 7+10, 11+14) rather than one per task, and ran both review stages in a single dispatch for the lower-risk batches. Task 4 alone got separate Stage 1 and Stage 2 dispatches. So this run is NOT a clean measurement of the documented per-task cycle cost — it is already a partially simplified variant, and it still caught three defects. Worth treating as weak evidence that some batching is safe, not as a measurement of the full cycle.

title: Cut test file count at constant coverage — Lever 3 done (536→508); Levers 1&2 need manual migration, not scripting
description:
Cut the size of the test suite. The suite is 468 files / 5,888 cases / 99,052 LOC against 182
source modules under `lib/` + `cli/` + `hooks/` — 2.6 suites per module, 16.8 LOC per case.

Per-behavior test granularity, the original framing of this issue, is **not** the lever. It is a
planning-time routing rule that decides which file a *new* task's tests land in; it deletes
nothing. Measured on this repo it would produce *more* suites than the 305 currently declared,
because specs average 10.9 behaviors against 5.2 test-bearing tasks per plan. It survives here as
a two-line footnote (see "Folded in" at the bottom), not as the objective.

## Triage method

Every `it()`/`test()` body in all 468 files was extracted by brace matching and classified by what
it actually exercises — not by filename or by whole-file heuristics, which over-credit a file as
"prose" when only some of its cases are. Case-level breakdown of 5,888 cases:

| Class | Cases | % | Files touched |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BEHAVIOR_UNIT` — calls a function imported from repo source | 3,001 | 51.0% | 239 |
| `OTHER` — calls a locally-defined helper; mixed | 1,551 | 26.3% | 211 |
| `BEHAVIOR_SUBPROCESS` — spawns the CLI or a hook | 630 | 10.7% | 87 |
| `PROSE_CONTAINMENT` — reads a repo file, asserts a substring | 484 | 8.2% | 85 |
| `ARTIFACT_STRUCTURAL` — reads a repo file, asserts shape | 170 | 2.9% | 78 |
| `MIXED_ARTIFACT` | 52 | 0.9% | 39 |

**706 cases (12%) assert on the text of a repo artifact rather than on behavior.** That is the
reduction target. The 4,181 behavior cases are not in scope.

## Lever 1 — pure-artifact files: 54 files, 436 cases, 5,489 LOC

Files where *every* case reads a repo file and asserts on its contents. The pattern is one `it()`
per substring, each re-reading the same file:

- `tests/skills/research.test.mjs` — 48 cases, each `readFileSync(prompt).includes("…")` for one
  token (`"1,500"`, `"attribution"`, `"Before Finalizing"`). One behavior — "the researcher prompt
  declares its required contract fields" — sharded 48 ways.
- `tests/docs/workflow-guides.test.mjs` — 40 cases, each re-reading `docs/design-phase.md` to
  assert it mentions one skill name.
- `tests/docs/foundation-onboarding.test.mjs` (26), `tests/docs/reference-section.test.mjs` (26),
  `tests/skills/document.test.mjs` (21), `tests/skills/assess.test.mjs` (15),
  `tests/skills/codehealth.test.mjs` (15), `tests/skills/plan-infra-requirements.test.mjs` (10).

These fail on rewording and pass on broken behavior. Replaced by declarative contract tables — one
row per artifact, one parameterized suite per artifact class (SKILL.md, prompts, docs, templates,
providers) — this collapses to roughly **6 files / 55 cases / 600 LOC**.

**Δ −48 files, −381 cases, −4,900 LOC.**

## Lever 2 — scattered artifact cases inside behavior files: 270 cases, 72 files, 4,087 LOC

Same assertion style, living in files that also hold real behavior cases. The files survive; the
artifact cases fold into Lever 1's tables.

**Δ −230 cases, −3,500 LOC, 0 files.**

## Lever 3 — tiny suites: 46 files, 104 cases, 4,559 LOC

Suites with ≤3 cases that are not already counted in Lever 1 — 44 LOC of scaffolding per case. The
suite makes 2,297 setup/teardown calls in total and this is where that mass concentrates. Includes
5 filename-stem clusters where one subject was split one-concern-per-file:
`json-adapter.{atomic,concurrent,parity,perf,schema-version}`,
`migrate-state-artifacts.{collision,constitution,containment,idempotency,redaction}`,
`render-markdown.{atomic,escape,roundtrip}`, `lifecycle-state.render`, `specify-amend.integration`.
Merging into subject-anchored siblings moves cases rather than deleting them.

**Δ −35 files, 0 cases, −1,500 LOC.**

## Projected result

| | Now | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Files | 468 | ~385 | **−18%** |
| Cases | 5,888 | ~5,280 | **−10%** |
| LOC | 99,052 | ~89,000 | **−10%** |

Not the 25%/15% quoted earlier in the session — that figure came from a whole-file classifier that
credited entire files as prose when only some cases were. Case-level triage is the honest number.

## Hard constraint: replacement lands before deletion

This repo's deliverable *is* markdown — skills, prompts, templates. The 706 artifact cases are weak
signal, not zero signal; they are the only thing checking that a SKILL.md declares its required
sections. Deleting them without the schema-driven replacement in place trades 706 weak tests for no
tests. Sequence is: build the contract tables → verify they catch what the old suites caught (run
both, diff the failures against deliberately broken artifacts) → then delete.

## Explicitly out of scope

- The 4,181 behavior cases (`BEHAVIOR_UNIT` + `BEHAVIOR_SUBPROCESS`).
- The 630 subprocess cases in `tests/cli/**` and `tests/hooks/**` — verified as real behavior
  (temp-dir fixtures, `runHook()`, spawned CLI), e.g. `tests/hooks/merge-guard.test.mjs`.
- 60 duplicated case titles / 84 redundant instances — only 1.4% of cases; not worth a pass.
- Wholesale reorganization of the 383 files that stay.

## Folded in from the original granularity framing

1. Declare `test_policy.granularity: per-behavior` in `manifest.yaml`. It resolves today from
   `granularity_source: "fallback"` — an undeclared default is one release away from silently
   changing under the project.
2. Correct `docs/test-strategies.md:220`, which tells adopters that `per-behavior` yields "fewer
   test files." Measured here it yields more. The doc should state what the rule actually buys —
   suite membership derivable from the spec instead of from task authorship.

## Provenance note

Of 499 historical test-file additions, only 104 carry a `Spec:` trailer and none carries a behavior
link, so no behavior-anchored regroup of the surviving suite is mechanically derivable. That is a
separate concern from reduction and is not addressed here.

## Full study

Method, per-project measurement table, case-level triage, and the reproduction scripts are recorded in `.context-index/research/test-suite-size-oss-benchmark.md` (branch `adev/research-test-suite-benchmark`, commit 9102fc5a).

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## Re-measured 2026-08-18 — Lever 1 does not hold; Lever 3 landed
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

### Baseline moved
536 files / 7,138 cases / 124,408 LOC / 206 source modules (was 468 / 5,888 /
99,052 / 182 at filing). The study's classifier was re-run and reproduced within
1 percentage point on every class, so the method is sound — only the corpus grew.

### Finding 1 — the artifact-case count was UNDER-stated
The triage classifier only caught cases whose body calls readFileSync directly.
Files reading through a local helper (`const readSkill = () => readFileSync(...)`)
landed in OTHER — 26.6% of cases, never analysed as a lever. Union of genuinely
pure-artifact files is 87, not 55: 730 cases, 8,596 LOC. So the reduction target
was larger than filed.

### Finding 2 — but it is NOT mechanically extractable, which is what matters
The hard constraint is replacement-before-deletion. Whether the contract tables
can be EXTRACTED (rather than hand-written) decides whether this is a scripted
change or a 700-assertion manual migration. Measured, each layer of rigor roughly
halves the set:

  87 files  look like pure artifact tests
  42 files  every assertion mechanically liftable   (87.2% assertion fidelity)
  15 files  artifact target also unambiguously resolvable

The extractor was iterated three times (71.3% -> 87.2%). The residue is not weak
parsing — it is real logic: cross-referencing FIELD_ALLOWLIST against a docs
table, collecting `violations` arrays and asserting empty, doesNotMatch/negative
assertions, set-size comparisons. Those are genuine consistency checks and should
STAY as code; they are not 'one it() per substring'.

So Lever 1's premise — 48 files collapse to 6 — holds for ~15 files (-2.6%), not
48. The rest is a hand migration of ~700 assertions, which is exactly where the
silent coverage loss this issue names as the undetectable failure mode would
enter. NOT attempted.

This issue has now inverted under measurement three times: per-behavior
granularity (yields more suites), the artifact-case undercount, and now the
mechanisation premise. Treat any remaining projection here as provisional.

### Lever 3 — DONE, landed at constant coverage
536 -> 508 files (-28). Suite total unchanged at 7,179 tests / 970 suites, which
is the constant-coverage proof: identical case count, 28 fewer files. Merging
moves cases verbatim, so no assertion was rewritten.

Merged: render-markdown 4->1, json-adapter(lib) 6->1, migrate-state-artifacts
6->1, json-adapter-cas 6->1, beads-adapter 3->1, json-adapter-internals 3->1,
lifecycle-state 3->1, plus four 2->1 merges.

Three candidates were reverted rather than forced: execution-state and
context-pack fail when combined (shared fixture state), and one
migrate-state-artifacts sibling imports assert from node:assert while the rest
use node:assert/strict — merging those flavors under one binding would silently
switch assert.equal between loose and strict.

Mechanism note for whoever continues: 'git checkout --' restores from the INDEX,
so a merge written to the working tree but not staged is silently undone by a
later revert. That happened here and cost 18 cases; caught by diffing the suite
total against baseline, not by the per-family check. Stage each merge before
attempting the next.

### Folded-in items
1. test_policy.granularity — ALREADY DONE and STALE in this issue. It is declared
   at manifest.yaml:175 and 'adev test-policy show --json' reports
   granularity_source: manifest, not fallback. Nothing to do.
2. docs/test-strategies.md — DONE. Corrected to state what per-behavior actually
   buys (suite membership derivable from the spec) and to name the ratio that
   decides file-count direction, rather than asserting a direction.

### Recommended repricing
What remains is Lever 1 + Lever 2 as a MANUAL migration (~700 assertions across
72 files), plus the ~15-file mechanical slice as an optional proof-of-pattern.
That is a different shape of work from what this issue was filed as and should
probably be split. The remaining tiny-suite merges (25 of the 55 had no
same-subject sibling) are also unaddressed.

title: Auto-recover from stale tasks.json.lock (orphan-lock cleanup)
description:
The CAS layer in lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs acquires tasks.json.lock via O_EXCL before each write and releases it in the finally block. If the process is killed mid-write (SIGKILL, OS crash, container OOM), the lock file persists. Every subsequent CAS mutator then hits EEXIST → STALE_BOARD_WRITE_RETRY → bounded retry → STALE_BOARD_WRITE. The issue board becomes effectively read-only until someone manually deletes the orphan lock. The error message does not mention the lock file, making the failure hard to debug.

.gitignore now excludes the lock file (committed in ba44d3b on the concurrent-write-protection branch) so it cannot propagate via git, but in-place developer environments still need recovery.

Proposed mitigation: when _write encounters EEXIST on the lock acquire, stat the existing lock file. If its mtime is older than a configurable threshold (default 30 seconds; override via manifest.tasks.cas_lock_stale_seconds), treat it as orphaned, unlink it, and retry the acquire (without consuming a CAS retry budget slot). Log a one-time warning on the recovery path so users notice if it happens repeatedly.

Surfaced 2026-05-17 during PR review of concurrent-write-protection. Filed at user direction as a follow-up; not in scope for the original spec.; Closed: [object Object]

title: Author docs/cli-reference.md — agent-facing CLI verb reference for all 24 verbs
description:
## Problem

`adev help` shows 5 of 24 CLI verbs. The remaining 19 (gate, report, build-state, partial, heuristics, source-manifest, domain, context, verify, state, execution-state, preflight, prototype, artifact, issues, diagnose, etc.) are referenced only in scattered SKILL.md prose. Agents looking for verb signatures or argument shapes have to (a) grep `cli/index.mjs` for the dispatch table, (b) read multiple SKILL.md files, or (c) run `node cli/index.mjs <verb> --help` against guesses. None of these is a usable discovery surface.

Confirmed by a session audit (2026-05-20): the agent-load path (SessionStart hook → using-adev SKILL.md → CLAUDE.md → Context Routing table) contains zero pointers to a CLI verb reference. `docs/skill-reference.md` exists for the /adev:* skills but there is no equivalent for the underlying CLI verbs.

## Recommended fix

Create `docs/cli-reference.md` mirroring the format and tone of `docs/skill-reference.md`. One section per CLI verb, grouped by audience.

## Scope

1. New file `docs/cli-reference.md` with two top-level sections:
   - **User-facing verbs** (5): `install`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`, `extension`, `migrate`. These are the public surface invoked via `npx @adev-org/adev-cli <verb>`.
   - **Lifecycle / internal verbs** (~19): `gate`, `report`, `build-state`, `partial`, `heuristics`, `source-manifest`, `domain`, `context`, `verify`, `state`, `execution-state`, `preflight`, `prototype`, `artifact`, `issues`, `diagnose`, `init`, `status`, `help`. These are invoked from SKILL.md prose and by other CLI verbs; agents need them for orchestration.
2. Per-verb entry format: one-line description, full argument signature (flags + types + defaults), one example invocation, link to implementing module (`lib/cli/<verb>.mjs` or anchor in `cli/index.mjs`), cross-references to relevant SKILL.md files that invoke it.
3. Add `docs/cli-reference.md` to `docs/README.md` under the Reference section (next to `skill-reference.md`).
4. Update the `using-adev` SKILL.md's existing reference to drop the 'when present' qualifier once the file lands.
5. Tests: optionally add a script-based check that every verb in the `cli/index.mjs` dispatch table has a corresponding section in `docs/cli-reference.md` (drift guard). Can ship as a v2 follow-on.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/cli-reference.md` exists and documents all 24 verbs currently registered in `cli/index.mjs`.
- Each verb has: one-line description, full argument signature, at least one example, link to implementing file.
- Verbs are grouped into user-facing vs lifecycle/internal sections.
- `docs/README.md` lists the new file under Reference.
- `skills/using-adev/SKILL.md` qualification ('when present') is removed.
- Spot-check: an agent asked about a specific verb (e.g., `adev partial`) should be able to answer from the new doc without reading source.

## References

- Session audit that surfaced this gap: this session's analysis of agent doc entrypoints (2026-05-20)
- Existing per-skill reference: `docs/skill-reference.md`
- CLI dispatch table source: `cli/index.mjs:1424-1450` (verb registry)
- Per-verb implementations: `lib/cli/*.mjs`
- Constitution Context Routing update: this session's edit to `.context-index/constitution.md` (added `docs/*.md` row) — landed on branch `feat/domain-extensions/init-extension-picker`.; Closed: Authored docs/cli-reference.md documenting all 29 CLI verbs (8 user-facing + 21 lifecycle), grouped by audience with signatures/examples/impl links/cross-refs; wired into docs/README.md; dropped the when-present qualifier in constitution, CLAUDE.md, and using-adev.

title: Correct harness-simplification-study: adev/frontmatter-present is an error-severity diagnostic reporting real violations, not overhead
description:
Found by consistency-analyzer (blocker_id consistency-analyzer:diagnostic-rename:59671228). The study listed the diagnostic as pure overhead based on 52% event volume. In fact lib/diagnostics/tier1/frontmatter-present.mjs returns {fired:false} for well-formed frontmatter and fires only on missing/malformed at severity error — the volume is 130 of 201 spec files genuinely violating the first-non-blank-line rule, already tracked by issue #3448 with a reconciliation spec as the designated fix. Study section "Part 2 / pure overhead" needs correcting; measurement-integrity Behavior 4 should be dropped or re-scoped.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-08-12): Root cause verified 2026-08-12. lib/diagnostics/tier1/frontmatter-present.mjs rejects any markdown body before the --- delimiter ("a markdown body (e.g. a leading # heading) before --- is rejected"). Natural experiment confirming causation: the 4 charter templates start with --- and 0 of 47 .charter.md files violate; the 6 spec templates start with an H1 and 128 of 235 .spec.md files violate. Full corpus scan by artifact kind (the 4 kinds the diagnostic covers): .charter.md 0/47, .spec.md 128/235, .review.md 153/203, .validate.md 122/123 — roughly 400 violating artifacts, which is what produces the ~52% event share. Reviews and validates have NO template; they are written by lib/cli/artifact.mjs and by skill prose that never specifies frontmatter position, so that half needs a writer fix rather than a template fix. Safety check: tests/templates/spec-template.behavioral.test.mjs only does substring includes() assertions (infra_requirements + security note) — nothing asserts ordering, so reordering the template does not break it. Remediation split into epic-104 (issue-585, issue-586, issue-587). title: End-to-end test-depth enforcement: verify authored suites match their assigned depth
description: Descoped from test-depth-policy at revision 6 (see its Scope Boundary section). That spec assigns and records a depth per task; nothing verifies the authored suite matches it. Round-5 review established why enforcement could not be bolted on, all verified against code: (1) write-handoff.mjs:43-46 hashes test file CONTENTS only, so any depth field added to Handoff Block frontmatter is unattested and written by the same subagent being checked — structurally identical to the existing self-reported gaming_check: passed. (2) "Case classes actually covered" has no machine-decidable definition; lib/test-strategies/gaming.mjs is depth-invariant by design so nothing computes it. (3) Packets are keyed on a spec-derived slug and overwritten each RED run (immutable-handoff-block.spec.md:37,41), so under the shipped per-behavior default N tasks share one packet and a later task destroys an earlier record. (4) A git-diff check cannot run at suite acceptance: that point is RED-complete so the source edits happen later in GREEN, and git diff --name-only cannot see the untracked files a Create: task produces. Doing this properly requires: amending immutable-handoff-block.spec.md (per spec-amendment-artifacts.spec.md) for packet keying and content; giving conformance evidence a per-task key; relocating the check to task-commit time against a pinned base plus git ls-files -o; and deciding whether raising a shared suite is permitted given the hash lock. Also unresolved and belonging here: nothing enforces that assert-assigned is called at all (under /adev:implement --parallel, group subagents run the TDD loop from prose inside worktrees), and depth is not reconciled across tasks sharing a suite. || DESIGN DECISION (human, 2026-08-13): shared suites ARE permitted; packets get re-keyed per task. Amend immutable-handoff-block.spec.md so packet keys are task-scoped (not spec-slug-scoped) and conformance evidence is per-task, replacing the current one-packet-per-spec-slug scheme. This (a) unblocks issue-614's 'prefer extending an existing suite' guidance, which the content-hash lock otherwise makes unworkable, and (b) fixes the existing bug where N tasks sharing a spec slug overwrite one another's packet (immutable-handoff-block.spec.md:37,41). Rejected alternatives: keeping one-suite-per-task and making plan tasks coarser (leaves the packet-overwrite bug, fights natural per-module test grouping); and specing 559 as detection-only (sidesteps the hash question but leaves depth unenforced, contradicting the audit's core lesson that prose does not bind — only deterministic gates do). issue-559 and issue-614 should be designed and implemented as ONE effort.

title: Skill Integration — Infrastructure Preflight
adev pr body: roll commit trailers up into a spec-scoped provenance table
description:
Every commit carries Spec:, Plan-task:, Issue:, Author-type:, Operator: trailers (manifest.yaml:168-178) and CI validates them per-commit — but nothing rolls them up, so a reviewer opening a 50-file PR gets no map of which hunks trace to which spec.

Aggregate over data that already exists: group commits by Spec:, show Plan-task: coverage, flag any commit lacking Spec:. Converts a large diff into a handful of spec-scoped reading units. Foundation for the routing-map and validate-verdict issues. Research: .context-index/research/pr-review-experience.md rec 2.

--- Forge-neutrality constraint (2026-08-12) ---
MUST emit markdown to stdout and know nothing about any forge. Its inputs (commit trailers, <spec>.routing.json, the validate report) are adev artifacts that exist in every adev project by construction, so the content layer is 100% provider-agnostic — it works on GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, Forgejo, a bare remote, or email-a-patch with zero changes. Whoever pipes stdout into a forge is a separate, project-specific concern.

Do NOT build a forge adapter as part of this issue. When adev is first run against a non-GitHub forge, add a registry following lib/issues/registry.mjs (json/file/beads -> adapter, graceful fallback when the binary is missing), which itself follows lib/provider/registry.mjs. NAMING TRAP: do not call the knob `provider` — that word already means agent harness (claude-code / opencode / codex / cursor / copilot) in lib/provider/registry.mjs. Use `forge:` or `completion.forge:`.

Note also that lib/milestones.mjs's `execGh` is NOT a portability seam despite appearances: it is named for gh and passes gh-shaped argv (["pr","list","--head",...]), so it is a test injection point only. A real adapter needs semantic verbs (postReviewComment(id, body)), not argv passthrough.

--- Depends on issue-588 (wired 2026-08-12) ---
.githooks/post-commit is the hook that emits the Spec:/Plan-task:/Author-type:/Operator: trailers issue-597 aggregates. The session-capture installer currently corrupts it (sentinel wrapper leaves a dangling `if`, bash syntax error at line 43), so commits made through a corrupted hook may carry no trailers at all. Fix the emitter before building the aggregator on top of it.

--- Constraint from issue-582 (NOT a blocking dep) ---
issue-582 (Spec: trailer -> node -e command injection) is marked in_progress on the board but the fix ALREADY LANDED on main via PR #214: .githooks/post-commit:61 now exports ADEV_PC_SPECS_TOUCHED and lib/session-summary.mjs reads env.ADEV_PC_SPECS_TOUCHED — no JS interpolation. No blocking dep added because the work is done; the board status is stale.

CONSTRAINT THAT SURVIVES: issue-582 also observed that the trailer value is emitted into YAML frontmatter UNQUOTED, so a Spec: value containing ] , or a newline corrupts downstream frontmatter parsing. issue-597 consumes the same trailers — it MUST reuse the sanitized path and quote on output, never re-parse raw git trailer text.

title: Measure workflow-backed hygiene against the serial baseline before generalizing
description:
Run both hygiene paths on this repo and decide, on evidence, whether the workflow substrate generalizes to other skills.

## Measure

| Dimension | How |
|---|---|
| Wall-clock | serial vs `--workflow` on the same commit |
| Token spend | orchestrator + all subagents, both paths |
| Finding count | overlap, workflow-only, serial-only |
| Finding quality | false-positive rate after the adversarial verify pass |
| Failure behavior | kill a subagent mid-run; confirm `null` handling and no partial report is written |

## Decision output

Append the result to the research artifact and either:
- **Generalize** — open follow-up issues for `/adev:review-specs`, `/adev:research`, `/adev:codehealth`; or
- **Hold** — keep the flag experimental and record why in the artifact; or
- **Revert** — remove the flag, keep `adev hygiene passes --json` (useful regardless).

Explicitly out of scope for this decision: `/adev:implement --parallel`. That needs its own design issue about who owns worktrees, adev or the harness.

title: adev hygiene passes --json: expose the audit pass list as a work-list
description:
Add a CLI verb that emits the hygiene audit passes as structured JSON, so an orchestrator (workflow or otherwise) can fan out over them without re-deriving the list from SKILL prose.

## Shape

```
adev hygiene passes [--json]
→ { passes: [ { id, title, scope, reads: [...], severity_floor } ] }
```

## Why

`skills/hygiene/SKILL.md` is ~1263 lines describing 23 audit passes walked in a single context that degrades as it fills. The pass list is data, not prose. Extracting it:

- is useful on its own (a real work-list for any orchestration strategy, serial included);
- is the `args` payload for the hygiene workflow prototype, since workflow scripts have no filesystem access and cannot read the SKILL or the repo themselves;
- keeps the deterministic half in `lib/hygiene/` where it belongs.

## Scope

- `lib/cli/hygiene.mjs` (or extend the existing surface) + `lib/hygiene/passes.mjs` as the single source of truth for the pass list.
- SKILL.md prose references the verb rather than restating the list, per cli-driver-surface.
- Tests covering the JSON contract and drift between the emitted list and the SKILL's documented passes.

title: Prototype: /adev:hygiene --workflow (opt-in workflow-backed audit)
description:
Ship an opt-in `--workflow` flag on `/adev:hygiene` backed by a workflow script, with the serial path unchanged as the default.

## Why hygiene first

It is the strongest candidate and the safest: 23 read-only audit passes, no state writes during the fan-out, no gate inside the loop, and no worktree ownership question. Whatever we learn transfers to `/adev:review-specs` and `/adev:research` without risking `/adev:implement`.

## Workflow shape

```
templates/workflows/adev-hygiene.mjs

parallel() over passes (from `adev hygiene passes --json`, passed as args)
  → barrier: dedup findings across passes (plain code, not an agent)
  → pipeline: per-finding adversarial verify
  → severity synthesis
```

Findings come back through a `schema`, so the object is validated at the tool-call layer and the model retries on mismatch — instead of the current prose-parsing of subagent reports.

## Requirements

- Default (no flag) behavior is byte-for-byte the serial path. No regression in the existing hygiene tests.
- The workflow returns findings; **the main loop writes the report and touches lifecycle state**. Nothing inside the workflow writes files.
- Graceful degradation: if `Workflow` is unavailable (non-Claude-Code provider mirror, or the tool errors), fall back to serial with a one-line notice, not a failure.
- Respect the workflow size guideline — log any pass or finding dropped by a cap rather than silently truncating.

title: Workflow-backed /adev:hygiene
description:
Make `/adev:hygiene` able to run its audit passes through a Claude Code dynamic workflow (`Workflow` tool) instead of walking them in a single context, as an opt-in path with the serial path unchanged as the default.

**This issue is deliberately not decomposed.** The task breakdown belongs to `/adev:plan`, from a reviewed Live Spec. Prior hand-authored breakdown (scaffolding, a passes verb, a flag, a measurement pass) was a guess made in chat and has been closed — do not treat it as the design.

## Why hygiene

Strongest candidate and safest. ~23 read-only audit passes described across ~1263 lines of SKILL prose, walked in one context that degrades as it fills, with findings parsed back out of subagent prose. No state writes during the fan-out, no gate inside the loop, no worktree-ownership question. What we learn transfers to `/adev:review-specs` and `/adev:research`.

## Constraints the spec must satisfy — verified by adev-plugin-wf-research-71qn

- **Provider mirroring is the hard one.** `scripts/sync-provider-skills.mjs` copies SKILL.md bodies **verbatim** to `providers/{codex,opencode}` (only the frontmatter description is transformed). Any workflow instruction in the canonical body reaches a Codex agent that has no `Workflow` tool. The only existing escape hatch is `PROVIDER_EXCLUDES`, which is whole-skill and all-or-nothing. The spec must choose: a runtime capability check in skill prose, or a new section-level transform in the sync script. This is a first-class design decision, not a footnote.
- **Gates cannot live inside the workflow** — workflow subagents have no `AskUserQuestion` and workflows launch background-only. Gates bracket the call.
- **Workflow subagents cannot dispatch subagents** (`Agent` absent). All fan-out is expressed in the script.
- **Subagents CAN write files.** "The main loop writes the report, nothing inside writes state" is a discipline needing its own guard, not a property of the substrate.
- **Skill extensions do load** inside workflow subagents, so the universal-skill-extensions contract holds on this path.
- **Default behavior unchanged.** No regression in existing hygiene tests; unavailable `Workflow` degrades to serial with a notice, not a failure.
- **Cost floor.** ~44k subagent tokens per agent measured on trivial probes. A 23-way fan-out is not free; measurement must count tokens, not just wall-clock.
- **No silent truncation.** Anything dropped by a size cap gets logged.

## Open questions for the spec

- Does the pass list get extracted into a CLI verb (useful on its own, independent of this feature) or passed some other way, given the script sandbox has no filesystem access?
- Do findings come back through a `schema`, replacing today's prose parsing?
- How does `resumeFromRunId` interact with execution-state and `/adev:recover` — which owns resume? Note the spike could not fully characterize cache semantics (see its caveat on mid-array edits).

## Lifecycle

Gated by the research spike (adev-plugin-wf-research-71qn). Then `/adev:brainstorm` → `/adev:specify` → `/adev:review-specs` → `/adev:plan`.

title: Research: dynamic workflows vs adev orchestration constraints
description:
Empirical spike: probe the Claude Code `Workflow` substrate directly and record observed behavior, rather than restating documentation.

**Status: two probe rounds run.** Round 1 = run `wf_36308d5c-9fe` (3 agents, 32s, 0 errors). Round 2 = resume of the same run with an edited script (4 agents, 8s, 0 errors). Provider portability answered by local inspection, no agents.

## Observed — script sandbox

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `Date.now()` / `new Date()` / `Math.random()` written literally | **Submission rejected before execution.** No agent runs. `try/catch` does not help. |
| Same clock reached indirectly via `globalThis[key]` with a computed key | **Throws at runtime**, same error text |
| `typeof require` / `process` / `fetch` / `globalThis.fs` | all `undefined` |
| `args` | round-trips exactly as passed |
| `budget.total` with no `+Nk` directive | `null`; `remaining()` → `Infinity`; `spent()` → live output-token count |

The determinism guard is **enforced at two layers** (static pre-screen plus runtime), not advisory. The script is genuinely data-only: no fs, no network, no Node API.

## Observed — what a workflow subagent has

cwd is the project root. Available: `Bash`, `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Skill`, `ToolSearch`, `StructuredOutput` (when `schema` is passed), plus the full MCP surface via `ToolSearch`.

Three absences matter more than the presences:

- **`AskUserQuestion` is absent.** Settles the gate question: a workflow subagent physically cannot prompt. Gates must bracket the workflow from the main loop.
- **`Agent` is absent.** A workflow subagent cannot dispatch further subagents. `/adev:implement`'s shape — orchestrator dispatches implementer, then spec reviewer, then code-quality reviewer per task — **cannot be reproduced inside a workflow agent**. Nested fan-out must be expressed in the script.
- **`Workflow` is absent.** No self-nesting from inside an agent.

**`Write`/`Edit` ARE available.** "Nothing inside the workflow writes files" is a discipline enforced by prompt wording, not by the substrate. Parallel agents can race on state writes and nothing stops them.

## Observed — adev integration reach

- `adev` binary reachable from a workflow subagent.
- `adev skill-ext load --skill hygiene` → exit 0, stdout `__NONE__`. **Skill extensions load normally inside workflow subagents**, so the universal-skill-extensions contract survives this path.

## Observed — resume semantics (round 2)

Edited the persisted script: left two agents byte-identical, changed a third's prompt, added a fourth. Resumed with `resumeFromRunId`.

- The two unchanged agents produced **no new `started` event in journal.jsonl** — 5 result lines total across both runs (3 + 2), so they genuinely did not re-execute. Their returned values were byte-identical (same 38-tool list, same verbatim notes).
- The changed agent got a **new cache key** (`v2:<hash>`) rather than reusing the old one, and returned the new value. The added agent ran live.
- Wall-clock dropped 32s → 8s.
- **Caveat:** the changed agent was last in the array, so this run cannot distinguish "longest unchanged prefix" semantics from per-agent content-addressing. The key being a content hash of (prompt, opts) suggests the latter, but it is one data point. Do not design around per-agent caching until a mid-array edit is tested.
- Token attribution is **not resolvable** from the journal — it records `{type, key, agentId, result}` with no per-agent usage. The run-level `subagent_tokens: 85,809` for 4 agents of which 2 replayed cannot be cleanly split. Wall-clock and journal-line count are the trustworthy replay evidence.

## Observed — provider portability (decisive)

`scripts/sync-provider-skills.mjs` copies each canonical `skills/<n>/SKILL.md` to `providers/{codex,opencode}/skills/` **verbatim**, transforming only the YAML `description` (appending "In Codex, invoke with $<name>"). Verified: `diff skills/hygiene/SKILL.md providers/codex/skills/hygiene/SKILL.md` is 4 lines, all frontmatter.

Consequences:

- Any workflow-backed instruction added to a canonical SKILL.md body **propagates verbatim** to Codex and OpenCode, where no `Workflow` tool exists. The mirrored agent would be told to call a tool it does not have.
- The only escape hatch today is `PROVIDER_EXCLUDES` in that script, which is **whole-skill, all-or-nothing**. There is no section-level transform. Excluding `/adev:hygiene` from Codex entirely is not acceptable.
- Therefore a workflow-backed skill step must either (a) be gated behind a capability check the skill prose performs at runtime, or (b) require a new body-level transform in the sync script. This is a design constraint on the hygiene feature, not an afterthought.

## Observed — failure semantics

- `parallel()` thunk that throws → `null` in that slot; siblings unaffected; call does not reject.
- `pipeline()` stage that rejects → that item becomes `null`, skips remaining stages; other items proceed.
- Failures surface in a `<failures>` block on the completion notification, not silently swallowed.
- An agent with no `schema` returns a plain `string`.

## Observed — cost

Round 1: three trivial probe agents cost ~133k subagent tokens (~44k each). Fan-out is not cheap — each agent carries a full context. Any adev fan-out must beat that floor, and the hygiene measurement must count tokens, not just wall-clock.

## Risk surface

Workflow subagents run headless with no ability to prompt, yet reach write-capable MCP connectors (message send, mail trash, calendar delete, CRM record delete, file share) through `ToolSearch`. Background + no-prompt + side-effect-capable is a combination adev must constrain explicitly in any workflow it ships.

## Still open

1. Mid-array script edit — prefix vs per-agent cache semantics (see caveat above).
2. Subagent death on a terminal API error; only thrown thunks were exercised, not agent death.
3. Concurrency cap (min(16, CPUs−2)) — per-workflow or shared across chained workflows. Deliberately not probed: needs 17+ agents, ~750k tokens, not justified for the answer's value.

## Deliverable

Fold the above into `.context-index/research/dynamic-workflows-evaluation.md` with a recommendation: adopt (scoped), adopt (broad), or decline.

title: Scaffold .claude/workflows/ from templates during /adev:init
description:
Add a `templates/workflows/` directory and scaffold it into the project's `.claude/workflows/` so adev-authored workflow scripts have a home that satisfies the cli-driver-surface charter.

## Why

A `Workflow` script is executable JS. CLAUDE.md forbids executable logic inside SKILL.md, and the cli-driver-surface charter forbids inline-Node in skills. Therefore a workflow must be a **named file on disk** that a skill invokes by name — `Workflow({name: 'adev-hygiene', args})` — exactly as skills today name an `adev <verb>`.

## Scope

- `templates/workflows/` with at least one real script (see the hygiene prototype issue).
- `/adev:init` scaffolds `.claude/workflows/` when the layer is opted into; skipping it must leave every skill working on its serial path.
- Manifest entry so the layer is declared and `/adev:hygiene` / `/adev:status` can see it.
- The `.githooks/pre-commit-no-inline-node` policy must NOT flag these files (they are not `skills/**/SKILL.md`) — add a regression test asserting that.
- Document the seam in `docs/` (likely `concepts.md` + `extensions.md`).

## Non-goals

Shipping workflows via `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — plugin format has no workflow slot today. Scaffolding from `templates/` is the path.

title: merge-guard.sh — workspace-safe manifest lookup
gate doctor verifies a different gate set than the one that actually executes
description: Found 2026-08-13 while running /adev:validate on issue-554. adev gate doctor (issue-552) reads .context-index/governance/gates.yaml DIRECTLY with no domain merge, while every actual consumer (/adev:validate Check 1, /adev:implement Step 2-post) resolves gates through 'adev domain load-gates' -> mergeGates(), which merges the domain starter and drops entries failing validateGate. The two sources disagree in BOTH directions, so the doctor can report a clean bill of health on a gate set that never runs. VERIFIED ON THIS REPO, zero overlap between verified and executed: (a) 'adev gate doctor' reports on exactly one gate -- id 'test', command "npm test" -- and exits 0 with '0 error(s), 1 warning(s)'. (b) 'adev domain load-gates --module unified-gates' on the same repo returns a merged list of TWO ENTIRELY DIFFERENT gates -- 'quality-gate' [npm,test] fast and 'integration-test' [npm,run,--if-present,test:integration] integration, both from the software domain default -- plus the warning INVALID_GATE: Gate 'test' command must be an argv list (array), not a string -- skipped. So the doctor validates a gate the executor discards, and is blind to both gates the executor runs. FAILURE MODE, both directions unsafe: (1) FALSE CLEAN -- a string-form gate is analysed and passed by the doctor while merge-gates.mjs:34-37 silently skips it, so a project whose only gate is string-form runs NOTHING while the doctor says it is fine; here the consequence is masked only because the software domain default happens to also run npm test. (2) BLIND SPOT -- domain-starter and extension-overlay gates are never examined by the doctor at all, which after issue-554 ships is where the default integration tier LIVES; the doctor would never diagnose the very defaults that PR shipped. WHY P1: this is precisely the failure class issue-552 was built to eliminate (the audit's highest-leverage finding was 'tests/gates declared but never executed, and adev never noticed'). A verifier reading a different source than the executor reproduces that bug inside the tool meant to detect it. SCOPE NOTE: the string-form half is pre-existing (merge-gates.mjs already rejects strings on main) and issue-554/PR #253 fixes templates/gates-template.yaml going forward -- header and every commented example now teach argv form. What remains unaddressed: every ALREADY-SCAFFOLDED project still carries a string-form gates.yaml plus a header comment teaching the rejected form (this repo included -- .context-index/governance/gates.yaml:10 still reads 'command: Shell command to execute'), and there is no migration or detection path. title: adev issues claim <id>: atomic check-and-set ownership, enforced in implement/debug preflight
description:
Root cause established 2026-08-12 after two agents independently fixed the same p0 vulnerability an hour apart (PR #214 and duplicate PR #215, both for issue-582), and after a whole concurrent epic (epic-102, issues 568-581, PRs #210-#214) stayed invisible to a study pursuing the same goal. The issue board resolves storage via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs) and IS shared across worktrees. Execution state does NOT: lib/execution-state.mjs reads <projectRoot>/.context-index/.execution-state.json, which is worktree-local. Measured live: /adev:work Step 1 reported status "idle" in this worktree while four epic-102 issues were in_progress and five PRs were open. Second, behavioural half: the board DID carry the signal (issue-582 was already in_progress) and nothing re-reads an issue at the moment work begins, so stale local knowledge won over the shared record.

Model it on the existing requireGate() pattern — a code-enforced precondition that exits 2 and refuses to proceed — rather than inventing a new concept. Verb sets status=in_progress plus owner and claimed_at atomically, and refuses when already claimed by a live owner. /adev:implement and /adev:debug call it in preflight. This is the check that would have refused work on issue-582. BLOCKED BY the JsonAdapter concurrency bug: claim semantics on a shared board are unverified while "survives N concurrent appenders without corrupting tasks.json" is failing.

title: Domain Extensions
Extension-supplied governance target escapes .context-index/governance/ — arbitrary file write on install
description:
`lib/extensions/content-install.mjs::mergeGovernanceEntries` writes to a path built from an
extension-supplied string with no containment check. An extension manifest controls where the write
lands.

## The path

`lib/extensions/install.mjs:91`:

```js
const target = govEntry.target || 'review.yaml';
```

`target` comes straight from the extension's `adev-extension.yaml` under `provides.governance[].target`.
It reaches `mergeGovernanceEntries` (`content-install.mjs:163`), which does:

```js
const govDir = join(projectRoot, '.context-index', 'governance');
const targetPath = join(govDir, targetFile);   // no resolve(), no containment assertion
// ...
writeFileSync(targetPath, yaml);
```

## Reproduced 2026-08-14

```
mergeGovernanceEntries(root, '../../ESCAPED.yaml', [{id: 'x.y'}])
  -> returned without error
  -> wrote <root>/ESCAPED.yaml
```

The write escaped `.context-index/governance/` entirely. Enough `../` segments escape the project
root. The file content is attacker-shaped too: `serializeGovernanceYaml` emits the entries verbatim,
so the written bytes are substantially controlled by the manifest.

## Why this is an oversight, not a design choice

Two sibling functions in the same file do exactly the check this one omits:

- `installSamples` — `content-install.mjs:307-318`: `resolve()` then
  `startsWith(resolvedDir + '/')` on both source and destination.
- `installSkillExtensions` — `content-install.mjs:383-384`: same pattern.

Only the governance path skips it.

## Fix

Apply the same resolve + containment pattern before any write in `mergeGovernanceEntries`, with a
distinct error code (`PATH_TRAVERSAL`, matching the convention already used in this file). This is
separate from `UNKNOWN_GOVERNANCE_TARGET`, which covers a recognized-but-unmapped registry name
rather than directory escape.

Also constrain `target` to the known registry set rather than accepting an arbitrary filename —
`validate.yaml | review.yaml | gates.yaml | boundaries.yaml | diagnostics.yaml`.

## Blast radius

Narrow today: neither shipped extension (`data-engineering`, `process-automation`) uses
`provides.governance` — both go through `installDomainProfile`. The only consumer is
`extensions/example-validation-check`, the reference example. But that also means this path has never
been exercised against a real project, and it is the documented mechanism for third-party extensions
to contribute checks.

## Provenance

Found by the security reviewer during the full-tier architecture review of
`explicit-governance-registries.spec.md` (blocker `security-reviewer:path-traversal:8fd4d9bf`), then
reproduced. That spec depends on this code path, so the fix is a prerequisite for it — but the defect
is live now and independent of the spec's fate.

## Spec ownership (2026-08-15)

Now specced by `.context-index/specs/cross-cutting/extension-governance-merge-hardening.spec.md`
(rev 1, review-pending), split out of `explicit-governance-registries.spec.md` at its revision 4.

That parent spec's BLOCK→revise loop halted on REGRESSED — two consecutive revisions closed blockers
while introducing new ones — because it held two contracts at once. The extension-merge strand is now
its own spec with its own contract: "an extension's contribution writes exactly what it declared,
only where it is permitted, and never mutates what it did not create."

The split also surfaced two further defects in the same function cluster, both now in scope there:
destructive serialization (sibling keys and comments dropped) and no scalar-escaping contract — a
newline in any supplied string writes YAML at column 0, defeating the field allowlist and provenance
stamping in one move.

title: Extension governance entries have no field allowlist — forged provenance and silent check disable
description:
`lib/extensions/content-install.mjs::validateGovernanceEntry` (lines 101-119) validates only the `id`
field — that it exists, is a non-empty string, and is ≤128 chars. There is no allowlist of permitted
field names, so an extension's declared governance entries may carry arbitrary fields, which are then
written into the project's governance yaml.

Two distinct consequences share that root cause.

## 1. Forged provenance

New-id entries are copied verbatim (`content-install.mjs:~213`):

```js
byId.set(extEntry.id, { ...extEntry });
```

An extension can therefore declare `source: project` on its own entry. Under the model specced in
`explicit-governance-registries.spec.md`, that entry then:

- survives `adev extension uninstall`, which removes only entries whose `source` matches
  `extension:<name>`, and
- is excluded from the widened hygiene drift pass, which skips non-`project` sources.

It reads as project-authored permanently, with no audit trail back to the extension that wrote it.

## 2. Silent disable on id collision

The collision path fills gaps rather than rejecting (`content-install.mjs:~203-210`):

```js
// Project wins: only fill in fields not already set
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(extEntry)) {
  if (!(key in projectEntry)) projectEntry[key] = value;
}
```

`enabled` is absent from a project entry in the default-on case — which is the common case, since
`enabled: true` is the implied default and nobody writes it explicitly. So an extension declaring an
entry whose id collides with an existing check can inject `enabled: false` plus a plausible
`disabled_reason`, and the "project wins" comment is satisfied while the check is turned off.

That includes the security reviewer's own row in `review.yaml` once reviewers are materialized.

## Fix

1. **Stamp `source` from install context, never accept it from entry data.** Reject or strip an
   extension-supplied `source` in `validateGovernanceEntry`.
2. **Protect a closed key set from the fill-gap path** — `enabled`, `disabled_reason`, `severity`,
   `source`. Only project-authored edits may change these; a later extension install must never
   introduce them onto an existing entry.
3. **Add a field allowlist** per registry so unknown fields are rejected at install rather than
   silently persisted.

## Blast radius

Same as `adev-plugin-xg1f.1`: no shipped extension uses `provides.governance` today, so this is
latent. It becomes load-bearing the moment the mechanism is used, and
`explicit-governance-registries.spec.md` depends on it.

Point 2 is a defect against the *current* code as well as the specced model — the fill-gap loop can
already inject any field absent from a project entry, regardless of whether `enabled`/`source` exist
as concepts yet.

## Provenance

Found by the security reviewer during the full-tier architecture review of
`explicit-governance-registries.spec.md` (blocker `security-reviewer:authorization:c4456237`).

## Spec ownership (2026-08-15)

Now specced by `.context-index/specs/cross-cutting/extension-governance-merge-hardening.spec.md`
(rev 1, review-pending), split out of `explicit-governance-registries.spec.md` at its revision 4.

That parent spec's BLOCK→revise loop halted on REGRESSED — two consecutive revisions closed blockers
while introducing new ones — because it held two contracts at once. The extension-merge strand is now
its own spec with its own contract: "an extension's contribution writes exactly what it declared,
only where it is permitted, and never mutates what it did not create."

The split also surfaced two further defects in the same function cluster, both now in scope there:
destructive serialization (sibling keys and comments dropped) and no scalar-escaping contract — a
newline in any supplied string writes YAML at column 0, defeating the field allowlist and provenance
stamping in one move.
