title: Extension uninstall has no governance reversal — and no uninstall path at all
description:
Entries an extension writes into .context-index/governance/ are permanent. Nothing under lib/extensions/ removes them, and there is no uninstall path to add reversal to: `adev extension` exposes only `install` and `list`, and no `uninstallExtension` exists anywhere in lib/ (verified 2026-08-15).

Scoped out of extension-governance-merge-hardening.spec.md at its revision 2, on review advice. Specifying reversal there would have specified behavior against a mechanism that does not exist — the defect class that stalled the parent spec twice, and one that all three reviewers flagged independently.

Prerequisite: the `source` provenance field, which the hardening spec stamps at install (`extension:<name>`). Once entries are attributable, reversal is a filter. Until then it is not implementable at all.

Scope when picked up: an `adev extension uninstall --name <n>` verb, plus governance reversal that removes entries carrying that extension's `source` and leaves project-authored entries untouched.

title: First-party data-engineering extension breaks /adev:review-specs on install: inline prompt prose resolved as a file path
description:
Installing the first-party `data-engineering` domain extension does not degrade
review — it stops `/adev:review-specs` working entirely in that project.

## Cause

`extensions/data-engineering/domain/reviewers.yaml` writes `prompt:` as inline
prose:

    prompt: "Review data contracts for schema completeness, SLA definitions,
             freshness guarantees, and data quality thresholds. ..."

`resolveReviewerPath` (`lib/governance/review-config.mjs`) has no inline branch.
`prompt:` is ALWAYS a path, resolved under one of two schemes: `plugin:<skill>/<file>`
under the plugin `skills/` tree, or a relative path under the project's
`.context-index/`. Prose falls into the second branch and is resolved as a filename.

## Reproduction (run 2026-08-18)

Copy the extension's reviewers.yaml to a scratch project as
`.context-index/governance/review.yaml`, add a `materialized_at:` marker, then
`adev governance reviewers --json`:

    reviewers dispatched: 0
    errors: [
      {
        "code": "FILE_MISSING",
        "message": "Reviewer 'data-contract-reviewer': prompt file not found:
          <root>/.context-index/Review data contracts for schema completeness,
          SLA definitions, freshness guarantees, and data quality thresholds.
          Verify that all output schemas are fully defined with types,
          nullability, and primary keys. Check that failure modes have explicit
          recovery actions.."
      }
    ]

## Why it is fatal rather than degraded

`skills/review-specs/SKILL.md` Step 3: "Abort on any `errors` entry." One
malformed reviewer therefore takes down the whole panel, including the three
bundled reviewers that are perfectly well-formed. The project is left with a
review gate that cannot run at all.

## What this implies beyond the one file

The reviewers-as-domain-data path is UNPROVEN end to end. This is the only
first-party domain that declares reviewers, and it has never successfully
loaded — strong evidence that no one has installed a reviewer-bearing domain
extension and run a review afterwards.

## Fix directions (any subset)

1. Support inline prompt bodies — a distinct field (`prompt_text:`) or accepting
   prose when the value is clearly not a path. The extension author evidently
   expected this to work, which makes it a contract gap as much as a data bug.
2. Correct `extensions/data-engineering/domain/reviewers.yaml` to reference real
   prompt files shipped inside the domain directory.
3. Validate at install time: have `adev extension install` load the merged
   registry before committing, and refuse rather than leave the project with an
   aborting review gate. This would have caught it at authoring time.
4. Consider whether one malformed reviewer should be fatal to the entire panel,
   or whether it should be dropped with a loud warning while well-formed
   reviewers still dispatch.

Found while brainstorming adev-plugin-j7pq.5 (reviewer/domain retargeting).

title: Unbundle the software domain into an extension (extension-native domain layer)
description:
Making `software` a domain extension rather than a bundled special case would mean the
default domain travels the same code path as every third-party domain — so every install
exercises that path. That matters: `adev-plugin-xg1f.4` is a first-party extension whose
reviewers have NEVER successfully loaded, and it survived undetected precisely because
almost nothing exercises the extension path.

Scoped OUT of the reviewer-domain-fit initiative after two charter-review iterations found
six architectural blockers. Recorded here so the next attempt starts from the findings
rather than rediscovering them.

## Blockers, each verified against the code

1. **`extends` verifies the bundled DIRECTORY, not set membership.**
   `lib/domains/domain-config.mjs:222` does
   `existsSync(join(realPluginRoot, 'templates', 'domains', extendsValue))` and throws
   `EXTENDS_NOT_FOUND` if absent; `:106` reads inherited files from that same hardcoded
   path. Both `data-engineering` and `process-automation` declare `extends: software`.
   Keeping `software` in `BUNDLED_DOMAIN_NAMES` is therefore NOT sufficient — moving the
   directory breaks both extensions regardless. Fixing it means resolving one extension's
   content from inside another extension's load, which is the shape of `adev-plugin-zsmh.5`.

2. **`content-install.mjs:53` is the only name-squatting guard.** It refuses to install any
   extension whose name is in `BUNDLED_DOMAIN_NAMES`. Permitting `adev extension install
   software` removes the sole protection against a third party declaring `name: software`
   and writing over `.context-index/domains/software/`. Relaxing the `:76`
   `BUNDLED_OVERRIDE_BLOCKED` guard at the same time drops both layers.

3. **The install path cannot express a ROOT domain.** `installDomainProfile`
   (`content-install.mjs:88-90`) writes `domain.yaml` with `extends: ${parent}`
   unconditionally. `software` has no parent: `extends: undefined` fails
   `DOMAIN_NAME_PATTERN` in `resolveExtends`, and `extends: software` is self-referential.

4. **The upgrade trigger is unowned.** A pre-upgrade project has `domain: software` in
   manifest.yaml and no `software` entry in `installed_extensions`. Something must install
   the vendored extension into existing projects, and it is not obvious whether that is
   `adev install`, `adev upgrade`, `adev diagnose`, or first use.

5. **Template discovery and extension install operate on different roots that never meet.**
   `resolveTemplate` discovers extensions by scanning `<pluginRoot>/extensions/*/domain/`
   (`lib/template-resolution.mjs::discoverExtensionRoots`) and its signature carries NO repo
   root. `adev extension install` writes domain content to
   `<projectRoot>/.context-index/domains/<name>/`. See the sibling issue on this — it is a
   standalone defect, not only an unbundling blocker.

6. **It contradicts `template-resolution.spec.md` Behaviors 3 and 4** — fall-through to the
   bundled `software` default, and "when `domain` is null or undefined then resolution starts
   at the bundled default". Any fail-closed replacement must amend that spec, not just the code.

## Suggested sequencing

Blocker 5 is the natural first step and is independently valuable. Blockers 1 and 3 are the
real design work. Blocker 2 needs a provenance mechanism distinguishing the vendored default
from a third-party claim. Only then is the move itself a mechanical change.

title: resolveTemplate cannot see CLI-installed extensions: domain packages silently supply only half their content
description:
Template resolution and extension install use two different roots, and a CLI-installed
extension is invisible to template resolution.

- `resolveTemplate` discovers domains by scanning `<pluginRoot>/extensions/*/domain/`
  (`lib/template-resolution.mjs::discoverExtensionRoots`, ~:87). Its signature is
  `resolveTemplate(layer, kind, domain)` — it receives no project root at all.
- `adev extension install` writes domain content to
  `<projectRoot>/.context-index/domains/<name>/` and stamps `installed_extensions` in the
  project manifest.

So a domain extension installed by a user through the documented CLI path supplies its
`reviewers.yaml`, `gates.yaml` and other domain-config files — `loadDomainConfig` reads
`.context-index/domains/<domain>/` first (`lib/domains/domain-config.mjs:90`) — but its
`spec-template.md` / `charter-template.md` are never found, because `resolveTemplate` only
looks plugin-side. The extension appears to install successfully and silently supplies half
of what it declares.

First-party extensions vendored under `<pluginRoot>/extensions/` are unaffected, which is
why this has not been noticed: `data-engineering` and `process-automation` both live there.
It bites the moment anyone installs a third-party domain extension that ships templates.

## Why it matters beyond the immediate bug

The extensions charter's whole premise is that a domain package supplies templates,
governance and samples as one unit. Half of that unit not resolving makes the contract
untrue for the primary install path.

## Fix directions

1. Give `resolveTemplate` a project root and search `.context-index/domains/<domain>/`
   before the plugin-side extension roots — mirroring `loadDomainConfig`'s
   project-then-bundled precedence, so both halves of a domain package resolve the same way.
2. Or have install copy templates into a location `resolveTemplate` already scans, though
   writing into `<pluginRoot>` from a project-scoped command is worse.
3. Either way, add a test that installs a domain extension shipping a `spec-template.md`
   into a scratch project and asserts `/adev:specify` writes from it.

Found during the adev-plugin-j7pq.5 charter review (2026-08-18).

title: opencode adapter shells out to execSync("cp -r") with an interpolated path instead of cpSync
description:
providers/opencode/adapter.mjs:76-80 copies the plugin into the cache by shelling
out, one child process per top-level entry:

  execSync(`cp -r "${src}" "${dest}"`);
  execSync(`cp "${src}" "${dest}"`);

Two problems.

1. CONSTITUTION. Principle 1 prefers Node built-ins over shelling out, and
   providers/cursor/adapter.mjs:162 carries a comment naming this exact file as
   the holdout: 'The OpenCode adapter still uses execSync for historical reasons;
   the new CursorAdapter does not need that legacy.' The other three copying
   adapters use cpSync.

2. INJECTION SURFACE. src and dest are interpolated into a shell string. Both
   derive from PLUGIN_ROOT (resolved from import.meta.url) and the resolved cache
   directory, so neither is user-supplied today and the quoting holds for ordinary
   paths. It breaks on a path containing a double quote, and any future change
   that lets a caller influence the cache location turns it into command
   injection. Not currently exploitable; cheap to remove as a class.

FIX
Replace both calls with cpSync(src, dest, { recursive: item.isDirectory() }), or
a single cpSync of the root using installCopyFilter(PLUGIN_ROOT) from
lib/provider/ship-filter.mjs the way claude-code and cursor now do. The second is
probably better — the readdir loop exists only to apply the copy filter per entry,
and ship-filter already expresses that.

Noticed while fixing adev-plugin-1gts, which changed this file's filter (the
denylist became shouldCopyTopLevel) but deliberately left the execSync calls alone
to keep that change scoped to what gets copied rather than how.

Verify tests/provider/ and any opencode install tests after changing it.

adev:issues skill prose drops body field silently on json backend create()
description:
The /adev:issues skill's create-issue prose accepts a body/description argument from the user, but the json backend's IssueManagerInterface.create() silently drops any field except the canonical schema (id, title, status, priority, type, dependencies, notes, next_action, created, updated). The field is named "notes" in the adapter, not "description".

Repro (observed in this session while filing issue-483):
1. Invoke /adev:issues create with a multi-paragraph body argument.
2. Skill calls manager.create({ title, description, type, priority }).
3. The created issue persists with notes="" — the description body is dropped without warning.
4. A follow-up manager.update(id, { notes }) is required to attach the body.

Impact:
- User-supplied issue bodies (repro steps, acceptance criteria, links) are silently lost on first create.
- Agent must do a defensive create-then-update dance to attach any body, or the skill prose must teach the agent to use notes (not description).
- No error is surfaced — the silent drop is the worst failure mode for a write API.

Two valid fixes (orthogonal — both prose-level, no behavioral change to the helper):
A) Update skills/issues/SKILL.md to consistently use "notes" instead of "description"/"body" when describing the create arguments, and add an explicit note that the body field is named "notes".
B) Update the json adapter's create() to accept and normalize a "description" alias to "notes" (still write to the same column).

Recommend option A (prose-only, fewer surfaces to keep in sync).

Affected files (audit needed):
- skills/issues/SKILL.md — "Create Issue" section and argument descriptions
- Any other SKILL.md that invokes /adev:issues create (notably /adev:plan and /adev:implement which auto-create issues)
- lib/issues/json-adapter.mjs (or wherever create() lives) — confirm the dropped-field behavior

Discovered while filing issue-483 in the same /adev:debug session (2026-05-14). See also: issue-483 is the original build-state path-drift bug that exposed this one.

Acceptance criteria:
- skills/issues/SKILL.md create-issue arguments documented using the field name the adapter actually stores
- Cross-skill audit: every place that calls manager.create() uses the correct field name
- Optional: adapter logs a warning when an unknown field is passed to create() (defense-in-depth against the same class of bug)
close_reason: Fixed in 684a677b. Confirmed by direct probe that validateIssue dropped body/description silently. Fixed at the SHARED boundary in lib/issues/interface.mjs rather than one adapter, because the beads adapter calls it too and was losing bodies identically. body/description now resolve as aliases of notes, which is what they already are everywhere (beads writes notes as --description). The conflict rule is deliberately ASYMMETRIC: two aliases disagreeing with no notes throws, but a non-empty canonical notes beside a disagreeing alias wins silently — because a symmetric throw BROKE adev issues migrate, since update() bypasses validateIssue and pre-fix boards carry stray keys that projectIssueForCreate replays through create(). That abort was reproduced and fixed both ways. 21 new tests asserting through a FRESH adapter; 540 board tests pass. Adjacent gap filed as issue-80m9s2: validateEpic has no notes field at all.

title: Implement Stage-2 review loop is unbounded ("Repeat until approved") while every sibling loop caps at 3
description:
skills/implement/SKILL.md:577 — "Critical or Important issues: The implementer fixes them. The reviewer reviews again. Repeat until approved."

No attempt cap, no convergence check, no escalation. Sibling loops (plan reviewer, implement Stage 1, implement visual) all cap at 3. The MAST failure taxonomy (Berkeley, NeurIPS 2025) catalogues this exact class as "step repetition without progress" and finds most agent failures are organizational rather than model-capability.

Fix: cap the loop and route the cap-trip through lib/loop-convergence.mjs verdicts (NO_PROGRESS / REGRESSED / BUDGET_EXHAUSTED) rather than a bare retry counter. The research also notes retry budgets are hardcoded prose strings ("maximum 3") in three places and should be config-backed per loop, like build.max_review_retries already is.

From .context-index/research/harness-simplification-study.md Part 3, "Loop inventory".

Source: 2026-08-14 research-vs-board audit. Claim re-verified against the codebase at that date, not taken from the research artifact alone.
close_reason: Fixed in 11b179d7. skills/implement/SKILL.md Step 2g no longer says "Repeat until approved": capped at 3 cycles, matching the sibling Stage 1 and visual loops, with each cycle routed through lib/loop-convergence.mjs rather than a bare counter. That required a new rule that finding ids be stable and reused across cycles — without stable ids NO_PROGRESS and REGRESSED are undecidable, which is presumably why the loop was unbounded. Terminal outcomes reuse build vocabulary (LOOP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED / LOOP_NO_PROGRESS / LOOP_REGRESSED) so one grep finds both loops. Escalation states plainly that Stage 2 has NOT passed. Budget hardcoded at 3 because no implement.max_review_retries knob exists; a config-backed budget mirroring build.max_review_retries is named as a follow-up. 11/11, no inline-Node introduced.

title: Install, Providers & Portability
br ignores adev's shared-worktree issue storage — worktrees read a stale board silently
description:
`CLAUDE.md` states: "Issue storage is shared across git worktrees — adapters resolve the main repo
root via `resolveStorageRoot()` in `lib/issues/resolve-root.mjs`, overridable with `tasks.db_path`
in manifest."

That guarantee holds for adev's own adapters. It does not hold for `br`, the external beads_rust
CLI that `tasks.backend: beads` delegates to. `br` discovers `.beads/*.db` relative to the current
working directory and knows nothing about `resolveStorageRoot()`.

## Observed behavior

Inside an adev-managed worktree (`.adev/worktrees/<slug>`), the worktree has a checked-out
`.beads/issues.jsonl` from its base branch but no `beads.db`. Two distinct failures follow:

1. **Read-only commands silently return stale data.** Reading `.beads/issues.jsonl` directly in a
   worktree returns the base branch's board, not the live one. Encountered live 2026-08-14: a
   just-closed issue still read as `open`, and a verification sweep was run against a
   three-commits-old board before the discrepancy was noticed.

2. **`br` itself refuses to open storage.** From a worktree:

   ```
   warning: could not prove that no sync merge is pending (Sync conflict: Pending sync-merge
   state is unknown because database '<worktree>/.beads/beads.db' is missing). Read-only command
   will proceed with automatic sync disabled; do not mutate until `br doctor` succeeds.
   Error: Sync conflict: Refusing storage open because pending sync-merge state could not be
   inspected under database-family authority
   ```

   And from any directory that is not a beads root at all (e.g. a scratchpad):

   ```
   Error: Beads not initialized: run 'br init' first
   ```

The second failure is loud and safe. The first is silent and is the dangerous one — an agent
working in a worktree reads a plausible-looking board and acts on it.

## Why it matters

Worktrees are the framework's own recommended isolation mechanism (`adev worktree add`, used by
`/adev:parallel` and by any agent avoiding conflicts with a concurrent session). The board is the
one piece of state explicitly promised to be shared across them, and it is the piece that silently
is not.

## Candidate fixes

- Teach the beads adapter to invoke `br` with an explicit `--db <mainRoot>/.beads/beads.db`
  (the flag exists) rather than relying on cwd discovery.
- Or run `br` with cwd pinned to `resolveStorageRoot()` output.
- Or, at minimum, make the adapter fail loudly when the resolved storage root and `br`'s discovered
  root disagree, so stale reads become errors rather than plausible answers.

Whichever route, `.beads/` should probably not be a tracked path that materializes a stale copy
into every worktree checkout.

## Scope note

Filed under Install, Providers & Portability as the closest available home; this is an
environment/tooling-integration defect rather than an issue-board feature. Blast radius is limited
to agents and humans operating inside worktrees.

title: Project-side files silently lag a plugin upgrade: generalize migrate-gate-commands into a version-keyed migration registry
description:
A plugin upgrade replaces skills/hooks/lib/templates atomically (new versioned dir under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/agentic-development/adev/<version>/, with installed_plugins.json pinning installPath). Project-side files under .context-index/ NEVER update: scaffoldContextKit() copies each template with `if (!existsSync(destPath))`, and governance registries additionally carry a write-once materialized_at marker. Documented at docs/governance.md:118.

Consequence: a project can run stale governance indefinitely with no signal. Observed twice.

CASE 1 (already fixed, and the precedent for this issue). Shell-string gate commands. lib/migrate-gate-commands.mjs exists solely because of this class of bug and states it: "Nothing migrated those files... the file that needs fixing is precisely the file the installer refuses to touch. The result is a project whose quality gates silently evaluate zero gates, which reads identically to a project that passed them."

CASE 2 (live in THIS repo, found 2026-08-17). PR #279 (merge d1878dcd, 2026-08-16), commit 631a12ad, changed templates/domains/software/reviewers.yaml context_pack from `base` to architecture / security / consistency. .context-index/governance/review.yaml was materialized 2026-08-15T19:35:30.978Z — one day earlier — so it still pins all three reviewers to `base`. Measured effect: rendering pack `base` for a real target yields exactly two fenced sections (constitution.md, platform-context.yaml), 8854 bytes. No charter, no sibling specs, no ADRs, no cross-cutting specs. Every /adev:review-specs run in this repo today is context-starved and its verdict is weaker than it looks.

NOTHING DETECTS CASE 2:
- `adev governance materialize --registry review --dry-run` => "already explicit / newly written: (none) / (no change)". It appends MISSING entries; entries on disk keep their bytes. All three entries already exist, so it is a no-op.
- `adev governance drift --registry review` reports only 3 [info] hygiene/non-project-execution-field notes about `prompt`. It does not mention context_pack, which is not in EXECUTION_FIELDS (command/runner/prompt/pattern).
- hygiene Pass 19 DELIBERATELY defers changed-since detection: lib/hygiene/registry-drift.mjs:44-49 — "A changed-since diff ... needs an install ledger, and no ledger exists."
- docs/governance.md:120-141 "Adopting an upgrade" covers only "an entry the upgraded starter declares that your file does NOT" — added entries, never a changed field value on an entry you already have.

ALSO OBSERVED: this repo manifest.yaml records adev_version: "0.27.9-next" while the installed plugin is 0.28.0-next.1 — `adev upgrade` was never run after the update. And computeUpgradeDelta (cli/index.mjs:251) was never maintained past 0.13.0: its only branches are `fMin < 13`, so for 0.27 -> 0.28 it returns an EMPTY delta and upgrade reports "nothing new" when plenty changed.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (build on it, do not reinvent):
- manifest.yaml `adev_version` written by stampVersion() (cli/index.mjs:756) — a minimal ledger.
- detectProjectState() reads it; computeUpgradeDelta(fromVersion) is already version-keyed.
- `adev upgrade` (cli/index.mjs:1200) is the entry point and already calls one concrete migrator, migrateLegacyGateCommands(), which already has the right safe/UNSAFE instinct (refuses shell strings with metacharacters rather than guessing).

FOUR GAPS:
1. Migrations are hardcoded, not registered — one call site; a second migration means editing cmdUpgrade.
2. computeUpgradeDelta is dead weight past 0.13.0 (see above).
3. No record of WHICH migrations ran. adev_version records the target, not what was applied, so a partial/failed run is untracked and unresumable.
4. No dry-run for migrations, unlike `governance materialize --dry-run`.

PROPOSED DESIGN. Key insight: the deferral in registry-drift.mjs applies to a GENERIC changed-since diff. A DECLARATIVE version-keyed migration needs no diff — you assert the transformation at the version where it shipped, which is exactly what migrate-gate-commands does for 0.25.0. Generalize that; do not build a differ.

  lib/migrations/index.mjs   — ordered registry
  lib/migrations/<id>.mjs    — one module per migration

Each migration declares:
  id             stable, e.g. 0.28.0-review-context-packs
  introducedIn   version where the change shipped
  detect(root)   pure read -> { applies, findings[] }, never writes
  apply(root,{dryRun}) -> { changed[], skipped[], unsafe[] }
  risk           auto | confirm | manual

Three risk tiers generalize the migrator existing safe/UNSAFE split:
  auto    — mechanical and reversible (add a missing optional field)
  confirm — changes runtime behavior; show a diff and prompt (the context_pack case)
  manual  — cannot be done safely; report with instructions (shell-metachar gate commands)

Promote the stamp to a real ledger:
  project:
    adev_version: "0.28.0-next.1"
    adev_migrations:
      - { id: 0.25.0-gate-commands-argv,   applied_at: ..., outcome: applied }
      - { id: 0.28.0-review-context-packs, applied_at: ..., outcome: confirmed }
This buys idempotency, resumability and audit — and it IS the ledger registry-drift.mjs says does not exist, so it unblocks Pass 19 changed-since diff as a FOLLOW-ON rather than a prerequisite.

Surface: `adev upgrade` runs auto, prompts confirm, reports manual; `adev upgrade --dry-run` for parity with materialize; `adev migrate list|run <id>` for targeted use; hygiene Pass 19 reads the ledger to report unapplied migrations.

CRITICAL BOUNDARY: migrations must be permitted to edit materialized_at-marked files — that is the entire point. The rule that keeps it safe: a migration MAY change field values on EXISTING entries, but MUST NOT add or remove entries (that stays materialize job), and MUST preserve `source:` provenance. This also cleanly resolves the docs "do not hand-copy rows out of the templates" warning, which is about whole rows, not field values.

APPROVAL: touches the install/upgrade contract, which CLAUDE.md lists under Requires Human Approval. Route via /adev:brainstorm then /adev:specify rather than straight to code.

RELATED: adev-plugin-j7pq.4 (closed — its remaining adoption lag is CASE 2 above), adev-plugin-8ekd.3 (declared-vs-actual gap), adev-plugin-j7pq.5 (reviewer prompts promise input they do not receive).

title: Extension discovery: no way to find extensions, only to install a known source
description:
Extensions can only be installed by SOURCE today — `adev extension install <path|npm-package|git-url>`.
There is no way to find out what exists. The extensions charter lists "Extension
marketplace or discovery service" as explicitly out of scope, and the catalog is
currently one bundled domain (`software`) plus three first-party extensions
(`data-engineering`, `process-automation`, `example-validation-check`).

Deferred deliberately during the adev-plugin-j7pq.5 brainstorm (2026-08-18): with
no catalog worth browsing yet, discovery would be infrastructure ahead of content.
Revisit once there are extensions a user would plausibly search for.

## Options considered, with trade-offs

1. **npm naming convention + `adev extension search <term>`** — adopt `adev-domain-*` /
   `adev-extension-*` and query the public npm registry. No service to host, npm is
   already the package manager so no new dependency, publishing open to anyone.
   Discovery is real but unmoderated.
2. **Curated index file in-repo** — a registry YAML in the plugin listing known-good
   extensions; `adev extension list --available` reads it. Zero infrastructure,
   fully offline, but the catalog only grows when adev ships a release.
3. **Git-based index repo** — `agentic-development/adev-registry` holding the index,
   fetched by the CLI. Decoupled from adev releases and community-PR-able, but adds
   a network dependency and a second repo to maintain.

## Precondition worth respecting

`adev-plugin-xg1f.4` found that the only first-party domain declaring reviewers has
never successfully loaded — the reviewers-as-domain-data path is unproven end to end.
Discovery should not ship before installing a reviewer-bearing extension demonstrably
works, or it will make a broken path easier to reach.

title: adev extension install has no inverse: extension remove is unimplemented
description:
`adev extension install` has no inverse. The extensions charter lists `extension remove`
as out of scope for 1.0, with the stated workaround being "manual file removal via git".

That workaround is weak for anything that merges into `.context-index/`: an extension
contributes governance config (review/validate/gates), domain profiles, and samples,
and after install those files are indistinguishable from project-authored content
without consulting the `installed_extensions` manifest stamp. A user who installs the
wrong domain has no supported way back.

Interacts with the materialized-registry model: since `explicit-governance-registries`
landed, a project's `review.yaml` IS the complete effective set. Removing an extension
therefore cannot just delete files — it has to decide what happens to registry entries
the extension contributed and the project may have since edited.

## Scope questions to settle first

- Does remove revert registry entries, disable them (`enabled: false`), or leave them
  and only remove unreferenced files?
- How are user edits to extension-contributed files detected and preserved?
- Is `installed_extensions` sufficient provenance to know what an extension added, or
  does install need to record a file manifest?

Deferred during the adev-plugin-j7pq.5 brainstorm (2026-08-18).

title: Extensions cannot depend on other extensions: no layering or ordering contract
description:
Each extension is self-contained today — the extensions charter lists "Extension
dependencies on other extensions" as out of scope, and there is no `requires` field
for extension-to-extension relationships (`requires.adev` covers only the adev version).

This becomes limiting as soon as extensions layer. A `web-service` domain and a
`fintech-compliance` overlay that extends it currently have to either duplicate content
or rely on the user installing both in the right order, with nothing detecting or
enforcing that.

## Questions to settle

- Resolution: does adev resolve and install transitively, or only verify the dependency
  is already present and refuse otherwise?
- Ordering: domain profiles and governance registries merge, so install order can change
  the result — a dependency graph implies a deterministic merge order.
- Conflicts: two extensions depending on incompatible versions of a third.
- Interaction with `adev-plugin-zsmh` (extension remove): removing a depended-upon
  extension must not silently break its dependents.

Deferred during the adev-plugin-j7pq.5 brainstorm (2026-08-18). Lower priority than
remove and discovery — no current extension needs it.

title: Installed extensions never check for updates: no drift signal against their source
description:
Extensions are installed at a point in time and never checked again. The extensions
charter lists "Automatic updates or version polling" as out of scope. `installed_extensions`
in manifest.yaml records name, version and install date, so adev knows what version a
project holds but never compares it to what the source now offers.

Consequence: an extension shipping a corrected reviewer, gate or template reaches
existing projects only if someone re-runs `adev extension install` by hand, with no
signal that doing so would change anything. This is the extension-scoped twin of the
problem hygiene Pass 19 solves for bundled/domain registry drift.

## Design notes

- Prefer the Pass 19 shape over background polling: DETECT drift and report it, with an
  explicit user-initiated apply path. Silent auto-update of governance content would
  undermine the materialized-registry guarantee that the file a project holds is the
  complete effective set.
- Needs a version-comparison story per source type: npm (registry metadata), git (ref or
  tag), local path (mtime/content hash — or simply unsupported).
- Overlaps `adev-plugin-zsmh.2` (project-side files silently lag a plugin upgrade) — same
  class of problem, different content owner. Consider whether one version-keyed migration
  registry should cover both.

Deferred during the adev-plugin-j7pq.5 brainstorm (2026-08-18).

title: /adev:validate emits no lifecycle events (no gate, no started, no completed)
description:
Surfaced by lifecycle-event audit on 2026-05-17 (LIFE-1, LIFE-3). skills/validate/SKILL.md Step 0a uses inline-Node imports of currentState/requireGate/resolveGateMode/reportStep instead of `adev gate require --skill validate --spec

` and `adev report --type step --status started`. Worse, no completion event is emitted — the section structure jumps from Check 11 to Overall Status to After Validation without ever calling `adev report --type step --step validate --status completed`. Consequence: after /adev:validate runs, the lifecycle log shows lifecycle_step:validate started with no terminal event. Any future skill that gates on validate completion would block permanently. Same shape of bug as issue-508 but for a different skill. Fix: 1. Replace the Step 0a inline-Node block with `adev gate require --skill validate --spec

` + `adev report --type step --step validate --status started`. 2. Add a final emission step that calls `adev report --type step --step validate --status completed --verdict ` where aggregate is PASS / PASS_WITH_NOTES / FAIL based on the consolidated check results. Acceptance: - /adev:validate runs end-to-end without inline-Node in its critical-path gate logic. - Lifecycle log after a validate run contains both lifecycle_step:validate started AND step_completed:validate with a verdict. - Manual verification: a fictional downstream skill calling `adev gate require --skill ` after validate does not block.; Closed: PR #132 merged; validate skill emits canonical lifecycle events
